title.zh: 卷19中 景穆十二王中
title.raw: 卷19中 景穆十二王中 Volume 19b: Emperor Jingmu Twelve Princes 2

sentences.zh: 任城王雲，年五歲，恭宗崩，號哭不絕聲。

translations.literal: Yun, Prince of Rencheng, was five years old when Gongzong died, and he wailed without cease.
translations.idiomatic: Yun, Prince of Rencheng, was only five when Gongzong died, yet he wailed without stopping.

sentences.zh: 世祖聞之而呼，抱之泣曰：「汝何知而有成人之意也！」

translations.literal: Shizu heard of this, summoned him, embraced him, and wept, saying, "What do you know, to have the mind of a grown man?"
translations.idiomatic: Shizu heard and called for him, took him in his arms, and wept. "How is it that you already have a grown man's heart?"

sentences.zh: 和平五年封，拜使持節、侍中、征東大將軍、和龍鎮都大將。

translations.literal: In Heping year 5 he was enfeoffed and appointed Bearer of the Staff, Palace Attendant, Grand General Who Conquers the East, and grand commander of Helong Garrison.
translations.idiomatic: In Heping year 5 he received his fief and was made Bearer of the Staff, Palace Attendant, Grand General Who Conquers the East, and commander of Helong Garrison.

sentences.zh: 顯祖時，拜都督中外諸軍事、中都坐大官，聽理民訟，甚收時譽。

translations.literal: Under Xianzu he was appointed commander of all military affairs within and beyond the court and seated high minister of the central capital; he heard civil lawsuits and won great praise in his time.
translations.idiomatic: Under Xianzu he commanded the armies inside and outside the court, served as seated high minister of the central capital, heard civil suits, and won wide renown.

sentences.zh: 延興中，顯祖集羣僚，欲禪位於京兆王子推。

translations.literal: During Yanxing, Xianzu assembled the officials and wished to abdicate to Zitui, Prince of Jingzhao.
translations.idiomatic: During the Yanxing era, Xianzu gathered his ministers, intending to abdicate to Zitui, Prince of Jingzhao.

sentences.zh: 王公卿士，莫敢先言。

translations.literal: None among the princes, dukes, ministers, and officers dared speak first.
translations.idiomatic: Among the princes, dukes, ministers, and officers, no one dared speak first.

sentences.zh: 雲進曰：「陛下方隆太平，臨覆四海，豈得上違宗廟，下棄兆民。

translations.literal: Yun stepped forward and said, "Your Majesty is now exalting great peace and overseeing all within the four seas; how could you above violate the ancestral temples and below abandon the myriad people?
translations.idiomatic: Yun stepped forward. "Your Majesty is raising an age of peace and shelters all within the four seas. How could you turn away from the ancestral temples above and cast off the people below?

sentences.zh: 父子相傳，其來久矣，皇魏之興，未之有革。

translations.literal: The succession from father to son has come down for a long time; since the rise of imperial Wei, it has not been changed.
translations.idiomatic: Father-to-son succession has long been the rule; since imperial Wei arose, it has never been altered.

sentences.zh: 皇儲正統，聖德夙章。

translations.literal: The crown prince is the orthodox heir, and his sagely virtue was manifest early.
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince is the rightful heir, and his virtue has shone since early youth.

sentences.zh: 陛下必欲割捐塵務，頤神清曠者，冢副之寄，宜紹寶曆，若欲捨儲，輕移宸極，恐非先聖之意，駭動人情。

translations.literal: If Your Majesty truly wishes to cut away worldly affairs and nourish the spirit in clear freedom, the charge of the heir should continue the precious calendar; if you mean to set aside the heir and lightly shift the imperial pivot, I fear it is not the intention of the former sages and will alarm human feeling.
translations.idiomatic: If Your Majesty truly wishes to lay aside worldly affairs and nourish your spirit in quiet freedom, the throne should pass to the heir. If you set the heir aside and lightly move the imperial pivot, I fear this defies the former sages and will shock the hearts of men.

sentences.zh: 又，天下是祖宗之天下，而陛下輒改神器，上乖七廟七靈，下長姦亂之道，此是禍福所由，願深思慎之。」

translations.literal: Moreover, the realm belongs to the ancestors, yet Your Majesty would suddenly change the sacred vessel, above going against the seven temples and seven spirits and below lengthening the road of treachery and disorder. This is where fortune and disaster begin; I beg you to think deeply and act carefully."
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, the realm belongs to the ancestors. If Your Majesty suddenly changes the sacred vessel, you will offend the ancestral spirits above and open the way to treachery and disorder below. Fortune and disaster begin here; please think deeply and proceed with care."

sentences.zh: 太尉源賀又進曰：「陛下今欲外選諸王而禪位于皇叔者，臣恐春秋蒸嘗，昭穆有亂，脫萬世之後，必有逆饗之譏，深願思任城之言。」

translations.literal: Grand Marshal Yuan He also stepped forward and said, "If Your Majesty now wishes to choose externally among the princes and abdicate to an imperial uncle, I fear that in spring and autumn sacrifices the order of Zhao and Mu will be confused, and after ten thousand generations there will surely be criticism of improper offerings. I earnestly hope you will consider Rencheng's words."
translations.idiomatic: Grand Marshal Yuan He also spoke. "If Your Majesty chooses from among the princes and abdicates to an imperial uncle, I fear the order of the ancestral rites will be thrown into confusion, and later ages will condemn the offerings as improper. I beg you to weigh Rencheng's words."

sentences.zh: 東陽公元丕等進曰：「皇太子雖聖德夙彰，然實沖幼。

translations.literal: Duke Yuan Pi of Dongyang and the others advanced and said, "Though the crown prince's sagely virtue has long been evident, he is in truth still young.
translations.idiomatic: Duke Yuan Pi of Dongyang and the others added, "Although the crown prince's virtue is already clear, he is still very young.

sentences.zh: 陛下富於春秋，始覽機政，普天景仰，率土傒心，欲隆獨善，不以萬物為意，其若宗廟何，其若億兆何！」

translations.literal: Your Majesty is rich in years and has only begun to oversee the mechanisms of government; all under heaven look up to you, and the whole land waits with longing. If you wish to exalt solitary goodness and give no thought to the myriad things, what of the ancestral temples? What of the millions of people?"
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty is young and has only begun to govern; all under heaven look to you, and every land waits on your heart. If you prize private purity and give no thought to the world, what becomes of the ancestral temples? What becomes of the people?"

sentences.zh: 顯祖曰：「儲宮正統，受終文祖，羣公相之，有何不可。」

translations.literal: Xianzu said, "The heir's palace is the orthodox line; he received the completion from Wenzu. If all you gentlemen assist him, what is unacceptable?"
translations.idiomatic: Xianzu replied, "The crown prince is the rightful line, receiving the succession from Wenzu. With all of you to assist him, what could be wrong?"

sentences.zh: 於是傳位於高祖。

translations.literal: Thereupon he passed the throne to Gaozu.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon he passed the throne to Gaozu.

sentences.zh: 後蠕蠕犯塞，雲為中軍大都督，從顯祖討之，遇於大磧。

translations.literal: Later, when the Rouran violated the frontier, Yun became grand commander of the central army, followed Xianzu in campaigning against them, and met them in the great desert.
translations.idiomatic: Later, when the Rouran raided the frontier, Yun served as grand commander of the central army and followed Xianzu against them, meeting them in the great desert.

sentences.zh: 事具蠕蠕傳。

translations.literal: The matter is fully recorded in the Rouran biography.
translations.idiomatic: The affair is recorded in the Rouran biography.

sentences.zh: 後仇池氐反，以雲為征西大將軍討平之。

translations.literal: Later, when the Di of Qiuchi rebelled, Yun was made Grand General Who Conquers the West and suppressed them.
translations.idiomatic: Later, when the Qiuchi Di rebelled, Yun was made Grand General Who Conquers the West and put them down.

sentences.zh: 除都督徐兗二州緣淮諸軍事、征東大將軍、開府、徐州刺史。

translations.literal: He was appointed commander of military affairs along the Huai in Xu and Yan provinces, Grand General Who Conquers the East, with an opened office, and Inspector of Xu Province.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed commander of military affairs along the Huai in Xu and Yan provinces, Grand General Who Conquers the East, opened his office, and served as inspector of Xu Province.

sentences.zh: 雲以太妃蓋氏薨，表求解任，顯祖不許，雲悲號動疾，乃許之。

translations.literal: When Yun's grand consort, Lady Gai, died, he memorialized requesting release from office. Xianzu refused; Yun's grief and wailing brought on illness, and only then was he permitted.
translations.idiomatic: When Yun's grand consort, Lady Gai, died, he asked to resign. Xianzu refused, but Yun grieved and wailed until he fell ill, and only then was he allowed to step down.

sentences.zh: 性善撫綏，得徐方之心，為百姓所追戀。

translations.literal: By nature he was good at comforting and pacifying people, won the hearts of the Xu region, and was long remembered by the commoners.
translations.idiomatic: He was naturally good at soothing and governing people, won the hearts of Xu, and was remembered fondly by its people.

sentences.zh: 送遺錢貨，一無所受。

translations.literal: Of the money and goods sent to him as gifts, he accepted not a single thing.
translations.idiomatic: He refused every gift of money or goods sent to him.

sentences.zh: 顯祖聞而嘉之。

translations.literal: Xianzu heard of this and praised him.
translations.idiomatic: Xianzu heard of this and praised him.

sentences.zh: 復拜侍中、中都大官，賜帛千匹、羊千口。

translations.literal: He was again appointed Palace Attendant and high minister of the central capital, and was granted a thousand bolts of silk and a thousand sheep.
translations.idiomatic: He was again made Palace Attendant and high minister of the central capital, and received a thousand bolts of silk and a thousand sheep.

sentences.zh: 出為冀州刺史，仍本將軍。

translations.literal: He went out as Inspector of Ji Province, retaining his original generalship.
translations.idiomatic: He was sent out as inspector of Ji Province, retaining his former general's rank.

sentences.zh: 雲留心政事，甚得下情，於是合州請戶輸絹五尺、粟五升以報雲恩。

translations.literal: Yun gave close attention to government and greatly won the feelings of those below; thereupon the whole province requested that each household contribute five chi of silk and five sheng of grain to repay Yun's kindness.
translations.idiomatic: Yun governed attentively and understood those under him so well that the whole province asked to give five chi of silk and five sheng of grain per household in gratitude for his kindness.

sentences.zh: 高祖嘉之，遷使持節、都督陝西諸軍事、征南大將軍、長安鎮都大將、雍州刺史。

translations.literal: Gaozu praised him and transferred him as Bearer of the Staff, commander of military affairs in Shaanxi, Grand General Who Conquers the South, grand commander of Chang'an Garrison, and Inspector of Yong Province.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu praised him and transferred him to serve as Bearer of the Staff, commander of military affairs in Shaanxi, Grand General Who Conquers the South, commander of Chang'an Garrison, and inspector of Yong Province.

sentences.zh: 雲廉謹自修，留心庶獄，挫抑豪強，羣盜息止，州民頌之者千有餘人。

translations.literal: Yun cultivated himself in integrity and caution, attended carefully to ordinary lawsuits, suppressed the powerful and arrogant, and bandits ceased; more than a thousand people of the province sang his praises.
translations.idiomatic: Yun was upright and careful, gave close attention to common lawsuits, checked the powerful, and brought banditry to an end; more than a thousand people in the province praised him in verse.

sentences.zh: 文明太后嘉之，賜帛千匹。

translations.literal: Empress Dowager Wenming praised him and granted him a thousand bolts of silk.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Dowager Wenming praised him and gave him a thousand bolts of silk.

sentences.zh: 太和五年，薨於州。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Taihe, he died in the province.
translations.idiomatic: In Taihe year 5 he died in office in the province.

sentences.zh: 遺令薄葬，勿受賵禭。

translations.literal: His final instructions ordered a modest burial and forbade acceptance of funerary gifts.
translations.idiomatic: In his last instructions he ordered a simple burial and forbade the acceptance of funerary gifts.

sentences.zh: 諸子奉遵其旨。

translations.literal: His sons respectfully followed his wishes.
translations.idiomatic: His sons carried out his wishes.

sentences.zh: 喪至京師，車駕親臨，哭之哀慟，贈以本官，諡曰康。

translations.literal: When the coffin reached the capital, the emperor came in person, wept over him with deep grief, posthumously granted him his former offices, and gave him the title Kang.
translations.idiomatic: When his coffin reached the capital, the emperor came in person and wept bitterly over him; Yun was posthumously restored to his offices and titled Kang.

sentences.zh: 陪葬雲中之金陵。

translations.literal: He was buried beside the Jinling at Yunzhong.
translations.idiomatic: He was buried alongside the Jinling mausoleum at Yunzhong.

sentences.zh: 雲長子澄，字道鎮，少而好學。

translations.literal: Yun's eldest son Cheng, courtesy name Daozhen, loved learning from youth.
translations.idiomatic: Yun's eldest son Cheng, styled Daozhen, loved learning from an early age.

sentences.zh: 及康王薨，澄居喪以孝聞。

translations.literal: When Prince Kang died, Cheng became known for filial conduct during mourning.
translations.idiomatic: After Prince Kang died, Cheng became known for filial devotion in mourning.

sentences.zh: 襲封，加征北大將軍。

translations.literal: He inherited the fief and was additionally made Grand General Who Conquers the North.
translations.idiomatic: He inherited the fief and was given the added rank Grand General Who Conquers the North.

sentences.zh: 高祖時，蠕蠕犯塞，加澄使持節、都督北討諸軍事以討之。

translations.literal: In Gaozu's time, when the Rouran violated the frontier, Cheng was added as Bearer of the Staff and commander of the armies for the northern campaign to attack them.
translations.idiomatic: Under Gaozu, when the Rouran raided the frontier, Cheng was made Bearer of the Staff and commander of the northern expedition against them.

sentences.zh: 蠕蠕遁走，又以氐羌反叛，除都督梁益荊三州諸軍事、征南大將軍、梁州刺史。

translations.literal: The Rouran fled; later, when the Di and Qiang rebelled, he was appointed commander of military affairs in Liang, Yi, and Jing provinces, Grand General Who Conquers the South, and Inspector of Liang Province.
translations.idiomatic: The Rouran fled. Later, when the Di and Qiang rebelled, he was appointed commander of military affairs in Liang, Yi, and Jing provinces, Grand General Who Conquers the South, and inspector of Liang Province.

sentences.zh: 文明太后引見澄，誡厲之，顧謂中書令李沖曰：「此兒風神吐發，德音閑婉，當為宗室領袖。

translations.literal: Empress Dowager Wenming summoned Cheng, admonished him, and turned to Secretariat Director Li Chong, saying, "This child's bearing and expression are outstanding, and his words are gentle and refined; he will become a leader of the imperial clan.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Dowager Wenming received Cheng, admonished him, then turned to Secretariat Director Li Chong. "This young man's bearing is splendid and his speech is gentle; he will become a leader of the imperial clan.

sentences.zh: 是行使之必稱我意。

translations.literal: On this mission he will certainly satisfy my intent.
translations.idiomatic: On this mission he will surely satisfy me.

sentences.zh: 卿但記之，我不妄談人物也。」

translations.literal: You need only remember this; I do not speak of men falsely."
translations.idiomatic: Remember this: I do not misjudge men."

sentences.zh: 梁州氐帥楊仲顯、婆羅、楊卜兄弟及符叱盤等，自以居邊地險，世為山狡。

translations.literal: The Di leaders of Liang Province, Yang Zhongxian, the brothers Poluo and Yang Bu, Fu Chipan, and others relied on living in dangerous borderlands and had for generations acted as mountain brigands.
translations.idiomatic: The Di leaders in Liang Province, including Yang Zhongxian, the brothers Poluo and Yang Bu, and Fu Chipan, trusted in the rugged frontier and had long lived as mountain raiders.

sentences.zh: 澄至州，量彼風俗，誘導懷附。

translations.literal: When Cheng reached the province, he assessed their customs and guided them into submission.
translations.idiomatic: When Cheng arrived, he studied their customs and coaxed them into allegiance.

sentences.zh: 表送婆羅，授仲顯循城鎮副將，楊卜廣業太守，叱盤固道鎮副將，自餘首帥，各隨才而用之，款附者賞，違命加誅，於是仇池帖然，西南款順。

translations.literal: He memorialized to send Poluo to court, appointed Zhongxian deputy commander of Xuncheng Garrison, Yang Bu governor of Guangye, and Chipan deputy commander of Gudao Garrison; the remaining chiefs were each employed according to their talents. Those who sincerely submitted were rewarded, and those who disobeyed were punished. Thus Qiuchi became settled, and the southwest submitted.
translations.idiomatic: He sent Poluo to court, made Zhongxian deputy commander at Xuncheng, Yang Bu governor of Guangye, and Chipan deputy commander at Gudao, and used the other chiefs according to their abilities. Those who submitted were rewarded, those who resisted were punished; Qiuchi was pacified and the southwest came over.

sentences.zh: 加侍中，賜衣一襲、乘馬一匹，以旌其能。

translations.literal: He was additionally made Palace Attendant and was granted one set of robes and one riding horse to commend his ability.
translations.idiomatic: He was additionally made Palace Attendant and given a set of robes and a riding horse in recognition of his skill.

sentences.zh: 後轉征東大將軍、開府、徐州刺史，甚有聲績。

translations.literal: Later he was transferred as Grand General Who Conquers the East, opened his office, and served as Inspector of Xu Province, where he had a very strong reputation for achievement.
translations.idiomatic: Later he became Grand General Who Conquers the East, opened his office, and served as inspector of Xu Province, earning a strong record of achievement.

sentences.zh: 朝於京師，引見於皇信堂。

translations.literal: He came to court at the capital and was received in the Hall of Imperial Trust.
translations.idiomatic: He came to the capital for court audience and was received in the Hall of Imperial Trust.

sentences.zh: 高祖詔澄曰：「昔鄭子產鑄刑書，而晉叔向非之。

translations.literal: Gaozu issued an edict to Cheng: "In former times Zheng Zichan cast the written laws, and Shu Xiang of Jin criticized him.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu asked Cheng, "When Zheng Zichan cast the penal code, Shu Xiang of Jin criticized him.

sentences.zh: 此二人皆是賢士，得失竟誰？」

translations.literal: Both men were worthies; in the end, who was right and who was wrong?"
translations.idiomatic: Both were worthy men; in the end, who was right?"

sentences.zh: 對曰：「鄭國寡弱，攝於強鄰，民情去就，非刑莫制，故鑄刑書以示威。

translations.literal: Cheng replied, "The state of Zheng was weak and constrained by powerful neighbors; the people's movements could not be controlled without punishments, so Zichan cast the written laws to display authority.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng replied, "Zheng was weak and hemmed in by powerful neighbors. The people could not be controlled without punishments, so Zichan cast the laws to show authority.

sentences.zh: 雖乖古式，合今權道，隨時濟世，子產為得。

translations.literal: Though this departed from ancient norms, it suited the expedient way of that time; he adapted to the age and aided the world, so Zichan was right.
translations.idiomatic: Though it violated ancient form, it fit the needs of the moment. Zichan adapted to his age and helped the world, so he was right.

sentences.zh: 而叔向譏議，示不忘古，可與論道，未可語權。」

translations.literal: Shu Xiang's criticism showed that he did not forget antiquity; one may discuss the Way with him, but not expediency."
translations.idiomatic: Shu Xiang's criticism showed that he had not forgotten antiquity; one could discuss principle with him, but not expedience."

sentences.zh: 高祖曰：「任城當欲為魏之子產也。」

translations.literal: Gaozu said, "Rencheng must wish to be the Wei state's Zichan."
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu said, "Rencheng must wish to be Wei's Zichan."

sentences.zh: 澄曰：「子產道合當時，聲流竹素。

translations.literal: Cheng said, "Zichan's way matched his time, and his name was handed down in the bamboo and silk records.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng replied, "Zichan's way suited his time, and his name passed into the histories.

sentences.zh: 臣既庸近，何敢庶幾。

translations.literal: Your servant is mediocre and shallow; how would I dare hope to approach him?
translations.idiomatic: I am mediocre and shallow. How could I dare compare myself to him?

sentences.zh: 今陛下以四海為家，宣文德以懷天下，但江外尚阻，車書未一，季世之民，易以威伏，難以禮治。

translations.literal: Now Your Majesty has made the four seas your household and proclaims civil virtue to embrace the realm, but beyond the river there is still obstruction, and carriage tracks and writing have not yet been unified. People of a declining age are easy to subdue with authority and hard to govern by ritual.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty now makes the four seas your household and uses civil virtue to embrace the realm, but beyond the river resistance remains, and script and carriage tracks are not yet one. People in a late age are easy to subdue by force and hard to govern by ritual.

sentences.zh: 愚謂子產之法，猶應暫用，大同之後，便以道化之。」

translations.literal: In my foolish view, Zichan's laws should still be used for a time; after great unity is achieved, then they may be transformed by the Way."
translations.idiomatic: In my foolish view, Zichan's methods should still be used for a time; once unity is complete, then the Way can transform them."

sentences.zh: 高祖心方革變，深善其對，笑曰：「非任城無以識變化之體。

translations.literal: Gaozu's mind was then set on reform and change, and he deeply approved Cheng's answer, smiling as he said, "Without Rencheng, no one could understand the substance of transformation.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu was then intent on reform, and he deeply approved Cheng's answer. Smiling, he said, "Without Rencheng, no one would understand the essence of transformation.

sentences.zh: 朕方創改朝制，當與任城共萬世之功耳。」

translations.literal: I am now beginning to alter the institutions of the court and shall share with Rencheng a work for ten thousand generations."
translations.idiomatic: I am just beginning to remake the court's institutions; Rencheng and I shall share in a work for ten thousand generations."

sentences.zh: 後徵為中書令，改授尚書令。

translations.literal: Later Cheng was summoned as Director of the Secretariat, then reassigned as Director of the Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: Later Cheng was summoned as Director of the Secretariat and then made Director of the Masters of Writing.

sentences.zh: 蕭賾使庾蓽來朝，蓽見澄音韻遒雅，風儀秀逸，謂主客郎張彝曰：「往魏任城以武著稱，今魏任城乃以文見美也。」

translations.literal: When Xiao Ze sent Yu Bi to court, Bi saw that Cheng's speech was strong and elegant and his bearing fine and graceful, and he told Reception Gentleman Zhang Yi, "In the past Wei's Rencheng was known for martial prowess; now Wei's Rencheng is admired for culture."
translations.idiomatic: When Xiao Ze sent Yu Bi to court, Bi found Cheng's speech forceful and elegant and his bearing refined. He told Reception Gentleman Zhang Yi, "The former Rencheng of Wei was known for arms; this Rencheng of Wei is admired for culture."

sentences.zh: 時詔延四廟之子，下逮玄孫之冑，申宗宴於皇信堂，不以爵秩為列，悉序昭穆為次，用家人之禮。

translations.literal: At the time an edict extended invitation from sons of the four temples down to descendants in the dark-garment generation, holding an imperial-clan banquet in the Hall of Imperial Trust. They were not arranged by noble rank, but all were ordered by Zhao and Mu seniority and treated with family rites.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the court invited the imperial kin, from sons of the four temples down to great-great-grandsons, to a clan banquet in the Hall of Imperial Trust. They were seated not by rank but by ancestral order, using the rites of one family.

sentences.zh: 高祖曰：「行禮已畢，欲令宗室各言其志，可率賦詩。」

translations.literal: Gaozu said, "The rites are complete; I wish each member of the imperial clan to speak his aspirations. You may all compose poems."
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu said, "The rites are finished. I want each kinsman to state his aspirations; let each compose a poem."

sentences.zh: 特令澄為七言連韻，與高祖往復賭賽，遂至極歡，際夜乃罷。

translations.literal: He specifically ordered Cheng to compose linked seven-character rhymes, and he and Gaozu exchanged verses in contest until their joy became extreme; only when night had fallen did they stop.
translations.idiomatic: He specially ordered Cheng to compose linked seven-character rhymes. Cheng and Gaozu traded verses in playful contest until they were thoroughly delighted, stopping only late at night.

sentences.zh: 後高祖外示南討，意在謀遷，齋於明堂左个，詔太常卿王諶，親令龜卜，易筮南伐之事，其兆遇革。

translations.literal: Later Gaozu outwardly displayed plans for a southern campaign, but his intention was to plan the move of the capital. Fasting in the left chamber of the Mingtang, he ordered Grand Director of Ceremonies Wang Chen to divine personally by turtle shell and milfoil about the southern campaign; the sign received was Revolution.
translations.idiomatic: Later Gaozu publicly presented plans for a southern campaign, while actually planning the capital move. Fasting in the left chamber of the Mingtang, he had Grand Director of Ceremonies Wang Chen personally divine by turtle and milfoil about the campaign; the omen was Revolution.

sentences.zh: 高祖曰：「此是湯武革命，順天應人之卦也。」

translations.literal: Gaozu said, "This is the hexagram by which Tang and Wu changed the mandate, following Heaven and responding to men."
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu said, "This is the hexagram by which Tang and Wu changed the mandate, obeying Heaven and answering the people."

sentences.zh: 羣臣莫敢言。

translations.literal: None of the ministers dared speak.
translations.idiomatic: None of the ministers dared speak.

sentences.zh: 澄進曰：「易言革者更也。

translations.literal: Cheng stepped forward and said, "In the Changes, ge means change.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng stepped forward. "In the Changes, Revolution means change.

sentences.zh: 將欲應天順人，革君臣之命，湯武得之為吉。

translations.literal: When one is about to accord with Heaven and respond to men and change the mandate between ruler and minister, Tang and Wu obtained it as auspicious.
translations.idiomatic: When Tang and Wu obeyed Heaven, answered the people, and changed the mandate between ruler and minister, this hexagram was auspicious.

sentences.zh: 階下帝有天下，重光累葉。

translations.literal: Your Majesty possesses the realm, and bright succession has continued through many generations.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty already possesses the realm, with shining succession through many generations.

sentences.zh: 今曰卜征，乃可伐叛，不得云革命。

translations.literal: Today you call this a divination for campaign; it can mean suppressing rebels, but it cannot be called changing the mandate.
translations.idiomatic: Today the divination is for a campaign; it may mean attacking rebels, but it cannot mean changing the mandate.

sentences.zh: 此非君人之卦，未可全為吉也。」

translations.literal: This is not a hexagram for one who rules men, and it cannot be taken wholly as auspicious."
translations.idiomatic: This is not the hexagram for a reigning lord, and it cannot be taken as wholly auspicious."

sentences.zh: 高祖厲聲曰：「象云『大人虎變』，何言不吉也！」

translations.literal: Gaozu said in a stern voice, "The Image says, 'The great man changes like a tiger.' How can you say it is not auspicious?"
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu said sternly, "The Image says, 'The great man changes like a tiger.' How can you say it is not auspicious?"

sentences.zh: 澄曰：「陛下龍興既久，豈可方同虎變！」

translations.literal: Cheng said, "Your Majesty's dragon rise has long endured; how can it be compared to the tiger's change?"
translations.idiomatic: Cheng replied, "Your Majesty's dragon rise has long been established; how can it be compared to a tiger's change?"

sentences.zh: 高祖勃然作色曰：「社稷我社稷，任城而欲沮眾也！」

translations.literal: Gaozu suddenly changed color and said, "The altars of state are my altars of state; does Rencheng wish to obstruct the assembly?"
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu's face darkened. "The state is my state. Does Rencheng mean to obstruct everyone?"

sentences.zh: 澄曰：「社稷誠知陛下之社稷，然臣是社稷之臣子，豫參顧問，敢盡愚衷。」

translations.literal: Cheng said, "I truly know the altars of state are Your Majesty's altars, yet I am a servant and son of the state. Since I have been allowed to join in consultation, I dare exhaust my foolish sincerity."
translations.idiomatic: Cheng said, "I know well that the state is Your Majesty's, but I am its servant and son. Since I have been admitted to counsel, I dare give all my foolish sincerity."

sentences.zh: 高祖既銳意必行，惡澄此對，久之乃解，曰：「各言其志，亦復何傷。」

translations.literal: Gaozu was already determined to proceed and disliked Cheng's reply, but after a long while he relented and said, "Each has spoken his will; what harm is there?"
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu was determined to proceed and disliked Cheng's answer, but after a long while he relented. "Each has stated his mind; what harm is there?"

sentences.zh: 車駕還宮，便召澄，未及昇階，遙謂曰：「向者之革卦，今更欲論之。

translations.literal: When the imperial carriage returned to the palace, he at once summoned Cheng. Before Cheng had climbed the steps, Gaozu said to him from a distance, "That hexagram Revolution just now: I wish to discuss it further.
translations.idiomatic: After returning to the palace, Gaozu immediately summoned Cheng. Before Cheng had mounted the steps, Gaozu called to him from afar, "About that Revolution hexagram: I want to discuss it further.

sentences.zh: 明堂之忿，懼眾人競言，阻我大計，故厲色怖文武耳，想解朕意也。」

translations.literal: In the anger in the Mingtang, I feared that everyone would compete to speak and obstruct my great plan, and therefore I showed a stern face to frighten the civil and military officials. I suppose you understood my meaning."
translations.idiomatic: In the Mingtang, I was angry because I feared everyone would start speaking at once and block my great plan, so I put on a stern face to frighten the civil and military officials. I trust you understood my intent."

sentences.zh: 乃獨謂澄曰：「今日之行，誠知不易。

translations.literal: Then he said to Cheng alone, "Today's undertaking, I truly know, is not easy.
translations.idiomatic: Then he said to Cheng privately, "I know very well that today's undertaking is not easy.

sentences.zh: 但國家興自北土，徙居平城，雖富有四海，文軌未一，此間用武之地，非可文治，移風易俗，信為甚難。

translations.literal: Yet the state rose from the northern lands and moved to reside at Pingcheng. Though it possesses all within the four seas, writing and carriage tracks are not yet one; this place is ground for using arms, not one that can be governed by civil rule. To move customs and change habits is indeed very difficult.
translations.idiomatic: Our state rose in the north and later settled at Pingcheng. Though we possess the empire, its script and roads are not yet unified; this is a place for military power, not civil administration. Changing customs and habits here is truly difficult.

sentences.zh: 崤函帝宅，河洛王里，因茲大舉，光宅中原，任城意以為何如？」

translations.literal: Xiao and Han are the imperial dwelling, and the He and Luo are the royal precinct. If by this great act we brightly dwell in the Central Plain, what does Rencheng think?"
translations.idiomatic: The Xiao and Han passes are an imperial seat, and the He and Luo region is a royal home. If we use this great move to establish ourselves splendidly in the Central Plain, what does Rencheng think?"

sentences.zh: 澄曰：「伊洛中區，均天下所據，陛下制御華夏，輯平九服，蒼生聞此，應當大慶。」

translations.literal: Cheng said, "The Yi and Luo region is the central district, equally the place occupied by all under Heaven. If Your Majesty controls China and pacifies the nine regions, the common people, on hearing this, should greatly rejoice."
translations.idiomatic: Cheng replied, "The Yi and Luo region lies at the center, the seat shared by all under Heaven. If Your Majesty governs China from there and brings peace to the nine regions, the people will surely rejoice when they hear it."

sentences.zh: 高祖曰：「北人戀本，忽聞將移，不能不驚擾也。」

translations.literal: Gaozu said, "The northerners are attached to their roots. If they suddenly hear that a move is planned, they cannot avoid alarm and disturbance."
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu said, "The northerners cling to their homeland. If they suddenly hear that the capital is to be moved, they are bound to be alarmed and unsettled."

sentences.zh: 澄曰：「此既非常之事，當非常人所知，唯須決之聖懷，此輩亦何能為也。」

translations.literal: Cheng said, "Since this is an extraordinary matter, it is not what ordinary people should know. It need only be decided in the sacred mind; what can this crowd do?"
translations.idiomatic: Cheng replied, "This is an extraordinary matter, beyond the understanding of ordinary men. It only needs Your Majesty's decision; what can this crowd do about it?"

sentences.zh: 高祖曰：「任城便是我之子房。」

translations.literal: Gaozu said, "Rencheng is indeed my Zifang."
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu said, "Rencheng is truly my Zifang."

sentences.zh: 加撫軍大將軍、太子少保，又兼尚書左僕射。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Grand General Who Pacifies the Army and Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent, and also concurrently served as Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Grand General Who Pacifies the Army and Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent, while concurrently serving as Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs.

sentences.zh: 及駕幸洛陽，定遷都之策，高祖詔曰：「遷移之旨，必須訪眾。

translations.literal: When the imperial carriage went to Luoyang and the plan to move the capital was settled, Gaozu issued an edict saying, "The purpose of relocation must be put to consultation with the multitude.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor went to Luoyang and settled on moving the capital, Gaozu issued an edict: "The decision to relocate must be discussed with the officials.

sentences.zh: 當遣任城馳驛向代，問彼百司，論擇可否。

translations.literal: We should send Rencheng by relay horse toward Dai to ask the hundred offices there and deliberate on whether it should be chosen or not.
translations.idiomatic: Rencheng should be sent by courier to Dai to ask the officials there and discuss whether the move is acceptable.

sentences.zh: 近日論革，今真所謂革也，王其勉之。」

translations.literal: Recently we discussed change; now this is truly what is called change. Prince, exert yourself in this."
translations.idiomatic: Recently we discussed transformation; now this is transformation in the true sense. Let the prince exert himself."

sentences.zh: 既至代都，眾聞遷詔，莫不驚駭。

translations.literal: When he reached the capital at Dai, everyone who heard the edict to move the capital was shocked and frightened.
translations.idiomatic: When he arrived at the old capital of Dai, all who heard the relocation edict were shocked and alarmed.

sentences.zh: 澄援引今古，徐以曉之，眾乃開伏。

translations.literal: Cheng cited past and present and gradually explained it to them, and only then did all understand and submit.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng cited examples from antiquity and recent times, explaining the matter patiently, and only then did everyone understand and accept it.

sentences.zh: 澄遂南馳還報，會車駕於滑臺。

translations.literal: Cheng then hastened south to report back and met the imperial carriage at Huatai.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng then hurried south to report back, meeting the emperor at Huatai.

sentences.zh: 高祖大悅曰：「若非任城，朕事業不得就也。」

translations.literal: Gaozu was greatly pleased and said, "If not for Rencheng, my undertaking could not have been accomplished."
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu was delighted. "Without Rencheng, my undertaking could not have succeeded."

sentences.zh: 從幸鄴宮，除吏部尚書。

translations.literal: He followed the emperor to Ye Palace and was appointed Minister of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: He accompanied the emperor to Ye Palace and was appointed Minister of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 及幸代，車駕北巡，留澄銓簡舊臣。

translations.literal: When the emperor went to Dai and the imperial carriage made a northern tour, Cheng was left behind to select and rank the former officials.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor went to Dai and toured the north, Cheng was left to review and rank the old officials.

sentences.zh: 初，魏自公侯以下，迄于選臣，動有萬數，冗散無事。

translations.literal: At first, in Wei, from dukes and marquises down to selected officials, there were often tens of thousands, redundant and scattered, with no duties.
translations.idiomatic: At that time in Wei, from dukes and marquises down to appointed officials, there were often tens of thousands of supernumerary men, idle and without duties.

sentences.zh: 澄品為三等，量其優劣，盡其能否之用，咸無怨者。

translations.literal: Cheng graded them into three ranks, measured their merits and defects, and fully used what they could and could not do, and none resented it.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng classified them into three grades, weighed their strengths and weaknesses, and used each according to his ability; no one complained.

sentences.zh: 駕還洛京，復兼右僕射。

translations.literal: When the imperial carriage returned to the Luoyang capital, he again concurrently served as Right Vice Director.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor returned to Luoyang, Cheng again served concurrently as Right Vice Director.

sentences.zh: 高祖至北邙，遂幸洪池，命澄侍昇龍舟，因賦詩以序懷。

translations.literal: When Gaozu reached Beimang, he then went to Hongchi, ordered Cheng to attend him and board the dragon boat, and there composed poems to set forth his thoughts.
translations.idiomatic: When Gaozu reached Beimang, he went on to Hongchi, ordered Cheng to attend him aboard the imperial boat, and composed poems there to express his thoughts.

sentences.zh: 高祖曰：「朕昨夜夢一老公，頭鬢皓白，正理冠服，拜立路左。

translations.literal: Gaozu said, "Last night I dreamed of an old man, with head and temples white, properly arranging his cap and garments, bowing and standing on the left side of the road.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu said, "Last night I dreamed of an old man with white hair and temples. His cap and robes were properly arranged, and he bowed as he stood on the left side of the road.

sentences.zh: 朕怪而問之，自云晉侍中嵇紹，故此奉迎。

translations.literal: I wondered at this and asked him, and he said he was Xi Shao, Palace Attendant of Jin, and therefore had come to receive me.
translations.idiomatic: I was surprised and asked who he was. He said he was Xi Shao, Palace Attendant of Jin, and had come to welcome me.

sentences.zh: 神爽卑懼，似有求焉。」

translations.literal: His spirit was humble and fearful, as if he had some request."
translations.idiomatic: His spirit seemed humble and apprehensive, as though he had something to ask."

sentences.zh: 澄對曰：「晉世之亂，嵇紹以身衞主，殞命御側，亦是晉之忠臣；

translations.literal: Cheng replied, "In the disorder of the Jin age, Xi Shao used his own body to defend his lord and died beside the imperial carriage; he too was a loyal minister of Jin.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng replied, "During the disorders of Jin, Xi Shao shielded his lord with his own body and died at the emperor's side; he was a loyal minister of Jin.

sentences.zh: 比干遭紂兇虐，忠諫剖心，可謂殷之良士。

translations.literal: Bigan met the savagery of Zhou, and because of loyal remonstrance had his heart cut open; he may be called a worthy man of Yin.
translations.idiomatic: Bigan suffered King Zhou's cruelty and had his heart cut out for his loyal remonstrance; he may be called a worthy man of Yin.

sentences.zh: 二人俱死於王事，墳塋並在於道周。

translations.literal: Both men died in royal service, and their tombs are both beside the road.
translations.idiomatic: Both men died in service to their rulers, and both of their tombs lie beside the road.

sentences.zh: 然陛下徙御經殷墟而弔比干，至洛陽而遺嵇紹，當是希恩而感夢。」

translations.literal: Yet when Your Majesty moved the imperial carriage, you passed through the ruins of Yin and mourned Bigan, but reached Luoyang and omitted Xi Shao. It must be that he sought grace and moved you in a dream."
translations.idiomatic: Yet as Your Majesty traveled, you passed the ruins of Yin and mourned Bigan, but when you reached Luoyang you passed over Xi Shao. He must have sought your favor and moved you through a dream."

sentences.zh: 高祖曰：「朕何德，能幽感達士也。

translations.literal: Gaozu said, "What virtue do I have that I can make a hidden response reach a worthy man?
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu said, "What virtue do I possess, that I could move a worthy man in the unseen world?

sentences.zh: 然實思追禮先賢，標揚忠懿，比干、嵇紹皆是古之誠烈，而朕務濃於比干，禮略於嵇紹，情有愧然。

translations.literal: Yet I truly thought to pursue rites for former worthies and make loyalty and righteousness manifest. Bigan and Xi Shao were both sincere and fierce men of antiquity, but my attention was abundant toward Bigan and my rites slight toward Xi Shao, and in feeling I am ashamed.
translations.idiomatic: Still, I have truly wished to honor former worthies and make loyalty and righteousness shine. Bigan and Xi Shao were both faithful heroes of antiquity, but I gave Bigan rich attention and Xi Shao only slight rites. I am ashamed of this.

sentences.zh: 既有此夢，或如任城所言。」

translations.literal: Since there has been this dream, perhaps it is as Rencheng has said."
translations.idiomatic: Since this dream has occurred, perhaps it is just as Rencheng says."

sentences.zh: 於是求其兆域，遣使弔祭焉。

translations.literal: Thereupon he sought the boundaries of Xi Shao's grave site and sent envoys to offer mourning and sacrifice there.
translations.idiomatic: He then searched for the site of Xi Shao's tomb and sent envoys to mourn and sacrifice there.

sentences.zh: 蕭鸞既殺蕭昭業而自立，昭業雍州刺史曹虎請以襄陽內附。

translations.literal: After Xiao Luan killed Xiao Zhaoye and set himself up, Cao Hu, Zhaoye's Inspector of Yongzhou, requested to bring Xiangyang in allegiance.
translations.idiomatic: After Xiao Luan killed Xiao Zhaoye and took power, Cao Hu, Zhaoye's Inspector of Yongzhou, asked to surrender Xiangyang.

sentences.zh: 分遣諸將，車駕將自赴之。

translations.literal: Gaozu separately dispatched the various generals, and the imperial carriage was about to go there in person.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu sent out several generals and was preparing to go there in person.

sentences.zh: 豫州又表，虎奉誠之使不復重來。

translations.literal: Yuzhou further memorialized that Hu's envoy offering sincerity had not come again.
translations.idiomatic: Yuzhou then reported that no further envoy had come from Hu to confirm his sincerity.

sentences.zh: 高祖引澄及咸陽王禧、彭城王勰、司徒馮誕、司空穆亮、鎮南李沖等議之。

translations.literal: Gaozu brought in Cheng, Xianyang Prince Xi, Pengcheng Prince Xie, Minister over the Masses Feng Dan, Minister of Works Mu Liang, General Who Guards the South Li Chong, and others to discuss it.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu summoned Cheng, Yuan Xi the Prince of Xianyang, Yuan Xie the Prince of Pengcheng, Situ Feng Dan, Sikong Mu Liang, General Who Guards the South Li Chong, and others to discuss the matter.

sentences.zh: 高祖曰：「比得邊州表云，襄陽慕化，朕將鳴鑾江沔，為彼聲勢。

translations.literal: Gaozu said, "Recently I received a memorial from the border province saying that Xiangyang admires our transformation, and I was about to sound the imperial bells by the Jiang and Mian to give them support.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu said, "Recently I received a report from the border province saying that Xiangyang longed for our transforming rule, and I was about to take the imperial carriage to the Jiang and Mian to support them.

sentences.zh: 今復表稱，更無後信，於行留之計，竟欲如何？」

translations.literal: Now another memorial says that there has been no later message. As for the plan to go or remain, what, in the end, do you intend?"
translations.idiomatic: Now another report says there has been no later message. So, on the question of going or staying, what do you finally advise?"

sentences.zh: 禧等或云宜行，或言宜止。

translations.literal: Xi and the others sometimes said it was fitting to go, and sometimes said it was fitting to stop.
translations.idiomatic: Xi and the others were divided, some saying they should go and others saying they should stop.

sentences.zh: 高祖曰：「眾人紛紜，意見不等，朕莫知所從。

translations.literal: Gaozu said, "The many men are in confusion, and their opinions are not the same; I do not know which to follow.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu said, "Everyone is arguing at once and their opinions differ; I do not know whose advice to follow.

sentences.zh: 必欲盡行留之勢，使言理俱暢者，宜有客主，共相起發。

translations.literal: If we must exhaust the strengths of going and staying, and have words and principle both fully expressed, there should be guest and host, mutually drawing each other out.
translations.idiomatic: If we are to examine fully the case for going and the case for staying, so that both argument and principle are clear, we should set up opposing sides to draw each other out.

sentences.zh: 任城與鎮南為應留之議，朕當為宜行之論，諸公俱坐聽得失，長者從之。」

translations.literal: Rencheng and General Who Guards the South will make the argument for staying; I shall make the argument for going. Let all the lords sit and listen to the gains and losses, and follow the superior argument."
translations.idiomatic: Rencheng and the General Who Guards the South may argue for staying, and I will argue for going. Let the lords sit and hear the merits of each side, and then follow the better case."

sentences.zh: 於是高祖曰：「二賢試言留計也。」

translations.literal: Thereupon Gaozu said, "Let the two worthies try to speak on the plan for staying."
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu then said, "Let the two worthies state the plan for staying."

sentences.zh: 沖對曰：「臣等正以徒御草創，人斯樂安，內而應者未審，不宜輕爾動發。」

translations.literal: Chong replied, "We simply think that the servants and escorts have only just been established, the people are now happy in peace, and those within who would respond have not been verified; it is not fitting to set out lightly."
translations.idiomatic: Li Chong replied, "We only think that the retinue has just been organized, the people are content with peace, and the supposed supporters inside have not been confirmed. We should not set out lightly."

sentences.zh: 高祖曰：「襄陽款問，似當是虛。

translations.literal: Gaozu said, "The message of submission from Xiangyang seems likely to be false.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu said, "Xiangyang's offer of submission may well be false.

sentences.zh: 亦知初遷之民，無宜勞役。

translations.literal: I also know that the people who have just been moved should not be burdened with labor.
translations.idiomatic: I also know that the people newly moved to the capital should not be burdened with service.

sentences.zh: 脫歸誠有實，即當乘其悅附，遠則有會稽之會，近則略平江北。

translations.literal: But if the return to sincerity is real, then we should take advantage of their pleased attachment; at the farthest there may be an assembly at Kuaiji, and at the nearest we may roughly pacify the north of the Yangzi.
translations.idiomatic: But if their surrender is genuine, we should take advantage of their willingness to attach themselves to us. At best, we might hold an assembly at Kuaiji; at least, we could bring the land north of the Yangzi roughly under control.

sentences.zh: 如其送款是虛，且可遊巡淮楚，問民之瘼，使彼土蒼生，知君德之所在，復何所損而惜此一舉？

translations.literal: If their sending of submission is false, we can simply make an inspection tour of Huai and Chu, ask after the people's sufferings, and let the common people of that land know where the ruler's virtue lies. What loss would there be, that we should begrudge this one move?
translations.idiomatic: If the offer is false, we can still tour Huai and Chu, inquire into the people's hardships, and let the people there see where the ruler's virtue lies. What harm would that do, that we should shrink from this single move?

sentences.zh: 脫降問是實，而停不撫接，不亦稽阻款誠，毀朕大略也。」

translations.literal: If the surrender message is real, and we stop without comforting and receiving them, would this not delay and obstruct their sincerity of submission and ruin my grand strategy?"
translations.idiomatic: If the surrender is real and we halt without receiving and reassuring them, would that not block their sincere submission and ruin my larger plan?"

sentences.zh: 澄曰：「降問若審，應有表質。

translations.literal: Cheng said, "If the surrender message were verified, there should be a memorial and pledge.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng said, "If the surrender report were reliable, there should be a formal memorial and pledge.

sentences.zh: 而使人一返，靜無音問，其詐也可見。

translations.literal: But after the envoy returned once, there has been silence and no further word; its falseness can be seen.
translations.idiomatic: But since the envoy returned, there has been only silence and no further message. Its falseness is obvious.

sentences.zh: 今代遷之眾，人懷戀本，細累相攜，始就洛邑，居無一椽之室，家闕儋石之糧，而使怨苦即戎，泣當白刃，恐非歌舞之師也。

translations.literal: Now the multitude moved from Dai all cherish attachment to their roots; bringing wives, children, and small dependents, they have only just reached Luoyi, have no house of even a single rafter to live in, and their households lack even a dan or shi of grain. To make them resentfully and bitterly take up arms, weeping before naked blades, I fear this is not an army of song and dance.
translations.idiomatic: The people moved from Dai still long for their old home. They have only just reached Luoyang with their families and dependents; they have not even a single-raftered house to live in, and their households lack a bare measure of grain. If we drive them bitterly to war, weeping before drawn blades, this will hardly be an army marching in joy.

sentences.zh: 今茲區宇初構，又東作方興，正是子來百堵之日，農夫肆力之秋，宜寬彼逋誅，惠此民庶。

translations.literal: Now this region has only just been built, and spring plowing is just beginning. This is precisely the day when the people come to build the hundred walls, the season when farmers exert their strength. It is fitting to be lenient toward those there who have escaped punishment and to show favor to these common people.
translations.idiomatic: This region is only newly founded, and the spring labors are just beginning. It is the time for the people to build the city walls and for farmers to spend their strength in the fields. We should defer punishment over there and show kindness to the common people here.

sentences.zh: 且三軍已援，無稽赴接。

translations.literal: Moreover, the three armies have already been sent as support; there is no need for an unverified hastening to receive them.
translations.idiomatic: Besides, the armies have already been sent in support; there is no need to rush in person to receive an unverified surrender.

sentences.zh: 苟其款實，力足納撫，待克平襄沔，然後動駕。

translations.literal: If their submission is genuine, our forces are enough to take them in and pacify them; wait until Xiangyang and the Mian region have been pacified, and only then move the imperial carriage.
translations.idiomatic: If the offer is genuine, our forces are sufficient to receive and pacify them. Once Xiangyang and the Mian region have been secured, the emperor can move then.

sentences.zh: 今無故勞涉，空為往返，恐挫損天威，更成賊膽，願上覽盤庚始遷之艱難，下矜詩人由庚之至詠，輯寧新邑，惠康億兆。」

translations.literal: Now to labor and travel without cause, merely going and returning in vain, I fear will damage the heavenly majesty and instead embolden the rebels. I beg Your Majesty above to consider the hardships when Pan Geng first moved the capital, and below to pity the utmost chant of the poet in "You Geng," to bring peace to the new city and grant ease to the multitudes."
translations.idiomatic: To make this hard journey without cause, only to go and return in vain, would damage imperial majesty and embolden the rebels. I ask Your Majesty to remember the hardships Pan Geng faced when he first moved the capital, and to heed the poet's deepest praise in "You Geng": settle the new city and bring comfort to the people."

sentences.zh: 而司空亮以為宜行，公卿皆同之。

translations.literal: But Minister of Works Liang considered it fitting to go, and the dukes and ministers all agreed with him.
translations.idiomatic: But Sikong Mu Liang thought they should go, and the high ministers all agreed with him.

sentences.zh: 澄謂亮曰：「公在外見旌鉞既張，而有憂色，每聞談論，不願此行，何得對聖顏更如斯之語也。

translations.literal: Cheng said to Liang, "When you were outside and saw the banners and axes already arrayed, you had a worried look; whenever I heard you discuss it, you did not wish for this journey. How can you now, before the sacred countenance, speak like this?
translations.idiomatic: Cheng said to Liang, "Outside, when you saw the banners and axes already set out, you looked worried; whenever you discussed it, you did not want this expedition. How can you now say such things before His Majesty?

sentences.zh: 面背不同，事涉欺佞，非所謂論道之德，更失國士之體，或有傾側，當由公輩佞臣。」

translations.literal: If face and back are not the same, the matter borders on deceit and flattery. This is not the virtue called discussing the Way, and further loses the bearing of a man of state. If there is any leaning and overturning, it will be because of flatterers like you."
translations.idiomatic: To say one thing to a man's face and another behind his back borders on deceitful flattery. That is not the virtue of one who debates principle, and it falls short of the bearing of a statesman. If the state is thrown off balance, it will be because of flatterers like you."

sentences.zh: 李沖曰：「任城王可謂忠於社稷，願陛下深察其言。

translations.literal: Li Chong said, "The Prince of Rencheng may be called loyal to the altars of state. I hope Your Majesty will examine his words deeply.
translations.idiomatic: Li Chong said, "The Prince of Rencheng can truly be called loyal to the state. I hope Your Majesty will weigh his words carefully.

sentences.zh: 臣等在外，皆憚征行，唯貴與賤，不謀同辭，仰願聖心裁其可否。」

translations.literal: When we are outside, all of us dread a campaign. Noble and base alike do not consult one another yet speak the same words. I look up and hope the sacred mind will decide whether it can be done or not."
translations.idiomatic: Outside court, all of us fear the campaign. High and low have not conferred, yet we say the same thing. I beg Your Majesty to decide what is right."

sentences.zh: 高祖曰：「任城適以公等從朕，有如此論。

translations.literal: Gaozu said, "Rencheng just now used the fact that you gentlemen follow me to make such an argument.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu said, "Rencheng made that argument just because you gentlemen sided with me.

sentences.zh: 不從朕者，何必皆忠而通識安危也。

translations.literal: Must those who do not follow me all be loyal and penetratingly understand safety and danger?
translations.idiomatic: Are all who disagree with me necessarily loyal men with a penetrating grasp of danger and security?

sentences.zh: 小忠是大忠之賊，無乃似諸？」

translations.literal: Small loyalty is the thief of great loyalty. Is this not rather like that?"
translations.idiomatic: Small loyalty is the enemy of great loyalty. Is this not something like that?"

sentences.zh: 澄曰：「臣既愚闇，不識大理，所可言者，雖涉小忠，要是竭盡微款，不知大忠者竟何據？」

translations.literal: Cheng said, "I am foolish and benighted and do not know the great principle. What I can say may border on small loyalty, but in the end it exhausts my slight sincerity. I do not know, on what does great loyalty finally rest?"
translations.idiomatic: Cheng said, "I am foolish and dim and do not understand great principles. What I say may be only small loyalty, but it is the full measure of my poor sincerity. I do not know: what, in the end, is great loyalty based on?"

sentences.zh: 高祖曰：「任城脫居台鼎之任，欲令大忠在己也。」

translations.literal: Gaozu said, "If Rencheng were to occupy the responsibility of the Excellencies, he would want great loyalty to reside in himself."
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu said, "If Rencheng held the office of an Excellency, he would want great loyalty to belong to himself."

sentences.zh: 澄曰：「臣誠才非台弼，智闕和鼎，脫得濫居公鉉，庶當官而行，不負愚志。」

translations.literal: Cheng said, "My talent is indeed not that of a support to the Excellencies, and my wisdom lacks what is needed to harmonize the cauldron. If I should undeservedly occupy the handles of an Excellency, I hope I would act according to my office and not betray my foolish intent."
translations.idiomatic: Cheng replied, "My talent is not fit to support the highest offices, and my wisdom is not enough to season the cauldron of state. But if I undeservedly held an Excellency's place, I hope I would act according to the office and not betray my poor intentions."

sentences.zh: 高祖大笑。

translations.literal: Gaozu laughed loudly.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu burst out laughing.

sentences.zh: 澄又謂亮曰：「昔汲黯於漢武前面折公孫食脫粟飯，臥布被，云其詐也。

translations.literal: Cheng again said to Liang, "In the past, before Emperor Wu of Han, Ji An confronted Gongsun Hong to his face for eating coarse grain and sleeping under a cloth quilt, saying that it was fraudulent.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng then said to Liang, "Long ago, in front of Emperor Wu of Han, Ji An accused Gongsun Hong to his face of eating coarse grain and sleeping under a plain cloth quilt as a fraud.

sentences.zh: 于時公孫謙讓下之。

translations.literal: At that time Gongsun modestly yielded and placed himself below him.
translations.idiomatic: At the time, Gongsun humbly yielded and put himself below him.

sentences.zh: 武帝歎汲黯至忠，公孫長者，二人稱賢。

translations.literal: Emperor Wu sighed that Ji An was utterly loyal and Gongsun was an elder of virtue, and the two men were both called worthy.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu admired Ji An for utmost loyalty and Gongsun for elder virtue, and both men were praised as worthy.

sentences.zh: 公既道均昔士，願思長者之言。」

translations.literal: Since your way is equal to that of the old scholars, I hope you will think on the words of the elder."
translations.idiomatic: Since your conduct can equal that of men of old, I hope you will remember the elder's example."

sentences.zh: 高祖笑曰：「任城欲自比汲黯也。

translations.literal: Gaozu laughed and said, "Rencheng wishes to compare himself to Ji An.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu laughed. "Rencheng wants to compare himself to Ji An.

sentences.zh: 且所言是公，未知得失所在，何便謝司空也。」

translations.literal: Besides, what was said concerns the Duke, and it is not yet known where gain and loss lie. Why apologize to the Minister of Works so readily?"
translations.idiomatic: Besides, your words concerned the Duke, and we do not yet know who is right or wrong. Why rush to apologize to the Minister of Works?"

sentences.zh: 駕遂南伐。

translations.literal: The imperial carriage then went south on campaign.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor then went south on campaign.

sentences.zh: 五等開建，食邑一千戶。

translations.literal: When the five ranks were established, his fief was one thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: When the five ranks of nobility were instituted, his fief was set at one thousand households.

sentences.zh: 後從征至懸瓠，以篤疾還京。

translations.literal: Later he followed the campaign as far as Xuanhu, but because of severe illness returned to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Later he accompanied the campaign to Xuanhu, but returned to the capital because of serious illness.

sentences.zh: 駕餞之汝濆，賦詩而別。

translations.literal: The imperial carriage gave him a farewell banquet on the bank of the Ru and composed poems on parting.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor saw him off on the bank of the Ru River, composing poems as they parted.

sentences.zh: 車駕還洛，引見王公侍臣於清徽堂。

translations.literal: When the imperial carriage returned to Luoyang, he received the princes, dukes, and attendant ministers in Qinghui Hall.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor returned to Luoyang, he received the princes, dukes, and attendant ministers in Qinghui Hall.

sentences.zh: 高祖曰：「此堂成來，未與王公行宴樂之禮。

translations.literal: Gaozu said, "Since this hall was completed, I have not yet performed the rites of feasting and music with the princes and dukes.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu said, "Since this hall was completed, I have not yet held a proper feast here with the princes and dukes.

sentences.zh: 後東閤廡堂粗復始就，故今與諸賢欲無高而不昇，無小而不入。」

translations.literal: Afterward the eastern pavilion and side hall were roughly finished, and therefore today, together with the worthies, I wish there to be no high place we do not ascend and no small place we do not enter."
translations.idiomatic: Now that the eastern pavilion and side halls have roughly been completed, I want to go through them today with you worthies, ascending every height and entering every small place."

sentences.zh: 因之流化渠。

translations.literal: They then went to the Liuhua Canal.
translations.idiomatic: They then went to the Liuhua Canal.

sentences.zh: 高祖曰：「此曲水者亦有其義，取乾道曲成，萬物無滯。」

translations.literal: Gaozu said, "This winding water also has its meaning: it takes from the Way of Qian, which bends to complete things and lets the ten thousand things have no obstruction."
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu said, "This winding water has meaning too. It draws on the Way of Qian, which completes things by bending and leaves all things unobstructed."

sentences.zh: 次之洗煩池。

translations.literal: Next they went to the Xifan Pond.
translations.idiomatic: Next they went to the Xifan Pond.

sentences.zh: 高祖曰：「此池中亦有嘉魚。」

translations.literal: Gaozu said, "There are fine fish in this pond too."
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu said, "There are fine fish in this pond as well."

sentences.zh: 澄曰：「此所謂『魚在在藻，有頒其首』。」

translations.literal: Cheng said, "This is what is meant by, "The fish are there among the weeds; large are their heads.""
translations.idiomatic: Cheng said, "This is what the poem means: "The fish are there among the weeds; large are their heads.""

sentences.zh: 高祖曰：「且取『王在靈沼，於牣魚躍』。」

translations.literal: Gaozu said, "Let us rather take, "The king is in the Spirit Pond; how full it is, and the fish leap.""
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu said, "Let us instead take the line, "The king is at the Spirit Pond; it is full, and the fish leap.""

sentences.zh: 次之觀德殿。

translations.literal: Next they went to the Hall for Observing Virtue.
translations.idiomatic: Next they went to the Hall for Observing Virtue.

sentences.zh: 高祖曰：「射以觀德，故遂命之。」

translations.literal: Gaozu said, "Through archery one observes virtue, and therefore I named it so."
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu said, "Archery is used to observe virtue, so I gave it this name."

sentences.zh: 次之凝閑堂。

translations.literal: Next they went to the Ningxian Hall.
translations.idiomatic: Next they went to the Ningxian Hall.

sentences.zh: 高祖曰：「名目要有其義，此蓋取夫子閑居之義。

translations.literal: Gaozu said, "Names and labels must have meaning; this probably takes the meaning of the Master dwelling at leisure.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu said, "A name must have meaning. This one draws on the idea of the Master at leisure.

sentences.zh: 不可縱奢以忘儉，自安以忘危，故此堂後作茅茨堂。」

translations.literal: One must not indulge extravagance and forget frugality, nor settle in safety and forget danger; therefore behind this hall I built the Thatched Hall."
translations.idiomatic: One must not indulge in luxury and forget thrift, or rest in safety and forget danger. That is why I built the Thatched Hall behind it."

sentences.zh: 謂李沖曰：「此東曰步元廡，西曰遊凱廡。

translations.literal: He said to Li Chong, "This one to the east is called the Buyuan Gallery, and the one to the west is called the Youkai Gallery.
translations.idiomatic: He said to Li Chong, "The eastern gallery is called Buyuan, and the western one Youkai.

sentences.zh: 此堂雖無唐堯之君，卿等當無愧於元、凱。」

translations.literal: Though this hall has no ruler like Tang Yao, you gentlemen should have no shame before Yuan and Kai."
translations.idiomatic: Although this hall has no ruler equal to Tang Yao, you gentlemen should not be ashamed before Yuan and Kai."

sentences.zh: 沖對曰：「臣既遭唐堯之君，不敢辭元、凱之譽。」

translations.literal: Chong replied, "Since I have met a ruler like Tang Yao, I dare not decline the praise of Yuan and Kai."
translations.idiomatic: Chong replied, "Since I have encountered a ruler like Tang Yao, I dare not refuse the praise of being Yuan or Kai."

sentences.zh: 高祖曰：「光景垂落，朕同宗則有載考之義，卿等將出無遠，何得默爾，不示德音。」

translations.literal: Gaozu said, "The light and shadows are about to fall. For my men of the same clan, there is the meaning of continuing the night gathering; you gentlemen are about to go out and are not far off, so how can you be silent and not show virtuous sounds?"
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu said, "The daylight is fading. For my clansmen there is the duty of continuing the feast into the night, and you gentlemen are about to withdraw though the hour is not far advanced. How can you stay silent and not give us worthy words?"

sentences.zh: 即命黃門侍郎崔光、郭祚，通直郎邢巒、崔休等賦詩言志。

translations.literal: He at once ordered Palace Attendant of the Yellow Gates Cui Guang and Guo Zuo, and Gentleman for Unrestricted Attendance Xing Luan, Cui Xiu, and others to compose poems expressing their intentions.
translations.idiomatic: He then ordered Cui Guang and Guo Zuo, Palace Attendants of the Yellow Gates, and Xing Luan, Cui Xiu, and others, Gentlemen for Unrestricted Attendance, to compose poems expressing their thoughts.

sentences.zh: 燭至，公卿辭退。

translations.literal: When the candles arrived, the dukes and ministers took leave and withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: When the candles were brought in, the dukes and ministers took their leave.

sentences.zh: 李沖再拜上千萬歲壽。

translations.literal: Li Chong bowed twice and offered a toast for ten thousand times ten thousand years.
translations.idiomatic: Li Chong bowed twice and offered a long-life toast of countless years.

sentences.zh: 高祖曰：「卿向以燭至致辭，復獻千萬之壽，朕報卿以南山之詩。」

translations.literal: Gaozu said, "You just now offered words of departure when the candles arrived, and then presented a toast of ten thousand times ten thousand years. I answer you with the poem of the Southern Mountain."
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu said, "You used the arrival of the candles as a reason to withdraw, and then offered a toast of countless years. I will answer you with the poem of the Southern Mountain."

sentences.zh: 高祖曰：「燭至辭退，庶姓之禮；

translations.literal: Gaozu said, "Withdrawing when the candles arrive is the rite for those of other surnames;
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu said, "Taking leave when the candles arrive is the rite for those of other surnames;

sentences.zh: 在夜載考，宗族之義。

translations.literal: continuing the night gathering is the duty of the imperial clan.
translations.idiomatic: continuing the gathering into the night is the duty of the imperial clan.

sentences.zh: 卿等且還，朕與諸王宗室，欲成此夜飲。」

translations.literal: You gentlemen may return for now; I and the princes and imperial clansmen wish to complete this night's drinking."
translations.idiomatic: You gentlemen may go home for now. I and the princes of the imperial clan wish to finish tonight's drinking."

sentences.zh: 又從幸鄴。

translations.literal: He again followed the emperor to Ye.
translations.idiomatic: He again accompanied the emperor to Ye.

sentences.zh: 還洛，以出納之勞，增邑五百戶。

translations.literal: On returning to Luoyang, because of his labor in receiving and dispatching affairs, his fief was increased by five hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: After returning to Luoyang, his fief was increased by five hundred households for his work handling communications and affairs.

sentences.zh: 坐公事免官。

translations.literal: Because of an official matter, he was dismissed from office.
translations.idiomatic: He was dismissed from office over an official matter.

sentences.zh: 尋兼吏部尚書。

translations.literal: Soon he concurrently served as Minister of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was made acting Minister of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 恒州刺史穆泰在州謀反，推朔州刺史陽平王頤為主。

translations.literal: Mu Tai, Inspector of Hengzhou, plotted rebellion in his province and put forward Yi, Prince of Yangping and Inspector of Shuozhou, as leader.
translations.idiomatic: Mu Tai, Inspector of Hengzhou, plotted rebellion in his province and proposed Yuan Yi, Prince of Yangping and Inspector of Shuozhou, as their leader.

sentences.zh: 頤表其狀。

translations.literal: Yi memorialized the circumstances.
translations.idiomatic: Yi reported the situation in a memorial.

sentences.zh: 高祖召澄入見凝閑堂，曰：「適得陽平表曰，穆泰謀為不軌，招誘宗室。

translations.literal: Gaozu summoned Cheng in to be seen at Ningxian Hall and said, "I have just received Yangping's memorial, saying that Mu Tai is plotting lawlessness and enticing the imperial clan.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu summoned Cheng to Ningxian Hall and said, "I have just received Yangping's memorial. It says that Mu Tai is plotting rebellion and trying to draw in members of the imperial clan.

sentences.zh: 脫或必然，遷京甫爾，北人戀舊，南北紛擾，朕洛陽不立也。

translations.literal: If this should prove certainly true, the move of the capital has only just happened, the northerners are attached to the old place, north and south will be in disorder, and my Luoyang will not stand.
translations.idiomatic: If this is true, the capital has only just been moved, the northerners still cling to the old places, north and south will fall into turmoil, and my Luoyang will not stand.

sentences.zh: 此事非任城不辦，可為我力疾向北。

translations.literal: This matter cannot be handled by anyone but Rencheng; for me, exert yourself despite illness and go north.
translations.idiomatic: No one but Rencheng can handle this. For my sake, struggle through your illness and go north.

sentences.zh: 如其弱也，直往擒翦；

translations.literal: If he is weak, go straight there and seize and cut him down;
translations.idiomatic: If he is weak, go directly and capture or destroy him;

sentences.zh: 若其勢強，可承制發并肆兵以殄之。

translations.literal: if his power is strong, you may receive authority from the throne and call out the troops of Bing and Si to annihilate him.
translations.idiomatic: if his forces are strong, you may act under imperial authority and mobilize the troops of Bing and Si to wipe him out.

sentences.zh: 雖知王患，既是國家大事，不容辭也。」

translations.literal: Although I know the Prince is ill, this is a great affair of state and does not permit refusal."
translations.idiomatic: I know you are ill, but this is a great matter of state and cannot be declined."

sentences.zh: 澄曰：「泰等愚惑，正戀本為此，非有遠圖。

translations.literal: Cheng said, "Mu Tai and the others are foolish and deluded; they are doing this only because they are attached to their old home, and they have no far-reaching plan.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng said, "Mu Tai and the others are foolish and confused. They do this only from attachment to their old home; they have no long-term plan.

sentences.zh: 臣誠怯弱，不憚是輩，雖復患惙，豈敢有辭。

translations.literal: I am indeed timid and weak, but I do not fear this sort. Though I am again ill and exhausted, how would I dare make any refusal?
translations.idiomatic: I am timid and weak, but I do not fear men like these. Though I am ill and worn down, how could I dare refuse?

sentences.zh: 謹當罄盡心力，繼之以死，願陛下勿憂。」

translations.literal: I shall reverently exhaust all my heart and strength and follow it with death; I hope Your Majesty will not worry."
translations.idiomatic: I will devote all my heart and strength, even unto death. I ask Your Majesty not to worry."

sentences.zh: 高祖笑曰：「得任城此行，朕復何憂也。」

translations.literal: Gaozu laughed and said, "Having Rencheng make this journey, what further worry do I have?"
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu laughed. "With Rencheng making this trip, what do I have left to worry about?"

sentences.zh: 遂授節，銅虎、竹使符，御仗，左右，仍行恒州事。

translations.literal: Thereupon he granted him the staff of authority, bronze tiger and bamboo envoy tallies, imperial weapons, and attendants on left and right, and had him continue to act in the affairs of Hengzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He then granted Cheng the staff, bronze tiger tally and bamboo envoy tally, imperial weapons and attendants, and had him administer Hengzhou affairs.

sentences.zh: 行達雁門，太守夜告泰已握眾西就陽平，城下聚結，唯見弓仗。

translations.literal: When his journey reached Yanmen, the commandery governor reported at night that Tai had already taken control of the crowd and gone west to join Yangping; below the city they were gathering, and only bows and weapons could be seen.
translations.idiomatic: When Cheng reached Yanmen, the governor reported by night that Mu Tai had gathered his followers and gone west to join Yangping. Men were assembling below the city, and bows and weapons were everywhere.

sentences.zh: 澄聞便速進。

translations.literal: When Cheng heard this, he immediately advanced rapidly.
translations.idiomatic: On hearing this, Cheng advanced at once.

sentences.zh: 時右丞孟斌曰：「事不可量，須依敕召并肆兵，然後徐動。」

translations.literal: At the time, Right Aide Meng Bin said, "The situation cannot be measured; we must follow the edict and summon the troops of Bing and Si, and only afterward move slowly."
translations.idiomatic: Right Aide Meng Bin said, "The situation is uncertain. We should obey the edict, summon the troops of Bing and Si, and only then proceed carefully."

sentences.zh: 澄曰：「泰既構逆，應據堅城，而更迎陽平，度其所為，似當勢弱。

translations.literal: Cheng said, "Since Tai has formed a rebellion, he should occupy a strong city, yet instead he has gone to meet Yangping. Judging what he is doing, his position seems likely to be weak.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng said, "If Tai has truly mounted a rebellion, he should be holding a strong city; instead he has gone to meet Yangping. From his conduct, his position seems weak.

sentences.zh: 泰既不相拒，無故發兵，非宜也。

translations.literal: Since Tai is not resisting us, to raise troops without cause is not fitting.
translations.idiomatic: Since Tai is not opposing us directly, it would be wrong to call up troops without cause.

sentences.zh: 但速往鎮之，民心自定。」

translations.literal: If we only go there quickly and suppress it, the hearts of the people will settle of themselves."
translations.idiomatic: If we simply get there quickly and hold things down, the people will settle by themselves."

sentences.zh: 遂倍道兼行，出其不意。

translations.literal: He then traveled double stages and pressed the journey, coming out where they did not expect him.
translations.idiomatic: He then doubled his stages, pressed forward, and caught them by surprise.

sentences.zh: 又遣治書侍御史李煥先赴，至即擒泰，民情怡然。

translations.literal: He also sent Li Huan, Investigating Censor for the Bureau of Evaluation, ahead; when Huan arrived, he immediately seized Tai, and the people's feelings were calm and pleased.
translations.idiomatic: He also sent Li Huan, Investigating Censor for the Bureau of Evaluation, ahead. When Li Huan arrived he immediately captured Tai, and the people were reassured.

sentences.zh: 窮其黨與，罪人皆得，鉅鹿公陸叡、安樂侯元隆等百餘人皆獄禁。

translations.literal: They pursued his associates to the end, and all the criminals were obtained; Lu Rui, Duke of Julu, Yuan Long, Marquis of Anle, and more than a hundred others were all imprisoned.
translations.idiomatic: They tracked down his associates and captured all the offenders. Lu Rui, Duke of Julu, Yuan Long, Marquis of Anle, and more than a hundred others were imprisoned.

sentences.zh: 具狀表聞，高祖覽表大悅，召集公卿以下以表示之，曰：「我任城可謂社稷臣也，尋其罪案，正復臯陶斷獄，豈能過之。」

translations.literal: He reported the full circumstances in a memorial. Gaozu read the memorial and was greatly pleased; he summoned and gathered the dukes and ministers and those below them, showed them the memorial, and said, "My Rencheng may be called a minister of the altars of state. If one examines his criminal case, even Gaoyao deciding lawsuits, how could he surpass it?"
translations.idiomatic: Cheng reported the full case in a memorial. Gaozu read it with great delight, summoned the high ministers and officials, showed them the memorial, and said, "My Rencheng may truly be called a minister of state. In investigating this case, even Gaoyao himself could not have surpassed him."

sentences.zh: 顧謂咸陽王等曰：「汝等脫當其處，不能辦此。」

translations.literal: He looked back and said to the Prince of Xianyang and the others, "If you had been in that position, you could not have handled this."
translations.idiomatic: He turned to the Prince of Xianyang and the others. "Had you been in his place, you could not have managed this."

sentences.zh: 車駕尋幸平城，勞澄曰：「任城此行，深副遠寄。」

translations.literal: The imperial carriage soon went to Pingcheng, and he comforted Cheng, saying, "Rencheng's journey has deeply fulfilled the distant charge."
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward the emperor went to Pingcheng and commended Cheng: "Rencheng's mission has fully answered the trust placed in him from afar."

sentences.zh: 對曰：「陛下威靈遠被，罪人無所逃刑，臣何勞之有。」

translations.literal: He replied, "Your Majesty's awe-inspiring spirit reaches far; the criminals had nowhere to escape punishment. What labor of mine was there?"
translations.idiomatic: Cheng replied, "Your Majesty's awe reaches far; the guilty had nowhere to escape punishment. What effort of mine was there?"

sentences.zh: 引見逆徒，無一人稱枉，時人莫不歎之。

translations.literal: When the rebel followers were brought in and seen, not one person claimed injustice, and people of the time all sighed in admiration.
translations.idiomatic: When the rebels were presented, not one claimed to have been wronged, and everyone at the time marveled.

sentences.zh: 高祖顧謂左右曰：「昔仲尼云：『聽訟吾猶人也，必也使無訟乎。』

translations.literal: Gaozu looked back and said to his attendants, "In the past Zhongni said, 'In hearing lawsuits I am like other men; what is necessary is to make there be no lawsuits.'
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu turned to his attendants and said, "Long ago Confucius said, 'In hearing lawsuits I am no different from others; what matters is making it so there are no lawsuits.'

sentences.zh: 然聖人之聽訟，殆非常人所匹，必也無訟，今日見之矣。」

translations.literal: Yet a sage's hearing of lawsuits is probably not something ordinary men can match; as for there necessarily being no lawsuits, today I have seen it."
translations.idiomatic: But a sage's handling of cases is hardly something ordinary men can match. Today I have seen what it means to leave no one with a grievance."

sentences.zh: 以澄正尚書。

translations.literal: He made Cheng a regular Minister of State Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He made Cheng a full Minister of State Affairs.

sentences.zh: 車駕南伐，留澄居守，復兼右僕射。

translations.literal: When the imperial carriage campaigned south, Cheng was left to guard the capital and again concurrently served as Right Vice Director.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor campaigned south, Cheng was left in charge of the capital and again concurrently served as Right Vice Director.

sentences.zh: 澄表請以國秩一歲租布帛助供軍資，詔受其半。

translations.literal: Cheng memorialized requesting that one year's rent in cloth and silk from his state rank be used to help provide military supplies; the edict accepted half of it.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng memorialized asking to contribute one year of his fief income in cloth and silk to military supplies; by edict the court accepted half.

sentences.zh: 高祖幸鄴，值高車樹者反叛，車駕將親討之。

translations.literal: When Gaozu went to Ye, he encountered the rebellion of the Shuzhe of the Gaoche, and the imperial carriage was about to campaign against them in person.
translations.idiomatic: When Gaozu went to Ye, the Shuzhe branch of the Gaoche rebelled, and the emperor was about to campaign against them personally.

sentences.zh: 澄表諫不宜親行。

translations.literal: Cheng memorialized in remonstrance that it was not fitting for him to go in person.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng sent a memorial remonstrating that the emperor should not go in person.

sentences.zh: 會江陽王繼平之，乃止。

translations.literal: It happened that Jiangyang Prince Ji pacified them, and so it stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Then Yuan Ji, Prince of Jiangyang, pacified them, and the expedition was called off.

sentences.zh: 高祖還洛，引見公卿。

translations.literal: When Gaozu returned to Luoyang, he received the dukes and ministers.
translations.idiomatic: When Gaozu returned to Luoyang, he received the high ministers.

sentences.zh: 高祖曰：「營國之本，禮教為先。

translations.literal: Gaozu said, "In the foundation of ordering the state, ritual teaching comes first.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu said, "Ritual instruction comes first in ordering the state.

sentences.zh: 朕離京邑以來，禮教為日新以不？」

translations.literal: Since I left the capital city, has ritual teaching become daily renewed or not?"
translations.idiomatic: Since I left the capital, has ritual instruction been renewed day by day, or not?"

sentences.zh: 澄對曰：「臣謂日新。」

translations.literal: Cheng replied, "I think it is daily renewed."
translations.idiomatic: Cheng replied, "I believe it has been renewed day by day."

sentences.zh: 高祖曰：「朕昨入城，見車上婦人冠帽而著小襦襖者，若為如此，尚書何為不察？」
