translations.literal: Gaozu said, "Yesterday, when I entered the city, I saw women on carts wearing caps and dressed in small short jackets. If things are like this, why does the Ministry not inspect it?"
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu said, "Yesterday as I entered the city, I saw women on carts wearing caps and little short jackets. If this is going on, why has the Ministry failed to investigate?"

sentences.zh: 澄曰：「著猶少於不著者。」

translations.literal: Cheng said, "Those wearing them are still fewer than those not wearing them."
translations.idiomatic: Cheng said, "Those wearing them are still fewer than those who are not."

sentences.zh: 高祖曰：「深可怪也！

translations.literal: Gaozu said, "This is deeply astonishing!
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu said, "That is astonishing!

sentences.zh: 任城意欲令全著乎？

translations.literal: Does Rencheng mean to have them all wear them?
translations.idiomatic: Does Rencheng mean he wants all of them to wear such things?

sentences.zh: 一言可以喪邦者，斯之謂歟？

translations.literal: A single word may lose a state: is this what is meant?
translations.idiomatic: Is this what is meant by a single word being able to ruin a state?

sentences.zh: 可命史官書之。」

translations.literal: Order the historian to write this down."
translations.idiomatic: Have the historian record it."

sentences.zh: 又曰：「王者不降佐於蒼昊，皆拔才而用之。

translations.literal: He also said, "Kings do not receive assistants sent down by blue Heaven; they all select talent and use it.
translations.idiomatic: He also said, "Rulers do not receive assistants dropped down from Heaven; they select talented men and employ them.

sentences.zh: 朕失於舉人，任許一羣婦人輩奇事，當更銓簡耳。

translations.literal: I erred in choosing men, allowing the strange affair of a group of women. We should select and rank officials anew.
translations.idiomatic: I made a mistake in appointing men, allowing this strange business with a group of women. The officials must be reviewed and selected again.

sentences.zh: 任城在省，為舉天下綱維，為當署事而已？」

translations.literal: Is Rencheng in the department in order to raise up the guiding ropes of all under Heaven, or merely to sign documents?"
translations.idiomatic: Is Rencheng in the department to uphold the governing order of the realm, or merely to sign papers?"

sentences.zh: 澄曰：「臣實署事而已。」

translations.literal: Cheng said, "I am indeed only signing documents."
translations.idiomatic: Cheng said, "In truth, I am only signing papers."

sentences.zh: 高祖曰：「如此便一令史足矣，何待任城。」

translations.literal: Gaozu said, "If it is like this, then one clerk is enough. Why wait for Rencheng?"
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu said, "If that is so, one clerk would be enough. Why would we need Rencheng?"

sentences.zh: 又曰：「我遣舍人宣詔，何為使小人聞之？」

translations.literal: He also said, "I sent a palace attendant to proclaim the edict; why did you let petty men hear it?"
translations.idiomatic: He also said, "I sent a palace attendant to proclaim the edict. Why did you let petty men hear it?"

sentences.zh: 澄曰：「時雖有幹吏，去榜亦遠。」

translations.literal: Cheng said, "At the time, although there were capable officials, they were also far from the proclamation board."
translations.idiomatic: Cheng said, "At the time there were capable officials, but they too were far from the posted proclamation."

sentences.zh: 高祖曰：「遠則不聞，聞則不遠。

translations.literal: Gaozu said, "If they were far away, they would not have heard; if they heard, they were not far away.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu said, "If they were far away, they could not have heard it; if they heard it, they were not far away.

sentences.zh: 既得聞詔，理故可知。」

translations.literal: Since they were able to hear the edict, the principle could certainly be known."
translations.idiomatic: Since they heard the edict, they should have understood the principle."

sentences.zh: 於是留守羣臣遂免冠謝罪。

translations.literal: Thereupon the ministers left to guard the capital all removed their caps and apologized for their offense.
translations.idiomatic: The ministers left in charge of the capital then removed their caps and apologized for their fault.

sentences.zh: 尋除尚書右僕射。

translations.literal: Soon he was appointed Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was appointed Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs.

sentences.zh: 蕭寶卷遣其太尉陳顯達入寇漢陽。

translations.literal: Xiao Baojuan sent his Grand Commandant Chen Xianda to invade Hanyang.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Baojuan sent his Grand Commandant Chen Xianda to invade Hanyang.

sentences.zh: 是時高祖不豫，引澄入見清徽堂。

translations.literal: At this time Gaozu was unwell and brought Cheng in for audience at Qinghui Hall.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Gaozu was ill, and he summoned Cheng to Qinghui Hall.

sentences.zh: 詔曰：「顯達侵亂，沔陽不安，朕不親行，莫攘此賊。

translations.literal: The edict said, "Xianda is invading and causing disorder, and Mianyang is not at peace. If I do not go in person, no one will drive off this rebel.
translations.idiomatic: The edict said, "Xianda has invaded and thrown Mianyang into disorder. Unless I go in person, no one will repel this rebel.

sentences.zh: 朕疾患淹年，氣力惙弊，如有非常，委任城大事。

translations.literal: My illness has lingered for years, and my strength and breath are exhausted. If anything extraordinary happens, I entrust great affairs to Rencheng.
translations.idiomatic: My illness has dragged on for years, and my strength is spent. If anything unexpected happens, I entrust the great affairs to Rencheng.

sentences.zh: 是段任城必須從朕。」

translations.literal: On this occasion Rencheng must follow me."
translations.idiomatic: For this campaign, Rencheng must accompany me."

sentences.zh: 澄涕泣對曰：「臣謹當竭股肱之力，以命上報。」

translations.literal: Cheng replied in tears, "I shall respectfully exhaust the strength of my limbs and repay Your Majesty with my life."
translations.idiomatic: Cheng replied through tears, "I will devote all the strength of my limbs and repay Your Majesty with my life."

sentences.zh: 遂從駕南伐。

translations.literal: He then followed the imperial carriage on the southern campaign.
translations.idiomatic: He then accompanied the emperor on the southern campaign.

sentences.zh: 高祖崩，澄受顧命。

translations.literal: When Gaozu died, Cheng received the testamentary charge.
translations.idiomatic: When Gaozu died, Cheng received his final charge.

sentences.zh: 世宗初，有降人嚴叔懋告尚書令王肅遣孔思達潛通寶卷，圖為叛逆，寶卷遣俞公喜送敕於肅，公喜還南，肅與裴叔業馬為信。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Shizong's reign, a surrendered man, Yan Shumao, accused Wang Su, Director of the Department of State Affairs, of sending Kong Sida to communicate secretly with Baojuan and plot rebellion; Baojuan had sent Yu Gongxi to deliver an edict to Su, Gongxi had returned south, and Su and Pei Shuye had used horses as tokens.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of Shizong's reign, a defector named Yan Shumao accused Wang Su, Director of the Department of State Affairs, of sending Kong Sida to communicate secretly with Baojuan and plot rebellion. Baojuan, he said, had sent Yu Gongxi with an edict for Su; after Gongxi returned south, Su and Pei Shuye exchanged horses as tokens.

sentences.zh: 澄信之，乃表肅將叛，輒下禁止。

translations.literal: Cheng believed this, and therefore memorialized that Su was about to rebel, then immediately placed him under detention.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng believed the accusation, memorialized that Su was about to rebel, and immediately detained him.

sentences.zh: 咸陽、北海二王奏澄擅禁宰輔，免官歸第。

translations.literal: The two princes of Xianyang and Beihai memorialized that Cheng had arbitrarily detained a chief minister; he was dismissed from office and returned to his residence.
translations.idiomatic: The princes of Xianyang and Beihai memorialized that Cheng had detained a chief minister on his own authority, and Cheng was dismissed and sent home.

sentences.zh: 尋出為平西將軍、梁州刺史。

translations.literal: Soon he was sent out as General Who Pacifies the West and Inspector of Liangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was sent out as General Who Pacifies the West and Inspector of Liangzhou.

sentences.zh: 辭以母老。

translations.literal: He declined on the grounds that his mother was old.
translations.idiomatic: He declined because his mother was elderly.

sentences.zh: 除安東將軍、相州刺史，復固辭。

translations.literal: He was appointed General Who Pacifies the East and Inspector of Xiangzhou, but again firmly declined.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed General Who Pacifies the East and Inspector of Xiangzhou, but again firmly refused.

sentences.zh: 改授安西將軍、雍州刺史。

translations.literal: The appointment was changed to General Who Pacifies the West and Inspector of Yongzhou.
translations.idiomatic: His appointment was changed to General Who Pacifies the West and Inspector of Yongzhou.

sentences.zh: 尋徵赴季秋講武。

translations.literal: Soon he was summoned to attend the late-autumn martial review.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was summoned to attend the late-autumn martial review.

sentences.zh: 除都督淮南諸軍事、鎮南大將軍、開府、揚州刺史。

translations.literal: He was appointed Commander of all military affairs in Huainan, Grand General Who Guards the South, with an open office, and Inspector of Yangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Commander of all military affairs in Huainan, Grand General Who Guards the South with an open office, and Inspector of Yangzhou.

sentences.zh: 下車封孫叔敖之墓，毀蔣子文之廟。

translations.literal: When he arrived in office, he sealed the tomb of Sunshu Ao and destroyed the temple of Jiang Ziwen.
translations.idiomatic: On taking office, he marked and protected Sunshu Ao's tomb and destroyed the temple of Jiang Ziwen.

sentences.zh: 頻表南伐，世宗不許。

translations.literal: He repeatedly memorialized in favor of a southern campaign, but Shizong did not permit it.
translations.idiomatic: He repeatedly memorialized urging a southern campaign, but Shizong would not allow it.

sentences.zh: 又辭母老，乞解州任，寢而不報。

translations.literal: He again declined because his mother was old and begged to be relieved of his provincial office, but the request was put aside without reply.
translations.idiomatic: Again citing his mother's age, he asked to be relieved of the province, but the request was shelved without response.

sentences.zh: 加散騎常侍。

translations.literal: He was additionally made Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary.
translations.idiomatic: He was additionally made Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary.

sentences.zh: 澄表曰：「臣參訓先朝，藉規有日，前言舊軌，頗亦聞之。

translations.literal: Cheng memorialized, "I took part in instruction under the former court and have long relied upon its norms; I have also heard something of former sayings and old regulations.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng memorialized, "I took part in the instruction of the former court and have long lived under its rules; I have heard something of its words and precedents.

sentences.zh: 又昔在恒代，親習皇宗，熟祕序疑庭無闕日。

translations.literal: Moreover, in former times at Heng and Dai, I personally became familiar with the imperial clan; the schools, secret repositories, ordered inquiries, and court discussions had no days of absence.
translations.idiomatic: In earlier days at Heng and Dai, I was personally familiar with the imperial clan, and there was no lack of instruction, inquiry, and court discussion.

sentences.zh: 臣每於侍坐，先帝未嘗不以書典在懷，禮經為事，周旋之則，不輟於時。

translations.literal: Whenever I attended in seated audience, the former emperor never failed to keep the books and classics in mind and to make the ritual classics his business; the rules of movement and conduct were never interrupted at any time.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever I sat in attendance, the former emperor always kept the texts and classics in mind and made the ritual classics his concern; the rules of conduct were never neglected.

sentences.zh: 自鳳舉中京，方隆禮教，宗室之範，每蒙委及，四門之選，負荷銓量。

translations.literal: Since the phoenix rose to the central capital, ritual teaching was then flourishing. The standards of the imperial clan were often entrusted to me, and in the selection for the Four Gates I bore the burden of weighing and ranking.
translations.idiomatic: After the move to the central capital, ritual instruction flourished. Matters concerning the imperial clan's standards were often entrusted to me, and I bore responsibility for evaluating candidates for the Four Gates school.

sentences.zh: 自先皇升遐，未遑修述，學宮虛荷四門之名，宗人有闕四時之業，青衿之緒，於茲將廢。

translations.literal: Since the former emperor ascended afar, there has been no leisure to repair and set forth these things; the school palace emptily bears the name of the Four Gates, the clansmen lack the work of the four seasons, and the line of blue-collared students is about to be abandoned here.
translations.idiomatic: Since the former emperor passed away, there has been no time to restore these institutions. The school palace bears the Four Gates name in vain, the clansmen lack their seasonal studies, and the line of students is on the verge of disappearing.

sentences.zh: 臣每惟其事，竊所傷懷。

translations.literal: Whenever I think on this matter, it secretly grieves my heart.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever I think of this, I am privately grieved.

sentences.zh: 伏惟聖略宏遠，四方罕務，宴安之辰，於是乎在。

translations.literal: I bow and consider that Your Sacred Strategy is vast and far-reaching, and there are few pressing affairs on the four sides; the time of repose and security is now.
translations.idiomatic: I humbly think that Your Majesty's strategy is broad and far-reaching, and with few urgent affairs on the frontiers, this is the moment for secure repose.

sentences.zh: 何為太平之世，而令子衿之歎興焉；

translations.literal: Why, in an age of great peace, should the lament over the students arise?
translations.idiomatic: Why, in an age of great peace, should the lament for neglected students arise?

sentences.zh: 聖明之日，而使宗人之訓闕焉。

translations.literal: In days of sage brightness, why allow the instruction of the clansmen to be lacking?
translations.idiomatic: Why, in days of sage enlightenment, should the instruction of the imperial clan be lacking?

sentences.zh: 愚謂可敕有司，修復皇宗之學，開闢四門之教，使將落之族，日就月將。」

translations.literal: In my foolish opinion, an order may be given to the proper offices to restore the school of the imperial clan and open the teaching of the Four Gates, so that the clan now about to decline may advance by day and improve by month."
translations.idiomatic: In my foolish view, the offices should be ordered to restore the imperial clan school and reopen the Four Gates instruction, so that a clan now close to decline may improve day by day and month by month."

sentences.zh: 詔曰：「冑子崇業，自古盛典，國均之訓，無應久廢，尚書更可量宜修立。」

translations.literal: The edict said, "For sons of nobles to honor their studies has been a grand institution since antiquity, and the instruction of the state schools should not long remain abandoned. The Department of State Affairs may again assess what is suitable and restore it."
translations.idiomatic: The edict said, "The education of noble sons has been a great institution since antiquity, and instruction in the state schools should not long be abandoned. The Department may consider what is suitable and restore it."

sentences.zh: 澄又表母疾解州任，不聽。

translations.literal: Cheng again memorialized that his mother was ill and asked to be relieved of his provincial office, but it was not permitted.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng again memorialized that his mother was ill and asked to be relieved of his province, but this was not allowed.

sentences.zh: 蕭衍將張囂之寇陷夷陵戍，澄遣輔國將軍成興步騎赴討，大破之，復夷陵，囂之遁走。

translations.literal: Xiao Yan's general Zhang Xiaozhi attacked and captured the Yiling Garrison; Cheng sent General Who Assists the State Cheng Xing with infantry and cavalry to go and attack him, greatly defeated him, recovered Yiling, and Xiaozhi fled.
translations.idiomatic: When Xiao Yan's general Zhang Xiaozhi captured the Yiling Garrison, Cheng sent Cheng Xing, General Who Assists the State, with infantry and cavalry to attack. Cheng Xing defeated him badly, recovered Yiling, and Xiaozhi fled.

sentences.zh: 又遣長風戍主奇道顯攻蕭衍陰山戍，破之，斬其戍主龍驤將軍、都亭侯梅興祖。

translations.literal: He also sent Qi Daoxian, commander of the Changfeng Garrison, to attack Xiao Yan's Yinshan Garrison; he defeated it and beheaded its garrison commander, Mei Xingzu, General Who Rouses Dragons and Marquis of Duting.
translations.idiomatic: He also sent Qi Daoxian, commander of Changfeng Garrison, to attack Xiao Yan's Yinshan Garrison. Qi defeated it and beheaded its commander Mei Xingzu, General Who Rouses Dragons and Marquis of Duting.

sentences.zh: 仍引攻白槀戍，又破之，斬其寧朔將軍、關內侯吳道爽。

translations.literal: He then led the attack on Baigao Garrison, again defeated it, and beheaded its General Who Pacifies the North and Marquis within the Passes, Wu Daoshuang.
translations.idiomatic: He then pressed on to attack Baigao Garrison, defeated it as well, and beheaded Wu Daoshuang, General Who Pacifies the North and Marquis within the Passes.

sentences.zh: 澄表曰：「蕭衍頻斷東關，欲令巢湖汎溢。

translations.literal: Cheng memorialized, "Xiao Yan has repeatedly cut through Dongguan, wishing to make Chaohu overflow.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng memorialized, "Xiao Yan has repeatedly breached Dongguan, intending to make Chaohu overflow.

sentences.zh: 湖周回四百餘里，東關合江之際，廣不過數十步，若賊計得成，大湖傾注者，則淮南諸戍必同晉陽之事矣。

translations.literal: The lake is more than four hundred li around. Where Dongguan joins the river, its width is no more than several tens of paces. If the rebel plan succeeds and the great lake pours out, then all the Huainan garrisons will surely share the fate of Jinyang.
translations.idiomatic: The lake is over four hundred li in circuit, and where Dongguan meets the river it is only a few dozen paces wide. If the rebels succeed and the great lake pours out, all our Huainan garrisons will suffer the fate of Jinyang.

sentences.zh: 又吳楚便水，且灌且掠，淮南之地，將非國有。

translations.literal: Moreover, Wu and Chu are adept at water; flooding as they plunder, the lands of Huainan will no longer belong to the state.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, Wu and Chu are skilled in water warfare. If they flood while raiding, Huainan will no longer be ours.

sentences.zh: 壽陽去江五百餘里，眾庶惶惶，並懼水害。

translations.literal: Shouyang is more than five hundred li from the river, and the masses are anxious and afraid, all fearing the harm of water.
translations.idiomatic: Shouyang lies more than five hundred li from the river, and the people are terrified, all fearing flood damage.

sentences.zh: 脫乘民之願，攻敵之虛，豫勒諸州，纂集士馬，首秋大集，則南瀆可為飲馬之津，霍嶺必成徙倚之觀，事貴應機，經略須早。

translations.literal: If we take advantage of the people's wishes and attack the enemy's emptiness, prearrange the provinces, gather soldiers and horses, and assemble them at the beginning of autumn, then the southern channel may become a ford where we water horses, and Huo Ridge will surely become a lookout where we linger. Affairs value response to opportunity, and planning must be early.
translations.idiomatic: If we use the people's wishes, strike the enemy's weak point, prearrange the provinces, gather troops and horses, and assemble them in early autumn, then the southern channel can become a ford for watering our horses, and Huo Ridge a height from which we look out at ease. Opportunity must be answered, and planning must begin early.

sentences.zh: 縱混一不可必果，江西自是無虞。

translations.literal: Even if complete unification cannot be certainly achieved, the west of the Yangzi will naturally be without worry.
translations.idiomatic: Even if complete unification cannot be guaranteed, the lands west of the Yangzi will at least be secure.

sentences.zh: 若猶豫緩圖，不加除討，關塞既成，襄陵方及，平原民戍定為魚矣。」

translations.literal: If we still hesitate and slowly make plans, without adding removal and punishment, once the passes and barriers are completed and the waters reach the hills, the people and garrisons of the plains will certainly become fish."
translations.idiomatic: If we hesitate and delay instead of eliminating the threat, then once the barriers are finished and the waters rise to the hills, the people and garrisons of the plains will become fish."

sentences.zh: 詔發冀、定、瀛、相、并、濟六州二萬人，馬一千五百匹，令仲秋之中畢會淮南，并壽陽先兵三萬，委澄經略。

translations.literal: An edict mobilized twenty thousand men and one thousand five hundred horses from the six provinces of Ji, Ding, Ying, Xiang, Bing, and Ji, ordering them all to assemble in Huainan by mid-autumn; together with Shouyang's previous thirty thousand troops, they were entrusted to Cheng for planning.
translations.idiomatic: An edict mobilized twenty thousand men and fifteen hundred horses from Ji, Ding, Ying, Xiang, Bing, and Ji provinces, ordering them to assemble in Huainan by mid-autumn. Together with Shouyang's existing thirty thousand troops, they were placed under Cheng's command.

sentences.zh: 先是朝議有南伐之意，以蕭寶夤為東揚州刺史據東城，陳伯之為江州刺史戍陽石，以澄總督二鎮，授之節度。

translations.literal: Before this, the court deliberations had intended a southern campaign, appointing Xiao Baoyin Inspector of Eastern Yangzhou to occupy Dongcheng and Chen Bozhi Inspector of Jiangzhou to garrison Yangshi; Cheng was made commander-in-chief of the two garrisons and given authority over their commands.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, the court had planned a southern campaign, placing Xiao Baoyin at Dongcheng as Inspector of Eastern Yangzhou and Chen Bozhi at Yangshi as Inspector of Jiangzhou. Cheng was put in overall command of the two positions.

sentences.zh: 至是勒兵進討。

translations.literal: At this point he ordered the troops forward to attack.
translations.idiomatic: At this point he ordered the troops forward.

sentences.zh: 以東關水衝，大峴險要，東關縱水，陽石、合肥有急懸之切，不圖大峴，則歷陽有乘險之援，淮陵陸道，九山水路，並宜經略。

translations.literal: Because Dongguan was the water choke point and Daxian was a strategic pass, if Dongguan released water, Yangshi and Hefei would face an urgent suspended danger; if Daxian was not planned for, then Liyang would have support by using the pass. The land route through Huailing and the water route through Jiushan both had to be planned for.
translations.idiomatic: Dongguan controlled the water flow, and Daxian was a crucial pass. If Dongguan released the water, Yangshi and Hefei would be in immediate danger; if Daxian was ignored, Liyang could use the pass as support. The Huailing land route and the Jiushan water route both had to be included in the plan.

sentences.zh: 於是遣統軍傅豎眼、王神念等進次大峴、東關、九山、淮陵，皆分部諸將，倍道據之，總勒大眾，絡繹相接。

translations.literal: Thereupon he sent Commanders Fu Shuyan, Wang Shennian, and others to advance and camp at Daxian, Dongguan, Jiushan, and Huailing. All divided the generals by sections, marched by double stages to occupy them, and brought the great host under command, one unit after another in continuous connection.
translations.idiomatic: He therefore sent Fu Shuyan, Wang Shennian, and other commanders to advance to Daxian, Dongguan, Jiushan, and Huailing. The generals divided the sectors, hurried to occupy them, and linked the main forces in a continuous line.

sentences.zh: 而神念克其關要、潁川二城，斬衍軍主費尼。

translations.literal: Shennian captured the two cities of Guanyao and Yingchuan and beheaded Xiao Yan's army commander Fei Ni.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Shennian captured Guanyao and Yingchuan and beheaded Fei Ni, one of Xiao Yan's commanders.

sentences.zh: 而寧朔將軍韋惠、龍驤將軍李伯由仍固大峴。

translations.literal: Ning Shuo General Wei Hui and Longxiang General Li Boyou still firmly held Daxian.
translations.idiomatic: Ning Shuo General Wei Hui and Longxiang General Li Boyou were still holding Daxian.

sentences.zh: 澄遣統軍党法宗、傅豎眼等進軍克之，遂圍白塔、牽城，數日之間，便即逃潰。

translations.literal: Cheng sent Commanders Dang Fazong, Fu Shuyan, and others to advance their armies and take it. They then surrounded Baita and Qiancheng, and within several days these immediately fled and collapsed.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng sent Dang Fazong, Fu Shuyan, and other commanders forward to take it. They then besieged Baita and Qiancheng, which fled and collapsed within a few days.

sentences.zh: 衍清溪戍望風散走。

translations.literal: Xiao Yan's Qingxi Garrison scattered and fled at the sight of their momentum.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Yan's Qingxi Garrison scattered at the news.

sentences.zh: 衍徐州刺史司馬明素率眾三千，欲援九山；

translations.literal: Xiao Yan's Inspector of Xuzhou Sima Mingsu led three thousand men, wishing to reinforce Jiushan;
translations.idiomatic: Sima Mingsu, Xiao Yan's Inspector of Xuzhou, led three thousand men to reinforce Jiushan;

sentences.zh: 徐州長史潘伯隣規固淮陵；

translations.literal: Pan Bolin, Chief Clerk of Xuzhou, planned to hold Huailing;
translations.idiomatic: Pan Bolin, Chief Clerk of Xuzhou, planned to hold Huailing;

sentences.zh: 寧朔將軍王燮負險焦城。

translations.literal: Ning Shuo General Wang Xie relied on the defenses of Jiaocheng.
translations.idiomatic: and Ning Shuo General Wang Xie relied on the strong position at Jiaocheng.

sentences.zh: 法宗進克焦城，破淮陵，擒明素，斬伯隣。

translations.literal: Fazong advanced, captured Jiaocheng, broke Huailing, captured Mingsu, and beheaded Bolin.
translations.idiomatic: Dang Fazong advanced, captured Jiaocheng, broke Huailing, captured Mingsu, and beheaded Bolin.

sentences.zh: 其濟陰太守王厚強、廬江太守裴邃即亦奔退。

translations.literal: Their Governor of Jiyin Wang Houqiang and Governor of Lujiang Pei Sui then also fled in retreat.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Houqiang, their Governor of Jiyin, and Pei Sui, Governor of Lujiang, also fled.

sentences.zh: 詔澄曰：「將軍文德內昭，武功外暢，奮揚大略，將蕩江吳。

translations.literal: The edict to Cheng said, "General, your civil virtue shines within and your military achievement spreads without; you raise and display grand strategy and are about to sweep away Jiang and Wu.
translations.idiomatic: The edict to Cheng said, "General, your civil virtue shines within and your military achievements resound abroad. You have displayed a grand strategy and are about to sweep away Jiang and Wu.

sentences.zh: 長旌始舒，賊徒懾氣，銳旅方馳，東關席卷。

translations.literal: When the long banners first unfurled, the rebel followers lost heart; as the sharp troops were only beginning to race forward, Dongguan was swept up like a mat.
translations.idiomatic: As soon as the long banners were unfurled, the rebels lost heart; as the elite troops began to advance, Dongguan was rolled up like a mat.

sentences.zh: 想江湖弭波，在旦夕耳。

translations.literal: I expect the rivers and lakes will calm their waves in the space of morning and evening.
translations.idiomatic: I expect the rivers and lakes to be pacified very soon.

sentences.zh: 所送首虜，並已聞之。」

translations.literal: The heads and captives you sent have all been reported."
translations.idiomatic: The heads and captives you sent have all been reported."

sentences.zh: 初，澄出討之後，衍將姜慶真襲據壽春外郭，齊王蕭寶夤擊走之。

translations.literal: At first, after Cheng went out to attack, Xiao Yan's general Jiang Qingzhen attacked and occupied the outer wall of Shouchun, and Xiao Baoyin, Prince of Qi, attacked and drove him off.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, after Cheng had marched out, Xiao Yan's general Jiang Qingzhen attacked and occupied the outer wall of Shouchun, but Xiao Baoyin, Prince of Qi, attacked and drove him away.

sentences.zh: 長史韋纘坐免官，澄以在外無坐。

translations.literal: Chief Clerk Wei Zuan was dismissed from office for the offense, while Cheng, because he was away, was not implicated.
translations.idiomatic: Chief Clerk Wei Zuan was dismissed for this, while Cheng was not held responsible because he was away.

sentences.zh: 遂攻鍾離。

translations.literal: He then attacked Zhongli.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng then attacked Zhongli.

sentences.zh: 又詔：「鍾離若食盡，三月已前，固有可克，如至四月，淮水泛長，舟行無礙，宜善量之。

translations.literal: Another edict said, "If Zhongli exhausts its food, before the third month it can certainly be taken; if it reaches the fourth month, the Huai waters will rise and swell, and boats will move without obstruction. You should measure this well.
translations.idiomatic: Another edict said, "If Zhongli runs out of food, it can surely be taken before the third month; but if matters reach the fourth month, the Huai will rise and boats will pass freely. Weigh this carefully.

sentences.zh: 前事捷也，此實將軍經略，勳有常焉。

translations.literal: The previous success was truly the result of your planning, General, and the merit has its constant place.
translations.idiomatic: The earlier victory was truly due to your planning, General, and that merit stands secure.

sentences.zh: 如或以水盛難圖，亦可為萬全之計，不宜昧利無成，以貽後悔也。」

translations.literal: If perhaps the high water makes it difficult to plan, you may also make a plan of complete safety. It is not fitting to be blinded by advantage, achieve nothing, and leave later regret."
translations.idiomatic: If high water makes the objective difficult, you may choose a safer plan. Do not be blinded by advantage, fail to achieve the goal, and leave regret for later."

sentences.zh: 蕭衍冠軍將軍張惠紹，游擊將軍殷暹、驍騎將軍趙景悅、龍驤將軍張景仁等率眾五千，送糧鍾離。

translations.literal: Xiao Yan's General Who Conquers Champions Zhang Huishao, General of Mobile Assault Yin Xian, General of Valiant Cavalry Zhao Jingyue, Longxiang General Zhang Jingren, and others led five thousand men to send grain to Zhongli.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Yan's generals Zhang Huishao, Yin Xian, Zhao Jingyue, Zhang Jingren, and others led five thousand men escorting grain to Zhongli.

sentences.zh: 澄遣統軍王足、劉思祖等邀擊惠紹等，大破之。

translations.literal: Cheng sent Commanders Wang Zu, Liu Sizu, and others to intercept and strike Huishao and the others, greatly defeating them.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng sent Wang Zu, Liu Sizu, and other commanders to intercept Huishao and his men, defeating them badly.

sentences.zh: 獲惠紹、殷暹、景仁及其屯騎校尉史文淵等軍主以上二十七人。

translations.literal: They captured Huishao, Yin Xian, Jingren, and Shi Wenyuan, their Colonel of Garrison Cavalry, along with twenty-seven men of army commander rank and above.
translations.idiomatic: They captured Huishao, Yin Xian, Jingren, Shi Wenyuan, their Colonel of Garrison Cavalry, and twenty-seven officers of army commander rank or higher.

sentences.zh: 既而遇雨，淮水暴長，引歸壽春。

translations.literal: Afterward, they met with rain, the Huai waters suddenly rose, and he withdrew back to Shouchun.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward rain came, the Huai rose sharply, and Cheng withdrew to Shouchun.

sentences.zh: 還既狼狽，失兵四千餘人。

translations.literal: Once the return had become disorderly, he lost more than four thousand soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: The retreat became disordered, and he lost more than four thousand men.

sentences.zh: 頻表解州，世宗不許。

translations.literal: He repeatedly memorialized asking to be relieved of his province, but Shizong did not permit it.
translations.idiomatic: He repeatedly memorialized asking to be relieved of his province, but Shizong refused.

sentences.zh: 有司奏軍還失路，奪其開府，又降三階。

translations.literal: The responsible offices memorialized that the army had lost the road on its return; his open office was taken away, and he was further lowered three ranks.
translations.idiomatic: The officials memorialized that the returning army had lost its route; Cheng was stripped of his open office and demoted three ranks.

sentences.zh: 時蕭衍有移，求換張惠紹。

translations.literal: At the time Xiao Yan had sent an official letter requesting an exchange for Zhang Huishao.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Xiao Yan sent a letter requesting an exchange for Zhang Huishao.

sentences.zh: 澄表請不許，詔付八座會議。

translations.literal: Cheng memorialized requesting that this not be permitted, and an edict referred it to the Eight Seats for joint discussion.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng memorialized that the request should not be allowed, and the edict referred it to the Eight Seats for conference.

sentences.zh: 尚書令、廣陽王嘉等奏宜還之，詔乃聽還。

translations.literal: Director of the Department of State Affairs Jia, Prince of Guangyang, and others memorialized that he should be returned, and the edict then permitted the return.
translations.idiomatic: Jia, Prince of Guangyang and Director of the Department of State Affairs, and others memorialized that Zhang Huishao should be returned, and the edict allowed it.

sentences.zh: 後果復寇邊。

translations.literal: Later, as expected, he again raided the border.
translations.idiomatic: Later, as expected, he raided the border again.

sentences.zh: 轉澄鎮北大將軍、定州刺史。

translations.literal: Cheng was transferred to Grand General Who Guards the North and Inspector of Dingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng was transferred to Grand General Who Guards the North and Inspector of Dingzhou.

sentences.zh: 初，民中每有橫調，百姓煩苦，前後牧守，未能蠲除，澄多所省減，民以忻賴。

translations.literal: At first, whenever there were arbitrary levies among the people, the common people were troubled and suffering. The governors and administrators before and after him had not been able to remove them, but Cheng reduced many of them, and the people joyfully relied on him.
translations.idiomatic: The people had long suffered from arbitrary levies, which previous governors and administrators had failed to abolish. Cheng reduced many of them, and the people rejoiced and relied on him.

sentences.zh: 又明黜陟賞罰之法，表減公園之地，以給無業貧口，禁造布絹不任衣者。

translations.literal: He also clarified the laws of demotion and promotion, reward and punishment, memorialized to reduce the land of public parks in order to give it to poor households without occupations, and prohibited the making of cloth and silk not fit for clothing.
translations.idiomatic: He also clarified rules for promotion, demotion, reward, and punishment; memorialized to reduce public parkland and give it to poor households without livelihoods; and banned the production of cloth and silk unfit for clothing.

sentences.zh: 母孟太妃薨，居喪毀瘠，當世稱之。

translations.literal: When his mother, Grand Consort Meng, died, his mourning left him wasted and thin, and the age praised him.
translations.idiomatic: When his mother, Grand Consort Meng, died, he wasted away in mourning, and his contemporaries praised him for it.

sentences.zh: 服闋，除太子太保。

translations.literal: When the mourning period was complete, he was appointed Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: After the mourning period ended, he was appointed Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 於時高肇當朝，猜忌賢戚。

translations.literal: At that time Gao Zhao controlled the court and was suspicious and jealous of worthy imperial relatives.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Gao Zhao controlled the court and was suspicious of worthy imperial relatives.

sentences.zh: 澄為肇間構，常恐不全，乃終日昏飲，以示荒敗。

translations.literal: Cheng was estranged and framed by Zhao, and constantly feared he would not be preserved; he therefore drank muddily all day to show ruin and failure.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng was slandered and isolated by Gao Zhao and constantly feared for his life, so he drank heavily all day to appear ruined and useless.

sentences.zh: 所作詭越，時謂為狂。

translations.literal: The strange and excessive things he did were called madness at the time.
translations.idiomatic: His strange, excessive behavior was taken at the time for madness.

sentences.zh: 世宗夜崩，時事倉卒，高肇擁兵於外，肅宗沖幼，朝野不安。

translations.literal: Shizong died at night, events were urgent and confused, Gao Zhao held troops outside, Suzong was young, and court and countryside were unsettled.
translations.idiomatic: When Shizong died at night, events were sudden and confused. Gao Zhao held troops outside, Suzong was still a child, and both court and countryside were uneasy.

sentences.zh: 澄疏斥不預機要，而朝望所屬，領軍于忠、侍中崔光等奏澄為尚書令，於是眾心忻服。

translations.literal: Cheng had been distantly rejected and did not take part in the essentials of policy, yet the hopes of the court rested on him. Commander of the Guards Yu Zhong, Palace Attendant Cui Guang, and others memorialized that Cheng be made Director of the Department of State Affairs, and at this the hearts of the multitude joyfully submitted.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng had been kept at a distance and excluded from confidential affairs, but the court's hopes rested on him. Yu Zhong, Commander of the Guards, Cui Guang, Palace Attendant, and others memorialized that Cheng be made Director of the Department of State Affairs, and everyone gladly accepted this.

sentences.zh: 又加散騎常侍、驃騎大將軍，尋遷司空，加侍中，俄詔領尚書令。

translations.literal: He was also made Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary and Grand General of Agile Cavalry; soon he was transferred to Minister of Works and given the added title Palace Attendant, and shortly afterward an edict had him concurrently direct the Department of State Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He was also made Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary and Grand General of Agile Cavalry; soon he was promoted to Minister of Works with the added title Palace Attendant, and shortly afterward was ordered to concurrently direct the Department of State Affairs.

sentences.zh: 初，正始之末，詔百司普昇一級，而執事者不達旨意，刺史、守、令限而不及。

translations.literal: Earlier, at the end of the Zhengshi era, an edict had raised all the offices by one grade, but those handling the matter did not understand the intent, so inspectors, governors, and magistrates were limited and did not receive it.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, at the end of the Zhengshi era, an edict raised all offices by one grade, but the officials implementing it misunderstood the intent, so inspectors, governors, and magistrates were excluded.

sentences.zh: 澄奏曰：「竊惟雲構鬱起，澤及百司，企春望榮，內外同慶。

translations.literal: Cheng memorialized, "I privately consider that the cloud-built grace rose richly and its favor reached the hundred offices; looking toward spring and hoping for glory, inner and outer officials celebrated together.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng memorialized, "I humbly think that when imperial favor rose like gathering clouds and reached the hundred offices, officials inside and outside the court looked toward renewed honor and rejoiced together.

sentences.zh: 至於賞陟，不及守宰，爾來十年，冤訟不絕。

translations.literal: But when it came to rewarding advancement, it did not reach governors and magistrates, and for ten years since then grievances and lawsuits have not ceased.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the promotion did not reach governors and magistrates, and for ten years grievances and appeals have continued without end.

sentences.zh: 封回自鎮遠、安州入為太尉長史，元匡自征虜、恒州入作宗卿，二人遷授，並在先詔。

translations.literal: Feng Hui entered from General Who Guards Afar and Anzhou to become Chief Clerk to the Grand Commandant; Yuan Kuang entered from General Who Conquers Caitiffs and Hengzhou to become Chamberlain for the Imperial Clan. The promotions and appointments of these two men were both before the earlier edict.
translations.idiomatic: Feng Hui came in from Zhenyuan General and Anzhou to serve as Chief Clerk to the Grand Commandant, while Yuan Kuang came in from Zhenglu General and Hengzhou to serve as Chamberlain for the Imperial Clan. Both appointments occurred before the earlier edict.

sentences.zh: 應蒙之理，備在於斯。

translations.literal: The principle that they should receive the benefit is fully present in these cases.
translations.idiomatic: These cases fully show the principle by which they should receive the benefit.

sentences.zh: 兼州佐停私之徒，陪臣郡丞之例，尚蒙天澤下降，榮及當時。

translations.literal: In addition, provincial assistants, those who had suspended private service, subordinate ministers, and commandery deputies still received the descent of heavenly favor, and the honor reached them at the time.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, provincial assistants, private retainers who had ceased service, subordinate officers, and commandery deputies all received the court's favor and shared in the honor at the time.

sentences.zh: 然參佐之來，皆因府主，今府主不霑，佐官獨預，棄本賞末，愚謂未允。

translations.literal: Yet assistants come in all because of their office heads. Now the office heads do not receive the favor, while assistant officials alone participate; abandoning the root and rewarding the branch, in my foolish opinion, is not fair.
translations.idiomatic: But assistants come forward through their chiefs. For the chiefs to receive nothing while their subordinates alone benefit abandons the root and rewards the branch; in my foolish view this is not just.

sentences.zh: 今計刺史、守、宰之官，請準回匡，悉同汎限，上允初旨百司之章，下覆訟者元元之心。」

translations.literal: Now, calculating the offices of inspectors, governors, and magistrates, I request that they be modeled on Hui and Kuang and all be included within the general limit, above fulfilling the original edict's phrase "the hundred offices," and below answering the hearts of the common people who have appealed."
translations.idiomatic: I therefore ask that inspectors, governors, and magistrates be treated according to the precedents of Feng Hui and Yuan Kuang and included within the general scope, above fulfilling the original edict's words about the hundred offices, and below satisfying the hearts of the people who have appealed."

sentences.zh: 詔曰：「自今已後，內外之事，嘗經先朝者，不得重聞。」

translations.literal: The edict said, "From now on, matters inside and outside the court that once passed through the former reign may not be reported again."
translations.idiomatic: The edict said, "From now on, internal and external matters already handled under the former reign may not be reported again."

sentences.zh: 澄奏曰：「臣聞堯懸諫諍之鼓，舜置誹謗之木，皆所以廣耳目於芻蕘，達四聰於天下。

translations.literal: Cheng memorialized, "I have heard that Yao hung the drum for remonstrance and Shun set up the wood for criticism; both were means to broaden ears and eyes among woodcutters and herdsmen and make the fourfold hearing reach all under Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng memorialized, "I have heard that Yao hung up the remonstrance drum and Shun set up the criticism post, both to widen their hearing and sight among even the humblest people and let the ruler's fourfold hearing reach all under Heaven.

sentences.zh: 伏惟太祖開基，化隆自遠，累聖相承，於今九帝。

translations.literal: I bow and consider that Taizu opened the foundation and his transformation flourished from afar; successive sages have inherited one another, now reaching nine emperors.
translations.idiomatic: Taizu founded the dynasty and his transforming rule spread far. Sage rulers have succeeded one another, down to the ninth emperor today.

sentences.zh: 重光疊照，汚隆必同，與奪隨時，道無恒體。

translations.literal: Repeated radiance and layered illumination, decline and flourishing must all be the same; granting and taking follow the time, and the Way has no constant form.
translations.idiomatic: Their radiance has shone one after another; whether in decline or flourishing, the principle is the same. Granting and withholding follow the times, and the Way has no fixed form.

sentences.zh: 思過如渴，言重千金，故稱無諱之朝，邁蹤三、五。

translations.literal: They thirsted to think on faults and valued words at a thousand in gold; therefore ours was called a court without taboos, surpassing the tracks of the Three and Five.
translations.idiomatic: They thirsted for reflection on their faults and valued speech at a thousand pieces of gold; thus ours was called a court without taboos, surpassing the Three Sovereigns and Five Emperors.

sentences.zh: 高祖沖年纂曆，文明協統，變官易律，未為違典。

translations.literal: Gaozu succeeded to the calendar at a tender age, and Wenming cooperated in rule; they changed offices and altered laws, but this did not violate the classics.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu inherited the throne while young, and Empress Wenming assisted the government. They changed offices and laws, yet did not violate classical norms.

sentences.zh: 及慈聖臨朝，母儀宇縣，爰發慈令，垂心滯獄，深枉者仰日月於九泉，微屈者希曲照於盆下。

translations.literal: When the Compassionate Sage held court, her maternal model covered the realm; she then issued compassionate orders and set her heart on delayed lawsuits, so those deeply wronged looked up to the sun and moon from the Nine Springs, and those slightly aggrieved hoped for a bent light beneath the overturned basin.
translations.idiomatic: When the Compassionate Sage held court, her maternal example covered the realm. She issued merciful orders and attended to stalled cases, so the deeply wronged looked up to sun and moon even from the Nine Springs, and the slightly aggrieved hoped for a slant of light beneath the overturned basin.

sentences.zh: 今乃格以先朝，限以一例，斯誠奉遵之本心，實乖元元之至望。

translations.literal: Now to bar them by saying "the former reign" and limit them by a single rule truly follows the root intention of obedience, but in fact goes against the utmost hopes of the common people.
translations.idiomatic: Now to block such cases as belonging to the former reign and limit them by one rule may be meant as obedience, but it truly violates the people's deepest hopes.

sentences.zh: 在于謙挹，有乖舊典。

translations.literal: In humility and yielding, it departs from the old institutions.
translations.idiomatic: As a matter of humble receptiveness, it also departs from the old institutions.

sentences.zh: 謹尋抱枉求直，或經累朝。

translations.literal: I have carefully examined those who hold grievances and seek straightening; some have passed through several reigns.
translations.idiomatic: I have examined those who carry grievances and seek justice; some cases have lasted through several reigns.

sentences.zh: 毫釐之差，正之宜速；

translations.literal: A difference of a hair or a li should be corrected quickly;
translations.idiomatic: A difference of a hair's breadth should be corrected quickly;

sentences.zh: 謬若千里，駟馬弗追。

translations.literal: if the error is like a thousand li, even a team of four horses cannot catch it.
translations.idiomatic: if an error becomes a thousand li, even a four-horse team cannot catch it.

sentences.zh: 故禮有損益，事有可否，父有諍子，君有諫臣，琴瑟不調，理宜改作。

translations.literal: Therefore ritual has diminutions and additions, affairs have what may and may not be done, fathers have sons who contest them, and rulers have ministers who remonstrate with them. If zithers and lutes are not in tune, principle says they should be adjusted.
translations.idiomatic: Thus ritual can be reduced or augmented, affairs can be approved or rejected, fathers have sons who argue with them, and rulers have ministers who remonstrate. If zithers and lutes are out of tune, they should be adjusted.

sentences.zh: 是以防川之論，小決則通；

translations.literal: Thus in the argument about blocking rivers, a small opening lets them flow;
translations.idiomatic: Thus, in the argument over blocking rivers, a small opening lets them flow;

sentences.zh: 鄉校之言，擁則敗國。

translations.literal: as for speech in the village schools, if it is blocked, it ruins the state.
translations.idiomatic: and as for speech in the village schools, blocking it ruins the state.

sentences.zh: 矧伊陳屈，而可抑以先朝。

translations.literal: How much more when they are setting forth grievances: how can they be suppressed by saying "the former reign"?
translations.idiomatic: How much more when people are presenting grievances: how can they be suppressed merely because they concern a former reign?

sentences.zh: 且先朝屈者，非故屈之，或有司愛憎，或執事濁僻，空文致法，以誤視聽。

translations.literal: Moreover, those wronged under the former reign were not intentionally wronged. Sometimes there was love or hatred by the offices, sometimes murky partiality among those handling matters, and empty documents brought about law, thereby misleading hearing and sight.
translations.idiomatic: Those wronged under the former reign were not wronged deliberately by the throne. Sometimes officials were moved by favoritism or hatred, sometimes clerks were corrupt and biased, and empty paperwork produced legal judgments that misled the court.

sentences.zh: 如此冤塞，彌在可哀。

translations.literal: Such blocked grievances are all the more worthy of pity.
translations.idiomatic: Such obstructed grievances are all the more pitiful.

sentences.zh: 僭之與濫，寧失不經，乞收今旨，還依前詔。」

translations.literal: As for overstepping and excess, I would rather err on the side of irregularity; I beg that the present order be withdrawn and that we return to following the previous edict."
translations.idiomatic: If there is risk of excess, I would rather err on the side of irregular openness. I beg that the present order be withdrawn and that we return to the previous edict."

sentences.zh: 詔曰：「省奏，深體毗贊之情，三皇異軌，五代殊風，一時之制，何必詮改。

translations.literal: The edict said, "I have reviewed the memorial and deeply understand the feeling of assisting and supporting. The Three Sovereigns had different tracks and the Five Ages different customs; why must the institutions of one time all be weighed and changed?
translations.idiomatic: The edict said, "I have reviewed the memorial and deeply understand your wish to assist the throne. The Three Sovereigns followed different paths and the Five Ages different customs; why must the institutions of one period all be revised?

sentences.zh: 必謂虛文設旨，理在可申者，何容不同來執。

translations.literal: If it is necessarily said that empty texts set forth intentions and that the principle lies in what can be extended, how could we allow them not all to come and be taken up alike?
translations.idiomatic: If one says that formal texts merely express an intention and that the principle may be extended, then how could similar cases not all come forward to be taken up?

sentences.zh: 可依往制。」

translations.literal: It may follow the former system."
translations.idiomatic: Let the former system be followed."

sentences.zh: 澄表上皇誥宗制并訓詁各一卷，意欲皇太后覽之，思勸戒之益。

translations.literal: Cheng submitted one fascicle each of Imperial Admonitions, Clan Regulations, and Explanatory Glosses, intending that the Empress Dowager read them and consider their benefit for exhortation and warning.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng submitted one fascicle each of Imperial Admonitions, Clan Regulations, and Explanatory Glosses, hoping the Empress Dowager would read them and consider their value for admonition.

sentences.zh: 又奏利國濟民所宜振舉者十條。

translations.literal: He also memorialized ten articles on what should be revived and promoted to benefit the state and aid the people.
translations.idiomatic: He also submitted ten recommendations for measures that should be revived to benefit the state and aid the people.

sentences.zh: 一曰律度量衡，公私不同，所宜一之。

translations.literal: The first said: laws, measures, weights, and balances differ between public and private use; they should be unified.
translations.idiomatic: First: statutes, measures, weights, and balances differ between public and private use and should be unified.

sentences.zh: 二曰宜興學校，以明黜陟之法。

translations.literal: The second said: schools should be promoted in order to clarify the law of demotion and promotion.
translations.idiomatic: Second: schools should be promoted to clarify the rules for demotion and promotion.

sentences.zh: 三曰宜興滅繼絕，各舉所知。

translations.literal: The third said: what has perished should be revived and extinct lines continued, and each should recommend those he knows.
translations.idiomatic: Third: fallen lines should be revived and extinct lines continued, with each official recommending those he knows.

sentences.zh: 四曰五調之外，一不煩民，任民之力，不過三日。

translations.literal: The fourth said: beyond the five levies, the people should not be troubled at all, and use of the people's labor should not exceed three days.
translations.idiomatic: Fourth: beyond the five regular levies, the people should not be burdened, and labor service should not exceed three days.

sentences.zh: 五曰臨民之官，皆須黜陟，以旌賞罰。

translations.literal: The fifth said: officials who govern the people must all be demoted or promoted in order to make rewards and punishments clear.
translations.idiomatic: Fifth: officials who govern the people must be subject to promotion and demotion, so that reward and punishment are clear.

sentences.zh: 六曰逃亡代輸，去來年久者，若非伎作，任聽即住。

translations.literal: The sixth said: for fugitives whose dues are paid by substitutes, and whose coming and going has lasted many years, if they are not artisans, they should be freely allowed to settle where they are.
translations.idiomatic: Sixth: fugitives whose obligations are being paid by substitutes, and whose absence or return has lasted for years, should be allowed to settle where they are, unless they are registered artisans.

sentences.zh: 七曰邊兵逃走，或實陷沒，皆須精檢；

translations.literal: The seventh said: border soldiers who flee, or who in fact have fallen or been lost, must all be carefully examined;
translations.idiomatic: Seventh: cases of border soldiers who flee, or who have truly been captured or killed, must be carefully investigated;

sentences.zh: 三長及近親，若實隱之，徵其代輸，不隱勿論。

translations.literal: if the three chiefs and close kin have truly concealed it, collect substitute payments from them; if they did not conceal it, do not prosecute them.
translations.idiomatic: if the three chiefs or close relatives truly concealed the facts, collect the substitute payments from them; if they did not conceal them, do not prosecute.

sentences.zh: 八曰工商世業之戶，復徵租調，無以堪濟，今請免之，使專其業。

translations.literal: The eighth said: households whose hereditary occupations are crafts and commerce are again being charged rents and levies and have no means to endure and meet them. I now request that they be exempted, so that they may specialize in their occupations.
translations.idiomatic: Eighth: hereditary artisan and merchant households are again being charged rents and levies beyond what they can bear. I request that they be exempted so they can concentrate on their work.

sentences.zh: 九曰三長禁姦，不得隔越相領，戶不滿者，隨近并合。

translations.literal: The ninth said: the three chiefs, in preventing wrongdoing, may not cross boundaries to command one another; where households are insufficient, they should be merged with nearby units.
translations.idiomatic: Ninth: the three chiefs, in suppressing crime, should not command across boundaries; where there are too few households, they should be merged with nearby units.

sentences.zh: 十曰羽林虎賁，邊方有事，暫可赴戰，常戍宜遣蕃兵代之。

translations.literal: The tenth said: the Yulin and Huben guards may temporarily go to war when there are affairs on the frontier, but for regular garrison duty tribal troops should be sent to replace them.
translations.idiomatic: Tenth: the Yulin and Huben guards may be sent temporarily to fight when there is trouble on the frontier, but regular garrison duty should be assigned to tribal troops in their place.

sentences.zh: 靈太后下其奏，百僚議之，事有同否。

translations.literal: Empress Dowager Ling sent down his memorial for the hundred officials to discuss, and in the matters there were agreements and disagreements.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Dowager Ling sent his memorial down for discussion by the officials, who agreed on some points and disagreed on others.

sentences.zh: 時四中郎將兵數寡弱，不足以襟帶京師，澄奏宜以東中帶滎陽郡，南中帶魯陽郡，西中帶恒農郡，北中帶河內郡，選二品、三品親賢兼稱者居之，省非急之作，配以強兵，如此則深根固本、強幹弱枝之義也。

translations.literal: At the time the troops of the four Gentlemen Generals of the Center were few and weak, insufficient to belt and protect the capital. Cheng memorialized that the Eastern Center should take in Yingyang Commandery, the Southern Center Luyang Commandery, the Western Center Hengnong Commandery, and the Northern Center Henei Commandery; that men of the second and third ranks who were close, worthy, and qualified should be selected to occupy them; that nonurgent works should be eliminated; and that strong troops should be assigned. In this way, he said, lay the meaning of deepening the roots and strengthening the foundation, strengthening the trunk and weakening the branches.
translations.idiomatic: At the time the four Central Gentleman-General commands had too few weak troops to protect the capital. Cheng proposed that the Eastern Center be linked with Yingyang Commandery, the Southern Center with Luyang, the Western Center with Hengnong, and the Northern Center with Henei; that qualified close and worthy men of the second and third ranks be chosen to hold them; that nonurgent works be reduced; and that strong troops be assigned. This, he said, would deepen the roots, strengthen the base, strengthen the trunk, and weaken the branches.

sentences.zh: 靈太后初將從之，後議者不同，乃止。

translations.literal: Empress Dowager Ling at first was about to follow this, but later the discussants disagreed, and so it was stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Dowager Ling initially intended to follow the proposal, but later the discussants disagreed, so it was dropped.

sentences.zh: 澄又重奏曰：「固本宜強，防微在豫，故雖有文事，不忘武功。

translations.literal: Cheng again memorialized, "To secure the root it should be strengthened, and prevention of the slight lies in preparation; therefore, even when there are civil affairs, military achievement is not forgotten.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng memorialized again, "To secure the root, it must be strengthened; to guard against small dangers, one must prepare in advance. Thus even in civil affairs, military power is not forgotten.

sentences.zh: 況今南蠻仍獷，北妖頻結，來事難圖，勢同往變。

translations.literal: How much more now, when the southern Man remain fierce and the northern demons repeatedly form alliances; future events are difficult to plan for, and the situation is the same as past disturbances.
translations.idiomatic: How much more now, when the southern Man remain fierce and northern enemies repeatedly combine. Future events are hard to foresee, and the situation resembles past upheavals.

sentences.zh: 脫暴勃忽起，振動關畿，四府羸卒，何以防擬。

translations.literal: If sudden violence abruptly arises and shakes the passes and capital region, with the weak soldiers of the four offices, how will we defend and prepare?
translations.idiomatic: If a sudden uprising breaks out and shakes the passes and capital region, how can the weak troops of the four offices defend against it?

sentences.zh: 平康之世，可以寄安，遺之久長，恐非善策。

translations.literal: In an age of peace and health, we may entrust ourselves to security, but to leave it so for a long time, I fear, is not a good plan.
translations.idiomatic: In peaceful times one may rely on security, but to leave matters this way for long is not good policy.

sentences.zh: 如臣愚見，郎將領兵，兼總民職，省官實祿，於是乎在。

translations.literal: In my foolish view, that the Gentleman Generals command troops while also overseeing civil duties, and that offices be reduced while real salaries remain, lies precisely here.
translations.idiomatic: In my foolish view, the Gentleman Generals should command troops while also overseeing civil duties; this is where offices can be reduced while real salaries are preserved.

sentences.zh: 求還依前增兵益號，將位既重，則念報亦深，軍郡相依，則表裏俱濟，朝廷無四顧之憂，姦宄絕窺覦之望矣。」

translations.literal: I ask that we return to the former system of increasing troops and augmenting titles. Once the generals' positions are weighty, their thought of repaying the state will also be deep; when army and commandery rely on each other, inside and outside will both be aided, the court will have no worries on four sides, and criminals will lose any hope of peering in."
translations.idiomatic: I ask that we return to the earlier plan of increasing troops and strengthening the titles. If the generals' posts are weighty, their sense of obligation will deepen; if army and commandery depend on one another, inner and outer defenses will both be supplied. The court will have no worries on any side, and criminals will lose hope of taking advantage."

sentences.zh: 卒不納。

translations.literal: In the end it was not accepted.
translations.idiomatic: In the end the proposal was not accepted.

sentences.zh: 又以流人初至遠鎮，衣食無資，多有死者，奏并其妻子給糧一歲，從之。

translations.literal: He also, because exiles newly arrived at distant garrisons had no resources for clothing and food and many died, memorialized that they, together with their wives and children, be given grain for one year, and this was followed.
translations.idiomatic: He also noted that exiles newly sent to distant garrisons lacked clothing and food and often died, so he memorialized that they and their families be given a year's grain. This was approved.

sentences.zh: 尋以疾患，求解任，不許。

translations.literal: Soon, because of illness, he requested to be relieved of office, but it was not permitted.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he asked to be relieved because of illness, but this was not allowed.

sentences.zh: 蕭衍於浮山斷淮為堰，以灌壽春，乃除使持節、大將軍、大都督、南討諸軍事，勒眾十萬，將出彭宋，尋淮堰自壞，不行。

translations.literal: When Xiao Yan, at Fushan, cut off the Huai to make a dam in order to flood Shouchun, Cheng was appointed Bearer of the Staff, Grand General, Grand Commander of all armies for the southern campaign, and ordered to command one hundred thousand men and prepare to go out through Peng and Song. Soon the Huai dam broke by itself, and he did not proceed.
translations.idiomatic: When Xiao Yan dammed the Huai at Fushan to flood Shouchun, Cheng was appointed Bearer of the Staff, Grand General, and Grand Commander of the southern campaign armies, with orders to lead one hundred thousand men out through Peng and Song. Soon the Huai dam collapsed on its own, and the campaign did not proceed.

sentences.zh: 澄以北邊鎮將選舉彌輕，恐賊虜闚邊，山陵危迫，奏求重鎮將之選，修警備之嚴，詔不從。

translations.literal: Because Cheng considered the selection of commanders for the northern frontier garrisons increasingly slight, and feared that rebel captives would peer at the border and the imperial tombs would be endangered, he memorialized requesting that selection of garrison commanders be made weightier and the strictness of warning and defense be repaired, but the edict did not follow it.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng believed that commanders for the northern frontier garrisons were being chosen too lightly. Fearing that raiders would threaten the border and endanger the imperial tombs, he memorialized asking that garrison commanders be selected more carefully and defenses tightened, but the edict did not accept this.

sentences.zh: 賊虜入寇，至於舊都，鎮將多非其人，所在叛亂，犯逼山陵，如澄所慮。

translations.literal: When rebel captives entered and raided, reaching the old capital, many garrison commanders were not the right men, rebellions broke out everywhere, and they violated and pressed upon the imperial tombs, just as Cheng had feared.
translations.idiomatic: When the raiders entered and reached the old capital, many garrison commanders proved unfit, rebellions broke out in many places, and the imperial tombs were threatened, exactly as Cheng had feared.

sentences.zh: 澄奏都城府寺猶未周悉，今軍旅初寧，無宜發眾，請取諸職人及司州郡縣犯十杖已上百鞭已下收贖之物，絹一匹，輸磚二百，以漸修造。

translations.literal: Cheng memorialized that the offices and temples of the capital city were still not complete; now that military affairs had just become quiet, it was not fitting to mobilize the masses. He requested that they take from various office workers and from the ransom goods paid for offenses in Sizhou commanderies and counties punishable by ten strokes or more and one hundred lashes or less: for one bolt of silk, two hundred bricks should be delivered, gradually to carry out construction.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng memorialized that the capital's offices and temples were still incomplete, but since the armies had only just settled, the people should not be mobilized. He asked instead to use office laborers and the redemption payments for offenses in Sizhou commanderies and counties punishable by ten strokes to one hundred lashes: each bolt of silk would be commuted to two hundred bricks, so construction could proceed gradually.

sentences.zh: 詔從之。

translations.literal: The edict followed this.
translations.idiomatic: The edict approved this.

sentences.zh: 太傅、清河王懌表奏其事，遂寢不行。

translations.literal: Grand Tutor Yi, Prince of Qinghe, memorialized on the matter, and it was then set aside and not carried out.
translations.idiomatic: The Grand Tutor Yuan Yi, Prince of Qinghe, submitted a memorial about the matter, and it was shelved without being carried out.

sentences.zh: 澄又奏曰：「臣聞賞必以道，用防淫人之姦；

translations.literal: Cheng again memorialized, "I have heard that rewards must accord with the Way, to guard against the wickedness of excessive men;
translations.idiomatic: Cheng also memorialized, "I have heard that rewards must follow the Way, to guard against the schemes of corrupt men;

sentences.zh: 罰不濫及，以戒良士之困。

translations.literal: punishments must not reach indiscriminately, in order to warn against the distress of good men.
translations.idiomatic: punishments must not be indiscriminate, lest good men be driven into distress.

sentences.zh: 刑者，侀也。

translations.literal: Punishment means modeling.
translations.idiomatic: Punishment is a matter of setting a model.

sentences.zh: 每垂三宥，秉律執請，不得已而用之。

translations.literal: One always extends the three pardons, and only when holding the law and presenting the request leaves no alternative is it used.
translations.idiomatic: One should always extend the three pardons, and only when the law is upheld and the request cannot be granted should punishment be used.

sentences.zh: 是故小大之獄，察之以情，一人呼嗟，或虧王道。

translations.literal: Therefore, in prisons small and great, cases are examined according to feeling; if one person cries out in sorrow, it may diminish the kingly Way.
translations.idiomatic: Thus in cases great and small, one examines the circumstances; even one person crying out in grievance can diminish the kingly Way.

sentences.zh: 刑罰得失，乃興廢之所由也。

translations.literal: The success and failure of punishments are the route by which states rise or fall.
translations.idiomatic: The success or failure of punishments is the source of a state's rise or decline.

sentences.zh: 竊聞司州牧、高陽王臣雍栲殺奉朝請韓元昭、前門下錄事姚敬賢，雖因公事，理實未盡。

translations.literal: I have privately heard that Yong, Minister of Sizhou and Prince of Gaoyang, tortured and killed Han Yuanzhao, Gentleman for Court Audience, and Yao Jingxian, former Recorder of the Chancellery. Although this arose from official business, in principle the facts were not exhausted.
translations.idiomatic: I have heard privately that Yuan Yong, Minister of Sizhou and Prince of Gaoyang, tortured and killed Han Yuanzhao, Gentleman for Court Audience, and Yao Jingxian, former Recorder of the Chancellery. Although this arose from official business, the facts were not fully investigated.

sentences.zh: 何者？

translations.literal: Why is this?
translations.idiomatic: Why do I say this?

sentences.zh: 太平之世，草不橫伐，行葦之感，事驗隆周。

translations.literal: In an age of great peace, even grass is not cut sideways; the feeling of "walking among the reeds" was verified in the flourishing Zhou.
translations.idiomatic: In an age of great peace, even grasses are not wantonly cut; the compassion shown in "Walking among the Reeds" was proven in the flourishing Zhou.

sentences.zh: 若昭等狀彰，死罪以定，應刑於都市，與眾棄之；

translations.literal: If the circumstances of Zhao and the others were manifest and the capital crime fixed, they should have been executed in the marketplace and cast away with the crowd;
translations.idiomatic: If the crimes of Yuanzhao and the others were clear and death sentences certain, they should have been executed in the marketplace and cast out before the crowd;

sentences.zh: 如其疑似不分，情理未究，不宜以三清九流之官杖下便死，輕絕民命，傷理敗法。

translations.literal: if suspicion and likeness were not distinguished and the facts and principle not fully examined, it was not fitting for officials of pure rank and regular service to die beneath the staff, lightly cutting off the people's lives and injuring principle and ruining law.
translations.idiomatic: if the suspicions had not been distinguished and the facts had not been fully examined, officials of their rank should not have died under the cudgel, their lives lightly cut off in a way that injured principle and ruined law.

sentences.zh: 往年州於大市鞭殺五人，及檢贓狀，全無寸尺。

translations.literal: In a previous year, the province flogged five men to death in the great marketplace, and when the circumstances of stolen goods were inspected, there was not even an inch or foot of evidence.
translations.idiomatic: In a previous year the province flogged five men to death in the great marketplace, and when the alleged stolen goods were investigated there was not the slightest evidence.

sentences.zh: 今復酷害，一至於此。

translations.literal: Now again cruel harm has once reached this point.
translations.idiomatic: Now its cruelty has once again gone this far.

sentences.zh: 朝野云云，咸懷驚愕。

translations.literal: Court and countryside are full of talk, and all harbor shock and alarm.
translations.idiomatic: Court and countryside are talking, and everyone is shocked.

sentences.zh: 若殺生在下，虐專於臣，人君之權，安所復用。

translations.literal: If killing and giving life are in those below, and cruelty is monopolized by ministers, where can the ruler's authority be used again?
translations.idiomatic: If life and death lie in the hands of subordinates and cruelty is monopolized by ministers, what use remains for the ruler's authority?

sentences.zh: 自開古以來，明明之世，未聞斯比也。

translations.literal: From the opening of antiquity onward, in clear and enlightened ages, I have never heard of anything like this.
translations.idiomatic: Since antiquity began, in bright and enlightened ages, I have never heard of such a thing.

sentences.zh: 武王曰：『吾不以一人之命而易天下。』

translations.literal: King Wu said, "I would not exchange all under Heaven for the life of one man."
translations.idiomatic: King Wu said, "I would not trade one man's life for all under Heaven."

sentences.zh: 蓋重民命也。

translations.literal: This was because he valued the people's lives.
translations.idiomatic: This was because he valued human life.

sentences.zh: 請以見事付廷尉推究，驗其為劫之狀，察其栲殺之理，使是非分明，幽魂獲雪。」

translations.literal: I request that the present matter be given to the Chamberlain for Law Enforcement for investigation, to verify the circumstances of their robbery and examine the principle of the torture-killings, so that right and wrong may be made clear and the hidden souls may obtain exoneration."
translations.idiomatic: I request that the case be given to the Chamberlain for Law Enforcement to investigate, verify the alleged robbery, and examine the grounds for the torture-killings, so that right and wrong become clear and the dead may be vindicated."

sentences.zh: 詔從之。

translations.literal: The edict followed this.
translations.idiomatic: The edict approved this.

sentences.zh: 澄當官而行，無所回避。

translations.literal: Cheng acted according to his office and had nothing from which he turned aside or avoided.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng acted according to his office and avoided nothing.

sentences.zh: 又奏墾田授受之制八條，甚有綱貫，大便於時。

translations.literal: He also memorialized eight articles on the system for granting and receiving cultivated fields; they had much order and coherence and were greatly convenient at the time.
translations.idiomatic: He also memorialized eight provisions on the system for allotting reclaimed fields. They were orderly and coherent, and greatly suited the needs of the time.

sentences.zh: 前來尚書文簿，諸曹須，則出借。

translations.literal: Previously, when documents and registers of the Department of State Affairs were needed by the various bureaus, they were lent out.
translations.idiomatic: Previously, when the various bureaus needed documents and registers from the Department of State Affairs, the records were lent out.

sentences.zh: 時公車署以理冤事重。

translations.literal: At the time, the Office of Public Carriages considered the handling of grievance cases important.
translations.idiomatic: At the time, the Office of Public Carriages regarded the handling of grievance cases as important.

sentences.zh: 奏請真案。

translations.literal: It memorialized requesting the original case files.
translations.idiomatic: It memorialized requesting the original case files.

sentences.zh: 澄執奏以尚書政本，特宜遠慎，故凡所奏事，閣道通之，蓋以祕要之切，防其宣露，寧有古制所重，今反輕之，內猶設禁，外更寬也。

translations.literal: Cheng firmly memorialized that the Department of State Affairs was the root of government and especially should be treated with far-reaching caution; therefore, all memorialized affairs were transmitted through the gallery passage, precisely because of the urgent importance of secrecy and to guard against their being disclosed. How could something valued by the ancient system now instead be treated lightly, with prohibitions still set inside while outside they were made even looser?
translations.idiomatic: Cheng insisted in a memorial that the Department of State Affairs was the root of government and had to be handled with special caution. All memorialized matters were transmitted through the palace galleries precisely because secrecy was urgent and disclosure had to be prevented. How could something the ancient system treated as weighty now be treated lightly, keeping restrictions inside while loosening them outside?

sentences.zh: 宜繕寫事意，以付公車。

translations.literal: The meaning of the matter should be copied out and given to the Office of Public Carriages.
translations.idiomatic: The substance of the case should be copied out and given to the Office of Public Carriages.

sentences.zh: 詔從之。

translations.literal: The edict followed it.
translations.idiomatic: The edict agreed.

sentences.zh: 西域嚈噠、波斯諸國各因公使，並遺澄駿馬一匹。

translations.literal: The Hephthalites, Persia, and other countries of the Western Regions each used official envoys to present Cheng with one fine horse.
translations.idiomatic: The Hephthalites, Persia, and other countries of the Western Regions each sent Cheng a fine horse through official envoys.

sentences.zh: 澄請付太僕，以充國閑。

translations.literal: Cheng requested that they be given to the Grand Coachman to fill the state stables.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng asked that the horses be given to the Grand Coachman and added to the state stables.

sentences.zh: 詔曰：「王廉貞之德，有過楚相，可敕付廐，以成君子大哉之美。」

translations.literal: The edict said, "The Prince's virtue of incorrupt uprightness surpasses that of the minister of Chu. They may be ordered sent to the stables, to complete the noble man's great beauty."
translations.idiomatic: The edict said, "The Prince's incorrupt virtue surpasses that of the minister of Chu. Let the horses be sent to the stables, completing the great beauty of a gentleman."

sentences.zh: 御史中尉東平王匡奏請取景明元年以來，內外考簿、吏部除書、中兵勳案并諸殿最，欲以案校竊階盜官之人，靈太后許之。

translations.literal: Censor-in-Chief Kuang, Prince of Dongping, memorialized requesting to take the evaluation registers from inside and outside the court since the first year of Jingming, the Ministry of Personnel appointment documents, Central Army merit files, and all assessments of best and worst, wishing to use the files to check those who had stolen ranks and usurped offices. Empress Dowager Ling permitted it.
translations.idiomatic: Kuang, Prince of Dongping and Censor-in-Chief, requested the evaluation registers from inside and outside the court since Jingming year 1, the Ministry of Personnel appointment documents, Central Army merit files, and all best-and-worst assessments, intending to use them to investigate those who had stolen ranks and offices. Empress Dowager Ling allowed it.

sentences.zh: 澄表曰：「臣聞三季之弊，由於煩刑；

translations.literal: Cheng memorialized, "I have heard that the abuses of the three declining ages arose from cumbersome punishments;
translations.idiomatic: Cheng memorialized, "I have heard that the abuses of the three declining ages came from excessive punishments;

sentences.zh: 火德之興，在於三約。

translations.literal: the rise of the Fire Virtue lay in the Three Articles.
translations.idiomatic: the rise of the Fire Virtue rested on the Three Articles of law.

sentences.zh: 是以老聃云「法令滋彰，盜賊多有」，又曰「其政察察，其民缺缺」，又曰「天網恢恢，疏而不漏」。

translations.literal: Therefore Lao Dan says, "When laws and commands grow ever more manifest, robbers and thieves are many," and also says, "When government is sharply scrutinizing, the people are deficient," and also says, "The net of Heaven is vast; its mesh is wide, yet nothing escapes."
translations.idiomatic: Thus Lao Dan says, "The more laws and commands are displayed, the more thieves and robbers there are"; again, "When government is exacting, the people are impoverished"; and again, "The net of Heaven is vast; its mesh is wide, yet nothing escapes."

sentences.zh: 是故欲求治本，莫若省事清心。

translations.literal: Therefore, if one wishes to seek the root of order, nothing is better than reducing affairs and clearing the mind.
translations.idiomatic: Thus, to seek the root of good order, nothing is better than reducing affairs and clearing the mind.

sentences.zh: 昔漢文斷獄四百，幾致刑措，省事所致也。

translations.literal: In the past, Emperor Wen of Han decided four hundred prison cases and nearly brought punishments to rest; this was caused by reducing affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In the past, Emperor Wen of Han decided only four hundred cases and nearly brought punishment to rest; this came from reducing affairs.

sentences.zh: 蕭曹為相，載其清靜畫一之歌，清心之本也。

translations.literal: When Xiao He and Cao Shen served as ministers, songs recorded their purity, quietness, and uniformity; this was the root of clearing the mind.
translations.idiomatic: When Xiao He and Cao Shen served as ministers, songs praised their pure, quiet, and consistent rule; this was rooted in clearing the mind.

sentences.zh: 今欲求之於本，宜以省事為先，使在位羣官，纂蕭曹之心，以毗聖化。

translations.literal: Now if we wish to seek it at the root, we should put reducing affairs first, causing the officials in office to continue the mind of Xiao and Cao in order to aid the sacred transformation.
translations.idiomatic: If we now seek the root, we should begin by reducing affairs, so that officials continue the spirit of Xiao and Cao and assist the sacred transformation.

sentences.zh: 如此，則上下相安，遠近相信，百司不怠，事無愆失。

translations.literal: If this is so, then above and below will be at peace with each other, far and near will trust each other, the hundred offices will not be negligent, and affairs will have no errors or losses.
translations.idiomatic: Then ruler and subjects will be at peace, far and near will trust each other, the offices will not grow negligent, and affairs will not go astray.

sentences.zh: 豈宜擾世教以深文，烹小鮮以煩手哉。

translations.literal: How could it be fitting to disturb the teaching of the age with deep legal texts, or to cook small fish with troublesome hands?
translations.idiomatic: How could it be right to disturb the teaching of the age with over-subtle laws, or to cook small fish with fussy hands?

sentences.zh: 臣竊惟景明之初暨永平之末，內外羣官三經考課。

translations.literal: I privately consider that from the beginning of Jingming to the end of Yongping, the officials inside and outside the court went through three evaluations.
translations.idiomatic: I privately consider that from the start of Jingming to the end of Yongping, officials inside and outside the court underwent three evaluations.

sentences.zh: 逮延昌之始，方加黜陟。

translations.literal: Only when the Yanchang era began were demotions and promotions added.
translations.idiomatic: Only at the start of Yanchang were promotions and demotions applied.

sentences.zh: 五品以上，引之朝堂，親決聖目；

translations.literal: Those of the fifth rank and above were brought to the court hall and personally decided by the sacred eyes;
translations.idiomatic: Those of the fifth rank and above were brought into the court hall and personally judged by His Majesty;

sentences.zh: 六品以下，例由敕判。

translations.literal: those of the sixth rank and below were as a rule decided by edict.
translations.idiomatic: those of the sixth rank and below were decided by edict as a rule.

sentences.zh: 自世宗晏駕，大宥三行，所以蕩除故意，與物更始。

translations.literal: Since Shizong passed away, a great amnesty has been carried out three times, by which former intentions were swept away and things began anew.
translations.idiomatic: Since Shizong's death, three great amnesties have been issued to wipe away old intentions and begin anew.

sentences.zh: 革世之事，方相窮覈，以臣愚見，謂為不可。

translations.literal: For matters from a changed age now to be mutually pursued and investigated, in my foolish view, is impermissible.
translations.idiomatic: To reopen and investigate matters from a previous reign now is, in my foolish view, impermissible.

sentences.zh: 又尚書職分，樞機出納。

translations.literal: Moreover, the Department of State Affairs has its assigned duties: the issuing and receiving of pivotal affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, the Department of State Affairs has its own function: receiving and issuing the pivotal business of government.
