sentences.zh: 昔魏明帝卒至尚書門，陳矯亢辭，帝慚而返。

translations.literal: In the past, Emperor Ming of Wei suddenly went to the gate of the Department of State Affairs; Chen Jiao spoke bluntly, and the emperor was ashamed and returned.
translations.idiomatic: In the past, Emperor Ming of Wei suddenly arrived at the Department gate; Chen Jiao remonstrated firmly, and the emperor withdrew in shame.

sentences.zh: 夫以萬乘之重，非所宜行，猶屈一言，慚而回駕，羣官百司，而可相亂乎？

translations.literal: If even one with the weight of ten thousand chariots, in a place he should not go, still yielded to a single word and turned back in shame, how can the many officials and hundred offices disorder one another?
translations.idiomatic: If even the lord of ten thousand chariots, when he went somewhere improper, yielded to one word and turned back ashamed, how can the officials and offices be allowed to intrude on one another?

sentences.zh: 故陳平不知錢穀之數，邴吉不問僵道之死，當時以為達治，歷代用為美談。

translations.literal: Therefore Chen Ping did not know the number of coins and grain, and Bing Ji did not inquire into the death of the man fallen in the road. At the time this was considered understanding government, and later ages used it as a fine story.
translations.idiomatic: Thus Chen Ping did not know the accounts of coin and grain, and Bing Ji did not ask about the dead man lying by the road. Their age considered this good understanding of government, and later generations praised it.

sentences.zh: 但宜各守其職，思不出位，潔己以勵時，靖恭以致節。

translations.literal: One should merely each keep to his office, think without going beyond his position, cleanse himself to encourage the age, and be quiet and reverent in order to bring about integrity.
translations.idiomatic: Each man should keep to his own office, think without overstepping his position, keep himself pure to encourage the age, and be quiet and reverent to achieve integrity.

sentences.zh: 又尋御史之體，風聞是司，至於冒勳妄考，皆有處別，若一處有風謠，即應攝其一簿，研檢虛實，若差舛不同，偽情自露，然後繩以典刑，人孰不服。

translations.literal: Also, examining the function of the censors, hearing of matters by report is their office. As for falsely claiming merit and reckless evaluations, all have their separate places. If in one place there are rumors, then one register should be seized, false and true should be examined, and if discrepancies differ, the false intent will reveal itself; only afterward should they be bound by statute and punishment, and who would not submit?
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, the censorate's role is to act on reports. False claims of merit and reckless evaluations each have their proper offices. If rumors arise in one place, seize that one register and examine truth and falsehood; if discrepancies appear, the fraud will reveal itself. Then punish by statute, and who will not submit?

sentences.zh: 豈有移一省之案，取天下之簿，尋兩紀之事，窮革世之尤，如此求過，誰堪其罪！

translations.literal: How can there be moving the files of one department, taking the registers of all under Heaven, searching affairs of two dozen years, and exhausting the faults of a changed age? If errors are sought like this, who could bear the guilt?
translations.idiomatic: How can one move the files of an entire department, seize the registers of the whole empire, search through two decades of affairs, and pursue every fault of a former reign? If faults are sought this way, who could bear the guilt?

sentences.zh: 斯實聖朝所宜重慎也。」

translations.literal: This is truly something the sacred court should treat with great care."
translations.idiomatic: This is truly something the sacred court should treat with the greatest caution."

sentences.zh: 靈太后納之，乃止。

translations.literal: Empress Dowager Ling accepted this, and the matter stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Dowager Ling accepted this, and the matter was stopped.

sentences.zh: 後遷司徒公，侍中、尚書令如故。

translations.literal: Later he was promoted to Minister over the Masses, while Palace Attendant and Director of the Department of State Affairs remained as before.
translations.idiomatic: Later he was promoted to Minister over the Masses, while remaining Palace Attendant and Director of the Department of State Affairs as before.

sentences.zh: 澄又表曰：「伏惟世宗宣武皇帝命將授旗，隨陸啟顙，運籌制勝，淮漢自賓。

translations.literal: Cheng again memorialized, "I bow and consider that Emperor Xuanwu, Shizong, commissioned generals and granted banners; Sui and Lu bowed their heads; he planned and controlled victory, and the Huai and Han submitted of themselves.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng also memorialized, "I humbly recall that Emperor Xuanwu, Shizong, commissioned generals and granted banners; Sui and Lu bowed their heads, and through his strategy the Huai and Han submitted of themselves.

sentences.zh: 節用勞心，志清六合，是故纘武修文，仍世彌盛。

translations.literal: He economized expenditures and labored his mind, with the aim of clearing the six directions; therefore he continued martial achievement and cultivated civil rule, and each generation grew more flourishing.
translations.idiomatic: He saved resources and exhausted his mind, intending to clear the six directions. Thus he continued military achievement and cultivated civil rule, and the dynasty grew stronger generation after generation.

sentences.zh: 陛下當周康靖治之時，豈得晏安於玄默。

translations.literal: Your Majesty is in a time like the tranquil rule of King Kang of Zhou; how can you rest secure in dark silence?
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty lives in a time like the tranquil rule of King Kang of Zhou; how could you rest in silent ease?

sentences.zh: 然取外之理，要由內強；

translations.literal: Yet the principle of taking the outside necessarily comes from strengthening the inside;
translations.idiomatic: Yet to take what lies outside, one must first strengthen what lies within;

sentences.zh: 圖人之本，先在自備。

translations.literal: the root of planning against others first lies in preparing oneself.
translations.idiomatic: to plan against others, one must first prepare oneself.

sentences.zh: 蕭衍雖虐使其民，而窺覦不已。

translations.literal: Although Xiao Yan cruelly uses his people, his coveting and watching do not cease.
translations.idiomatic: Although Xiao Yan oppresses his people cruelly, he never stops coveting our lands.

sentences.zh: 若遇我虛疲，士民淍窘，賊衍年老志張，思播虺毒，此之弗圖，恐受其病。

translations.literal: If he encounters our emptiness and exhaustion, with soldiers and people withered and distressed, the rebel Yan, old in years but expanding in ambition, will think to spread his viper poison. If we do not plan for this, I fear we will suffer from it.
translations.idiomatic: If he finds us empty and exhausted, our soldiers and people worn down, then the aged rebel Yan, his ambition still swelling, will try to spread his venom. If we do not plan for this, I fear we will suffer.

sentences.zh: 伏惟陛下妙齡在位，聖德方昇；

translations.literal: I bow and consider that Your Majesty occupies the throne at a marvelous age, and your sacred virtue is just rising;
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty occupies the throne at a fine young age, and your sacred virtue is just ascending;

sentences.zh: 皇太后總御天機，乾乾夕惕。

translations.literal: the Empress Dowager oversees the heavenly mechanism, diligent and watchful day and night.
translations.idiomatic: the Empress Dowager directs the machinery of state, diligent and watchful day and night.

sentences.zh: 若留意於負荷，忿車書之未一。

translations.literal: If attention is kept on the burden borne, and anger is felt that carts and writing are not yet unified;
translations.idiomatic: If you keep the state's burden in mind and resent that carriage tracks and writing are not yet unified;

sentences.zh: 進賢拔能，重官人之舉；

translations.literal: if worthies are advanced and the able selected, and the choosing of officials to office is treated as weighty;
translations.idiomatic: if you advance worthies, select the able, and treat official appointments as weighty;

sentences.zh: 標賞忠清，旌養人之器；

translations.literal: if loyal purity is marked with rewards, and vessels for nurturing men are made clear;
translations.idiomatic: if you reward loyalty and purity and recognize men fit to nurture the people;

sentences.zh: 修干戈之用，畜熊虎之士；

translations.literal: if the use of shields and spears is repaired, and bear-and-tiger warriors are stored up;
translations.idiomatic: if you strengthen the use of arms and store up bear-and-tiger warriors;

sentences.zh: 愛時鄙財，輕寶重穀。

translations.literal: if time is cherished and wealth despised, treasures treated lightly and grain valued;
translations.idiomatic: if you cherish time, despise mere wealth, treat treasures lightly, and value grain;

sentences.zh: 七八年間，陛下聖略方剛，親王德幹壯茂，將相膂力未衰，愚臣猶堪戎伍，荷戈帶甲之眾蓄銳於今，燕弧冀馬之盛充牣在昔；

translations.literal: then within seven or eight years, Your Majesty's sacred strategy will be firm and strong, the virtue and capacity of the imperial princes will be robust, the strength of generals and ministers will not yet have declined, this foolish minister will still be fit for the ranks, the spear-bearing armored masses will have stored their edge by then, and the abundance of Yan bows and Ji horses will be full as of old;
translations.idiomatic: then in seven or eight years Your Majesty's strategy will be vigorous, the imperial princes' virtue and capacity will be mature, the generals and ministers will not yet have lost their strength, I will still be fit for the ranks, the armored troops will have stored up their sharpness, and the famous bows of Yan and horses of Ji will again be plentiful;

sentences.zh: 又賊衍惡積禍盈，勢不能久，子弟闇悖，釁逆已彰，亂亡之兆，灼然可見。

translations.literal: moreover the rebel Yan's evil will have accumulated and his disaster become full, his power cannot last, his sons and younger brothers are benighted and perverse, and their signs of rebellion are already manifest; the omens of chaos and ruin can be seen clearly.
translations.idiomatic: moreover Xiao Yan's evil will have ripened into disaster, his power cannot last, his sons and brothers are dark and perverse, and their rebellious rifts are already clear. The signs of chaos and ruin are plainly visible.

sentences.zh: 兼弱有徵，天與不遠，大同之機，宜須蓄備。

translations.literal: Combining the weak has signs, Heaven's giving is not distant, and the opportunity for great unity should await stored preparations.
translations.idiomatic: The signs point to annexing the weak; Heaven's gift is not far away, and the moment for great unity should be met with stored preparations.

sentences.zh: 昔漢帝力疾，討滅英布；

translations.literal: In the past, the Han emperor exerted himself through illness and attacked and destroyed Ying Bu;
translations.idiomatic: In the past, the Han emperor forced himself through illness to destroy Ying Bu;

sentences.zh: 高皇臥病，親除顯達。

translations.literal: the High Emperor lay ill, yet personally eliminated Xianda.
translations.idiomatic: our High Emperor lay ill, yet personally eliminated Xianda.

sentences.zh: 夫以萬乘之主，豈忘宴安，實以侵名亂正，計不得已。

translations.literal: How could lords of ten thousand chariots forget ease and security? It was truly because reputations were encroached upon and correctness disordered, and their plans left them no choice.
translations.idiomatic: How could rulers of ten thousand chariots forget comfort and security? They acted because names were violated and order disturbed, leaving no alternative.

sentences.zh: 今宜慕二帝之遠圖，以肅寧為大任。

translations.literal: Now we should admire the far-reaching plans of the two emperors and take solemn pacification as our great task.
translations.idiomatic: Now we should emulate the far-reaching plans of those two emperors and make solemn pacification our great task.

sentences.zh: 然頃年以來，東西難寇，艱虞之興，首尾連接，雖尋得翦除，亦大損財力。

translations.literal: Yet in recent years, difficult bandits in east and west have arisen in hardships and dangers one after another from beginning to end; although they were soon cut down and removed, they greatly damaged wealth and strength.
translations.idiomatic: Yet in recent years, hard campaigns against raiders in east and west have followed one another. Though they were soon eliminated, they greatly damaged our resources and strength.

sentences.zh: 且飢饉之氓，散亡莫保，收入之賦不增，出用之費彌眾，不愛力以悅民，無豐資以待敵，此臣所以夙夜懷憂，悚息不寧者也。

translations.literal: Moreover, hungry people scatter and flee and cannot be secured; the taxes received do not increase, while expenditures grow ever more numerous. If we do not spare strength to please the people and have no abundant resources with which to await the enemy, this is why I worry day and night and breathe in fear without peace.
translations.idiomatic: Hungry people scatter and cannot be secured; revenues do not grow, while expenses multiply. If we do not spare labor to please the people and build resources to await the enemy, I will continue to worry day and night, fearful and uneasy.

sentences.zh: 易曰：「何以守位曰仁，何以聚人曰財。」

translations.literal: The Changes says, "How does one guard position? It says: benevolence. How does one gather people? It says: wealth."
translations.idiomatic: The Changes says, "How does one hold position? By benevolence. How does one gather people? By wealth."

sentences.zh: 故曰：財者，非天不生，非地不長，非時不成，非人不聚。

translations.literal: Therefore it is said: wealth is not born without Heaven, does not grow without Earth, does not mature without the season, and does not gather without people.
translations.idiomatic: Thus wealth is not born without Heaven, does not grow without Earth, does not mature without the seasons, and does not gather without people.

sentences.zh: 生聚之由，如此其難；

translations.literal: The means by which it is produced and gathered are this difficult;
translations.idiomatic: Producing and gathering it is this difficult;

sentences.zh: 集人守位，若此之重。

translations.literal: gathering people and guarding position are this weighty.
translations.idiomatic: gathering people and holding position are this weighty.

sentences.zh: 興替之道，焉可不慮。

translations.literal: How can the way of rise and replacement not be considered?
translations.idiomatic: How can one fail to consider the path of rise and decline?

sentences.zh: 又古者使民，歲不過三日，食壯者之糧，任老者之智。

translations.literal: Also, in antiquity, when the people were used for labor, it did not exceed three days a year; the grain of the strong was used, and the wisdom of the old was employed.
translations.idiomatic: In antiquity, labor service imposed on the people did not exceed three days a year; the grain of the strong was used, and the wisdom of the old was employed.

sentences.zh: 此雖太平之法，難卒而因；

translations.literal: Although this is a law of great peace and difficult to follow immediately,
translations.idiomatic: Although this is a rule for an age of great peace and cannot be followed all at once,

sentences.zh: 然妨民害財，不亦宜戒！

translations.literal: should one not be warned against harming the people and damaging wealth?
translations.idiomatic: should we not be warned against harming the people and wasting wealth?

sentences.zh: 今墉雉素修，廐庫崇列。

translations.literal: Now the walls and battlements have already been repaired, and stables and storehouses stand in lofty rows.
translations.idiomatic: Now the walls and battlements are already repaired, and the stables and storehouses stand in lofty rows.

sentences.zh: 雖府寺膠塾，少有未周，大抵省府粗得庇憇理務，諸寺靈塔俱足致虔講道。

translations.literal: Although offices, temples, schools, and halls are in small part not yet complete, in general the government offices can roughly shelter rest and the handling of affairs, and the temples and spirit towers are all sufficient for reverent worship and lecturing on the Way.
translations.idiomatic: Although some offices, temples, schools, and halls are not yet complete, the government offices are generally sufficient for work and rest, and the temples and spirit towers suffice for worship and teaching.

sentences.zh: 唯明堂辟雍，國禮之大。

translations.literal: Only the Mingtang and Biyong are great matters of state ritual.
translations.idiomatic: Only the Mingtang and Biyong are major matters of state ritual.

sentences.zh: 來冬司徒兵至，請籌量減徹，專力經營，務令早就。

translations.literal: When the Minister over the Masses' troops arrive next winter, I request that plans be made to reduce and dismantle other works, focus efforts on managing these, and make every effort to finish them early.
translations.idiomatic: When the Minister over the Masses' troops arrive next winter, I ask that other works be reduced or dismantled, effort focused on these projects, and every effort made to complete them early.

sentences.zh: 其廣濟數施之財，酬商互市之弊，凡所營造，自非供御切須，戎仗急要，亦宜微減，以務阜積，庶府無橫損，民有全力。

translations.literal: As for the funds for Guangji and repeated almsgiving, and the abuses of payments to merchants and market exchange, all construction that is not urgently required for imperial supply or urgently needed for weapons should also be slightly reduced, so as to work at making stores abundant, so the treasuries suffer no irregular losses and the people preserve their full strength.
translations.idiomatic: Funds for Guangji, repeated almsgiving, merchant payments, and market exchanges, and all construction not urgently needed for imperial supply or military equipment, should be modestly reduced. This will build stores, prevent irregular losses to the treasuries, and preserve the people's strength.

sentences.zh: 夫食土簋而媯德昭，寢卑室而禹功盛，章臺麗而楚力衰，阿宮壯而秦財竭，存亡之由，灼然可覩。

translations.literal: Eating from earthen vessels made the virtue of Gui manifest; sleeping in a lowly chamber made Yu's achievement flourish. Zhangtai was beautiful and Chu's strength declined; Epang was grand and Qin's wealth was exhausted. The sources of survival and destruction may be seen clearly.
translations.idiomatic: Gui's virtue shone because he ate from earthen vessels; Yu's achievement flourished though he slept in a humble room. Zhangtai was splendid and Chu weakened; Epang was grand and Qin's wealth ran dry. The causes of survival and destruction are plain to see.

sentences.zh: 願思前王一同之功，畜力聚財，以待時會。」

translations.literal: I hope you will think of the former kings' achievement in bringing all to unity, store strength and gather wealth, and thereby await the meeting with opportunity."
translations.idiomatic: I hope you will reflect on the former kings' achievement in unifying all, store strength and gather wealth, and wait for the right moment."

sentences.zh: 靈太后銳於繕興，在京師則起永寧、太上公等佛寺，功費不少，外州各造五級佛圖，又數為一切齋會，施物動至萬計。

translations.literal: Empress Dowager Ling was eager in repair and construction. In the capital, she built Buddhist temples such as Yongning and Taishanggong, with no small expenditure of labor and funds; in the outer provinces each built five-tiered stupas, and she also repeatedly held universal vegetarian assemblies, where gifts often reached amounts counted by the ten thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Dowager Ling was eager for construction. In the capital she built Buddhist temples such as Yongning and Taishanggong at considerable cost; in the outer provinces, each built five-tiered stupas. She also repeatedly held universal vegetarian assemblies, where gifts often ran into the tens of thousands.

sentences.zh: 百姓疲於土木之功，金銀之價為之踊上，削奪百官事力，費損庫藏，兼曲賚左右，日有數千。

translations.literal: The common people were exhausted by works of earth and timber; the price of gold and silver leapt upward because of it. The service labor of the hundred officials was cut away and seized, the treasuries were spent and damaged, and special gifts to attendants amounted to several thousand each day.
translations.idiomatic: The people were exhausted by earthwork and carpentry, and the price of gold and silver soared. Officials' labor resources were seized, the treasuries drained, and special gifts to attendants reached several thousand each day.

sentences.zh: 澄故有此表。

translations.literal: Therefore Cheng made this memorial.
translations.idiomatic: This was why Cheng submitted the memorial.

sentences.zh: 雖卒不從，常優答禮之。

translations.literal: Although in the end she did not follow it, she always answered him generously and treated him with courtesy.
translations.idiomatic: Although she ultimately did not follow it, she always replied graciously and treated him with courtesy.

sentences.zh: 政無大小，皆引參決。

translations.literal: In government, whether matters were large or small, he was always brought in to participate in decisions.
translations.idiomatic: In affairs of government, great or small, he was always brought in to take part in decisions.

sentences.zh: 澄亦盡心匡輔，事有不便於民者，必於諫諍，雖不見用，殷勤不已，內外咸敬憚之。

translations.literal: Cheng also devoted his whole heart to correcting and assisting. If a matter was not convenient for the people, he would certainly remonstrate; even when he was not heeded, he was earnest without cease, and all inside and outside the court respected and feared him.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng devoted himself fully to correction and support. Whenever something was harmful to the people, he remonstrated; even when not heeded, he persisted earnestly. Those inside and outside the court all respected and feared him.

sentences.zh: 神龜二年薨，年五十三。

translations.literal: He died in the second year of Shengui, at the age of fifty-three.
translations.idiomatic: He died in Shengui year 2 at the age of fifty-three.

sentences.zh: 賻布一千二百匹、錢六十萬、蠟四百斤，給東園溫明祕器、朝服一具、衣一襲；

translations.literal: For funeral gifts, he received one thousand two hundred bolts of cloth, six hundred thousand cash, and four hundred jin of wax; he was given the Eastern Garden warm-bright secret coffin, one set of court robes, and one suit of clothes;
translations.idiomatic: For funeral gifts he received twelve hundred bolts of cloth, six hundred thousand cash, and four hundred jin of wax; he was given an Eastern Garden Wenming coffin, one set of court robes, and one suit of clothing;

sentences.zh: 大鴻臚監護喪事，詔百僚會喪；

translations.literal: the Grand Herald supervised and protected the funeral affairs, and an edict ordered the hundred officials to assemble for the funeral;
translations.idiomatic: the Grand Herald oversaw the funeral, and an edict ordered the officials to attend;

sentences.zh: 贈假黃鉞、使持節、都督中外諸軍事、太傅，領太尉公；

translations.literal: he was posthumously given Acting Yellow Axe, Bearer of the Staff, Commander of all military affairs inside and outside the court, Grand Tutor, and concurrently Grand Commandant;
translations.idiomatic: he was posthumously granted Acting Yellow Axe, Bearer of the Staff, Commander of all military affairs inside and outside the court, Grand Tutor, and concurrently Grand Commandant;

sentences.zh: 加以殊禮，備九錫，依晉大司馬、齊王攸故事；

translations.literal: special rites were added, with the Nine Bestowments complete, following the precedent of You, Grand Marshal of Jin and Prince of Qi;
translations.idiomatic: special rites were added, including the full Nine Bestowments, following the precedent of Sima You, Grand Marshal of Jin and Prince of Qi;

sentences.zh: 諡曰文宣王。

translations.literal: his posthumous title was Prince Wenxuan.
translations.idiomatic: His posthumous title was Prince Wenxuan.

sentences.zh: 澄之葬也，凶飾甚盛。

translations.literal: At Cheng's burial, the mourning decorations were very grand.
translations.idiomatic: At Cheng's burial, the mourning regalia were extremely grand.

sentences.zh: 靈太后親送郊外，停輿悲哭，哀動左右。

translations.literal: Empress Dowager Ling personally escorted him outside the suburbs, stopped her carriage and wept in grief, and her sorrow moved those at left and right.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Dowager Ling personally escorted him beyond the suburbs, stopped her carriage, and wept bitterly, moving all those around her.

sentences.zh: 百官會赴千餘人，莫不歔欷。

translations.literal: More than a thousand officials assembled and attended, and none failed to sigh and sob.
translations.idiomatic: More than a thousand officials attended, and all sighed and wept.

sentences.zh: 當時以為哀榮之極。

translations.literal: At the time this was considered the utmost of mourning and honor.
translations.idiomatic: At the time this was considered the height of mourning and honor.

sentences.zh: 第四子獻，襲。

translations.literal: His fourth son Xian succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: The fourth son, Xian, inherited.

sentences.zh: 彝，字子倫，繼室馮氏所生，頗有父風。

translations.literal: Yi, courtesy name Zilun, was born to the second wife Lady Feng and had much of his father's manner.
translations.idiomatic: Yi, courtesy name Zilun, was born to Cheng's second wife Lady Feng and had much of his father's manner.

sentences.zh: 拜通直散騎常侍。

translations.literal: He was appointed Regular Cavalier Attendant for Unrestricted Attendance.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Regular Cavalier Attendant for Unrestricted Attendance.

sentences.zh: 及元叉專權，而彝耻於託附，故不得顯職。

translations.literal: When Yuan Cha monopolized power, Yi was ashamed to attach himself to him, and therefore did not obtain prominent office.
translations.idiomatic: When Yuan Cha monopolized power, Yi was ashamed to attach himself to him and therefore did not obtain prominent office.

sentences.zh: 莊帝初，河陰遇害，贈車騎將軍、儀同三司、青州刺史。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the reign of Emperor Zhuang, he was killed in the Heyin incident and posthumously given General of Chariots and Cavalry, Equal in Honor to the Three Excellencies, and Inspector of Qingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of Emperor Zhuang's reign, he was killed at Heyin and posthumously granted General of Chariots and Cavalry, Equal in Honor to the Three Excellencies, and Inspector of Qingzhou.

sentences.zh: 諡曰文。

translations.literal: His posthumous title was Wen.
translations.idiomatic: His posthumous title was Wen.

sentences.zh: 子度世，襲。

translations.literal: His son Dushi succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: His son Dushi succeeded.

sentences.zh: 武定中，金紫光祿大夫。

translations.literal: In the Wuding era, he was Gold and Purple Guanglu Grandee.
translations.idiomatic: In the Wuding era, he served as Gold and Purple Guanglu Grandee.

sentences.zh: 齊受禪，爵例降。

translations.literal: When Qi received the Mandate, titles were reduced by precedent.
translations.idiomatic: After Qi took the throne, enfeoffments were lowered by precedent.

sentences.zh: 彝兄順，字子和。

translations.literal: Yi's elder brother Shun was styled Zihe.
translations.idiomatic: Yi's elder brother Shun was styled Zihe.

sentences.zh: 九歲師事樂安陳豐，初書王羲之小學篇數千言，晝夜誦之，旬有五日，一皆通徹。

translations.literal: At nine, he studied under Chen Feng of Le'an. At first he copied several thousand words of Wang Xizhi's Elementary Primer and recited it day and night; in fifteen days he had understood it all.
translations.idiomatic: At nine, he studied with Chen Feng of Le'an. He first copied several thousand words of Wang Xizhi's Elementary Primer, reciting it day and night, and in fifteen days he had mastered it all.

sentences.zh: 豐奇之，白澄曰：「豐十五從師，迄于白首，耳目所經，未見此比，江夏黃童，不得無雙也。」

translations.literal: Feng marveled at him and told Cheng, "I followed teachers from fifteen until white hair, and in all that my ears and eyes have passed through, I have never seen his like. The yellow-haired boy of Jiangxia cannot be without a match."
translations.idiomatic: Feng marveled and told Cheng, "I have studied with teachers from the age of fifteen to white-haired old age, and never in all I have seen or heard have I met his equal. The yellow-haired prodigy of Jiangxia cannot be peerless after all."

sentences.zh: 澄笑曰：「藍田生玉，何容不爾。」

translations.literal: Cheng smiled and said, "Lantian produces jade; how could it not be so?"
translations.idiomatic: Cheng smiled. "Lantian produces jade; how could it be otherwise?"

sentences.zh: 十六，通杜氏春秋，恒集門生，討論同異。

translations.literal: At sixteen he understood Master Du's Spring and Autumn, and he constantly gathered students to discuss agreements and differences.
translations.idiomatic: At sixteen he mastered Master Du's Spring and Autumn and often gathered students to debate points of agreement and difference.

sentences.zh: 于時四方無事，國富民康，豪貴子弟，率以朋遊為樂，而順下帷讀書，篤志愛古。

translations.literal: At the time there were no affairs on the four sides, the state was wealthy and the people at ease, and the sons of the powerful and noble generally took pleasure in companionable excursions; but Shun lowered the curtain and read, firmly intent on loving antiquity.
translations.idiomatic: At the time the frontiers were quiet, the state was rich, and the people were at peace. The sons of the powerful generally amused themselves with companions, but Shun shut himself behind the curtain to read, devoted to antiquity.

sentences.zh: 性謇諤，淡於榮利，好飲酒，解鼓琴，能長吟永歎，吒詠虛室。

translations.literal: By nature he was blunt in remonstrance, indifferent to glory and profit, fond of drinking wine, understood playing the zither, and could chant long and sigh deeply, crying out and singing in an empty room.
translations.idiomatic: He was naturally blunt, indifferent to honor and profit, fond of wine, and skilled at the zither; he could chant at length, sigh deeply, and sing out in an empty room.

sentences.zh: 世宗時，上魏頌，文多不載。

translations.literal: In Shizong's time, he submitted a Eulogy of Wei; much of the text is not recorded.
translations.idiomatic: During Shizong's reign he submitted a Eulogy of Wei, though much of the text is not preserved.

sentences.zh: 起家為給事中。

translations.literal: He began his career as Supervising Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: He began his career as Supervising Attendant.

sentences.zh: 時尚書令高肇，帝舅權重，天下人士，望塵拜伏。

translations.literal: At the time Gao Zhao, Director of the Department of State Affairs, was the emperor's maternal uncle, and his power was weighty; men of the realm bowed and prostrated themselves at the sight of his dust.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Gao Zhao, Director of the Department and the emperor's maternal uncle, held immense power; men throughout the realm bowed before even the dust of his carriage.

sentences.zh: 順曾懷刺詣肇門，門者以其年少，答云「在坐大有貴客」，不肯為通。

translations.literal: Shun once carried a calling card to Zhao's gate, but the gatekeeper, because he was young, replied, "Inside there are many honored guests seated," and refused to announce him.
translations.idiomatic: Shun once brought a calling card to Zhao's gate. Seeing his youth, the gatekeeper answered, "There are many great guests seated inside," and refused to announce him.

sentences.zh: 順叱之曰：「任城王兒，可是賤也！」

translations.literal: Shun rebuked him, saying, "Can the son of the Prince of Rencheng be base?"
translations.idiomatic: Shun scolded him: "Can the son of the Prince of Rencheng be someone base?"

sentences.zh: 及見，直往登牀，捧手抗禮，王公先達，莫不怪慴，而順辭吐傲然，若無所覩。

translations.literal: When he was received, he went straight forward and climbed onto the couch, held up his hands, and performed equal courtesy; the princes, dukes, and senior worthies all marveled and were awed, yet Shun's words and expression were proud, as though he saw no one.
translations.idiomatic: When admitted, he went straight to the couch, mounted it, clasped his hands, and greeted Zhao as an equal. Princes, dukes, and elder worthies were all startled and awed, while Shun spoke proudly as if no one else were there.

sentences.zh: 肇謂眾賓曰：「此兒豪氣尚爾，況其父乎！」

translations.literal: Zhao told the assembled guests, "This boy's heroic spirit is already like this; how much more his father!"
translations.idiomatic: Zhao told his guests, "If the boy's spirit is already like this, how much more his father!"

sentences.zh: 及出，肇加敬送之。

translations.literal: When he went out, Zhao showed added respect and saw him off.
translations.idiomatic: When Shun left, Zhao treated him with added respect and saw him off.

sentences.zh: 澄聞之，大怒，杖之數十。

translations.literal: When Cheng heard of it, he was furious and beat him several dozen strokes with a staff.
translations.idiomatic: When Cheng heard of this, he was furious and had him caned several dozen strokes.

sentences.zh: 後超轉中書侍郎，俄遷太常少卿。

translations.literal: Later he was exceptionally transferred to Secretariat Attendant, and shortly afterward promoted to Junior Chamberlain for Ceremonials.
translations.idiomatic: Later he was promoted out of turn to Secretariat Attendant, and soon advanced to Junior Chamberlain for Ceremonials.

sentences.zh: 以父憂去職，哭泣嘔血，身自負土。

translations.literal: Because of mourning for his father he left office; he wept until he vomited blood and personally carried earth.
translations.idiomatic: He left office to mourn his father, wept until he vomited blood, and carried earth for the grave himself.

sentences.zh: 時年二十五，便有白髮，免喪抽去，不復更生，世人以為孝思所致。

translations.literal: At that time he was twenty-five, yet already had white hair; when mourning was complete, he plucked it out, and it did not grow again. People of the age thought this was caused by filial grief.
translations.idiomatic: He was twenty-five at the time, yet already had white hair. After mourning ended he plucked it out, and it never grew back; people believed this came from filial grief.

sentences.zh: 尋除給事黃門侍郎。

translations.literal: Soon he was appointed Attendant of the Yellow Gate.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was appointed Attendant of the Yellow Gate.

sentences.zh: 時領軍元叉威勢尤盛，凡有遷授，莫不造門謝謁。

translations.literal: At the time Commander of the Guards Yuan Cha's authority was especially great; whenever anyone received a transfer or appointment, none failed to visit his gate and offer thanks.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Yuan Cha, Commander of the Guards, was extremely powerful. Whenever anyone received a transfer or appointment, he went to Yuan Cha's gate to give thanks.

sentences.zh: 順拜表而已，曾不詣叉。

translations.literal: Shun merely submitted a memorial of thanks and never went to Cha.
translations.idiomatic: Shun merely submitted a memorial of thanks and never called on Yuan Cha.

sentences.zh: 叉謂順曰：「卿何謂聊不見我？」

translations.literal: Cha said to Shun, "What do you mean by not once coming to see me?"
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Cha said to Shun, "Why have you not come to see me at all?"

sentences.zh: 順正色曰：「天子富於春秋，委政宗輔，叔父宜以至公為心，舉士報國，如何賣恩，責人私謝，豈所望也！」

translations.literal: Shun said with a stern expression, "The Son of Heaven is young, and government is entrusted to clan assistants. Uncle should take utmost fairness as his heart, promote scholars, and repay the state. How can you sell favors and demand private thanks from people? This is not what one would hope."
translations.idiomatic: Shun answered sternly, "The Son of Heaven is young and has entrusted government to clan ministers. Uncle should act with perfect fairness, raise worthy men, and serve the state. How can you sell favors and demand private thanks? This is not what one expects."

sentences.zh: 至於朝論得失，順常鯁言正議，曾不阿旨，由此見憚。

translations.literal: As for gains and losses in court discussion, Shun always spoke chokingly direct words and upright arguments, never once flattering the intent; because of this he was feared.
translations.idiomatic: In court debates over right and wrong, Shun always spoke bluntly and argued uprightly, never bending to anyone's wishes; for this he was feared.

sentences.zh: 出除平北將軍、恒州刺史。

translations.literal: He was sent out and appointed General Who Pacifies the North and Inspector of Hengzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was sent out as General Who Pacifies the North and Inspector of Hengzhou.

sentences.zh: 順謂叉曰：「北鎮紛紜，方為國梗，桑乾舊都，根本所繫，請假都督，為國捍屏。」

translations.literal: Shun said to Cha, "The northern garrisons are in turmoil and are just now a blockage to the state. Sanggan and the old capital are tied to the root and base. I request temporary authority as commander-in-chief, to serve as shield and screen for the state."
translations.idiomatic: Shun told Yuan Cha, "The northern garrisons are in turmoil and threaten the state. Sanggan and the old capital are bound to our foundation. Give me temporary command, and I will serve as the state's shield."

sentences.zh: 叉心疑難，不欲授以兵官，謂順曰：「此朝廷之事，非我所裁。」

translations.literal: Cha suspected and found this difficult; not wishing to grant him a military office, he said to Shun, "This is the court's affair, not something I decide."
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Cha was suspicious and reluctant to give him a military post, so he said, "This is a court matter, not mine to decide."

sentences.zh: 順曰：「叔父既握國柄，殺生由己，自言天之歷數應在我躬，何得復有朝廷也！」

translations.literal: Shun said, "Since Uncle holds the handle of the state, killing and giving life come from yourself. You yourself say the heavenly calendar should be in your person; how can there again be a court?"
translations.idiomatic: Shun said, "Uncle holds state power, and life and death come from you. You yourself say Heaven's mandate should rest in your own person; how can there still be a court?"

sentences.zh: 叉彌忿憚之。

translations.literal: Cha grew still more angry and afraid of him.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Cha grew even angrier and more afraid of him.

sentences.zh: 轉為安東將軍、齊州刺史。

translations.literal: He was transferred to General Who Pacifies the East and Inspector of Qizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Shun was transferred to General Who Pacifies the East and Inspector of Qizhou.

sentences.zh: 順自負有才，不得居內，每懷鬱怏，形於言色，遂縱酒歡娛，不親政事。

translations.literal: Shun relied on his own talent, and because he could not remain inside the court, he always harbored resentment, which showed in his words and expression; he then indulged in wine and pleasure and did not attend personally to government affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Confident in his talent and unable to remain at court, Shun nursed resentment that showed in his face and speech. He then gave himself over to wine and amusement and neglected government.

sentences.zh: 叉解領軍，徵為給事黃門侍郎。

translations.literal: When Cha was relieved of the Guards command, Shun was summoned as Attendant of the Yellow Gate.
translations.idiomatic: When Yuan Cha was relieved of command of the Guards, Shun was summoned as Attendant of the Yellow Gate.

sentences.zh: 親友郊迎，賀其得入。

translations.literal: Relatives and friends met him in the suburbs and congratulated him on being able to enter.
translations.idiomatic: Relatives and friends met him in the suburbs and congratulated him on returning to court.

sentences.zh: 順曰：「不患不入，正恐入而復出耳。」

translations.literal: Shun said, "I do not worry about not entering; I only fear entering and then going out again."
translations.idiomatic: Shun said, "I am not worried about failing to enter; I only fear entering and then being sent out again."

sentences.zh: 俄兼殿中尚書，轉侍中。

translations.literal: Soon he concurrently served as Minister of the Palace and was transferred to Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he concurrently served as Minister of the Palace and was then transferred to Palace Attendant.

sentences.zh: 初，中山王熙起兵討元叉，不果而誅，及靈太后反政，方得改葬。

translations.literal: Earlier, Xi, Prince of Zhongshan, had raised troops to attack Yuan Cha; he failed and was executed. When Empress Dowager Ling returned to government, only then was he able to be reburied.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Xi, Prince of Zhongshan, had raised troops against Yuan Cha, failed, and been executed. Only after Empress Dowager Ling resumed power was he allowed reburial.

sentences.zh: 順侍坐西遊園，因奏太后曰：「臣昨往看中山家葬，非唯宗親哀其冤酷，行路士女，見其一家七喪，皆為澘然，莫不酸泣。」

translations.literal: Shun was sitting in attendance in the Western Tour Garden and thereupon memorialized to the Empress Dowager, "Yesterday I went to see the burial of Zhongshan's household. Not only did the imperial kin mourn their cruel wrong; men and women on the road, seeing seven funerals from one family, were all moved to tears and sobbed bitterly."
translations.idiomatic: While sitting in attendance in the Western Tour Garden, Shun said to the Empress Dowager, "Yesterday I went to see the burial of the Zhongshan household. Not only did the imperial kin mourn their cruel wrong; travelers, men and women alike, saw seven dead from one family and all wept bitterly."

sentences.zh: 叉妻時在太后側，順指之曰：「陛下奈何以一妹之故，不伏元叉之罪，使天下懷冤！」

translations.literal: Cha's wife was then at the Empress Dowager's side. Shun pointed to her and said, "How can Your Majesty, because of one younger sister, not punish Yuan Cha's crime, making all under Heaven harbor injustice?"
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Cha's wife was beside the Empress Dowager at the time. Shun pointed to her and said, "How can Your Majesty, for the sake of one sister, fail to punish Yuan Cha's crime and leave the whole realm nursing injustice?"

sentences.zh: 太后默然不語。

translations.literal: The Empress Dowager was silent and did not speak.
translations.idiomatic: The Empress Dowager was silent.

sentences.zh: 就德興反於營州，使尚書盧同往討之，大敗而返。

translations.literal: Jiu Dexing rebelled in Yingzhou, and the Department official Lu Tong was sent to attack him, but returned in great defeat.
translations.idiomatic: When Jiu Dexing rebelled in Yingzhou, Lu Tong of the Department was sent against him but returned after a major defeat.

sentences.zh: 屬侍中穆紹與順侍坐，因論同之罪。

translations.literal: It happened that Palace Attendant Mu Shao was sitting in attendance with Shun, and they discussed Tong's crime.
translations.idiomatic: Palace Attendant Mu Shao happened to be sitting in attendance with Shun, and they discussed Lu Tong's offense.

sentences.zh: 同先有近宅借紹，紹頗欲為言。

translations.literal: Tong previously had a nearby residence that he lent to Shao, and Shao rather wished to speak on his behalf.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Tong had earlier lent Shao a nearby residence, and Shao wanted to speak for him.

sentences.zh: 順勃然曰：「盧同終將無罪！」

translations.literal: Shun suddenly said, "Lu Tong in the end will have no crime!"
translations.idiomatic: Shun suddenly said, "Lu Tong will end up without guilt!"

sentences.zh: 太后曰：「何得如侍中之言？」

translations.literal: The Empress Dowager said, "How can it be as the Palace Attendant says?"
translations.idiomatic: The Empress Dowager said, "How can it be as the Palace Attendant says?"

sentences.zh: 順曰：「同有好宅與要勢侍中，豈慮罪也。」

translations.literal: Shun said, "Tong has a fine residence to give to an important and powerful Palace Attendant; why would he worry about guilt?"
translations.idiomatic: Shun replied, "Tong has a fine house to give a powerful Palace Attendant. Why should he worry about guilt?"

sentences.zh: 紹慚，不敢復言。

translations.literal: Shao was ashamed and did not dare speak again.
translations.idiomatic: Shao was ashamed and did not dare speak again.

sentences.zh: 靈太后頗事妝飾，數出遊幸。

translations.literal: Empress Dowager Ling rather occupied herself with adornment and often went out on pleasure tours.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Dowager Ling was much occupied with adornment and often went out on excursions.

sentences.zh: 順面諍曰：「禮，婦人夫喪，自稱未亡人，首去珠玉，衣不被綵。

translations.literal: Shun remonstrated to her face, saying, "According to ritual, when a woman's husband has died, she calls herself the one not yet dead, removes pearls and jade from her head, and does not wear colored garments.
translations.idiomatic: Shun remonstrated with her directly: "According to ritual, when a woman loses her husband she calls herself the one not yet dead, removes pearls and jade from her hair, and does not wear colored clothing.

sentences.zh: 陛下母臨天下，年垂不惑，過甚修飾，何以示後世？」

translations.literal: Your Majesty mothers all under Heaven and is nearly forty, yet you excessively cultivate adornment. How will you show yourself to later generations?"
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty rules the realm as mother and is nearly forty, yet you adorn yourself excessively. What example does this show later generations?"

sentences.zh: 靈太后慚而不出。

translations.literal: Empress Dowager Ling was ashamed and did not go out.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Dowager Ling was ashamed and stopped going out.

sentences.zh: 還入宮，責順曰：「千里相徵，豈欲眾中見辱也！」

translations.literal: After returning to the palace, she reproached Shun, saying, "I summoned you from a thousand li away; did I mean to be humiliated before the crowd?"
translations.idiomatic: When she returned to the palace, she rebuked Shun: "I summoned you from a thousand li away; did you intend to shame me in public?"

sentences.zh: 順曰：「陛下盛服炫容，不畏天下所笑，何耻臣之一言乎？」

translations.literal: Shun said, "Your Majesty wears splendid robes and dazzles with your appearance, yet does not fear the laughter of all under Heaven. Why be ashamed of one word from me?"
translations.idiomatic: Shun replied, "Your Majesty dresses splendidly and displays your beauty without fearing the laughter of the realm. Why be ashamed of one word from me?"

sentences.zh: 初，城陽王徽慕順才名，偏相結納。

translations.literal: Earlier, Hui, Prince of Chengyang, admired Shun's talent and reputation and especially befriended and received him.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Hui, Prince of Chengyang, admired Shun's talent and reputation and made special efforts to befriend him.

sentences.zh: 而廣陽王淵姦徽妻于氏，大為嫌隙。

translations.literal: But Yuan, Prince of Guangyang, committed adultery with Hui's wife, Lady Yu, creating a great rift.
translations.idiomatic: But Yuan, Prince of Guangyang, had an affair with Hui's wife Lady Yu, creating a deep rift.

sentences.zh: 及淵自定州被徵，入為吏部尚書，兼中領軍。

translations.literal: When Yuan was summoned from Dingzhou and entered as Minister of Personnel, concurrently Central Commander of the Guards,
translations.idiomatic: When Yuan was summoned from Dingzhou to serve as Minister of Personnel and concurrently Central Commander of the Guards,

sentences.zh: 順為詔書，辭頗優美。

translations.literal: Shun drafted the edict for him, and its wording was quite excellent.
translations.idiomatic: Shun drafted the edict for him in notably elegant language.

sentences.zh: 徽疑順為淵左右，由是與徐紇間順於靈太后，出順為護軍將軍、太常卿。

translations.literal: Hui suspected Shun of siding with Yuan, and because of this, together with Xu He, he alienated Shun from Empress Dowager Ling; Shun was sent out as General Who Protects the Army and Chamberlain for Ceremonials.
translations.idiomatic: Hui suspected Shun of favoring Yuan, so he and Xu He slandered Shun to Empress Dowager Ling. Shun was sent out as General Who Protects the Army and Chamberlain for Ceremonials.

sentences.zh: 順奉辭於西遊園，徽紇侍側，順指之謂靈太后曰：「此人魏之宰嚭，魏國不滅，終不死亡。」

translations.literal: Shun took leave in the Western Tour Garden, with Hui and He standing in attendance at the side. Shun pointed to them and said to Empress Dowager Ling, "This man is Wei's Zai Pi; if the state of Wei is not destroyed, he will never die."
translations.idiomatic: Shun took leave in the Western Tour Garden while Hui and Xu He stood at the side. Pointing at Xu He, he said to Empress Dowager Ling, "This man is Wei's Zai Pi. Unless Wei is destroyed, he will never die."

sentences.zh: 紇脅肩而出。

translations.literal: He went out with his shoulders hunched.
translations.idiomatic: Xu He went out with his shoulders hunched.

sentences.zh: 順遂抗聲叱之曰：「爾刀筆小人，正堪為几案之吏，寧應忝茲執戟，虧我彝倫！」

translations.literal: Shun then raised his voice and rebuked him, saying, "You petty knife-and-brush man are fit only to be a desk clerk. How could you shamefully hold this halberd and damage our proper human relations!"
translations.idiomatic: Shun then shouted after him, "You petty clerk with knife and brush are fit only for desk work. How can you presume to hold a halberd here and disgrace our proper order!"

sentences.zh: 遂振衣而起。

translations.literal: He then shook out his robe and rose.
translations.idiomatic: He shook out his robe and rose.

sentences.zh: 靈太后默而不言。

translations.literal: Empress Dowager Ling was silent and did not speak.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Dowager Ling said nothing.

sentences.zh: 時追論順父顧託之功，增任城王彝邑二千戶，又析彝邑五百戶以封順，為東阿縣開國公。

translations.literal: At the time the court was retrospectively discussing the merit of Shun's father in receiving the testamentary charge. It increased the fief of Yi, Prince of Rencheng, by two thousand households, and also divided five hundred households from Yi's fief to enfeoff Shun as Founding Duke of Dong'e County.
translations.idiomatic: At the time the court was reviewing the merit of Shun's father in the imperial entrustment. Yi, Prince of Rencheng, received two thousand additional households, and five hundred households were carved from Yi's fief to enfeoff Shun as Founding Duke of Dong'e County.

sentences.zh: 順疾徽等間之，遂為蠅賦曰：「余以仲秋休沐，端坐衡門，寄想琴書，託情紙翰，而蒼蠅小蟲，往來牀几，疾其變白，聊為賦云：遐哉大道，廓矣洪氛。

translations.literal: Shun hated that Hui and the others had alienated him, and so he composed a Rhapsody on Flies, saying, "In mid-autumn, while resting from office, I sat upright by my humble gate, setting my thoughts on zither and books and entrusting my feelings to paper and brush; but the small insects, the bluebottle flies, came and went over bed and table. Hating how they change white, I have briefly made a rhapsody, saying: Vast is the great Way, broad the primal vapor.
translations.idiomatic: Shun hated Hui and the others for slandering him, and so he wrote a Rhapsody on Flies: "In mid-autumn, resting from office, I sat quietly at my humble gate, my thoughts on zither and books and my feelings entrusted to paper and brush. But tiny bluebottle flies came and went over bed and table. Hating how they transform white, I have made this rhapsody: Vast is the great Way, broad the primal vapor.

sentences.zh: 肇立秋夏，爰啟冬春。

translations.literal: It first established autumn and summer, and then opened winter and spring.
translations.idiomatic: It first set autumn and summer in place, then opened winter and spring.

sentences.zh: 既含育於萬性，又芻狗而不仁。

translations.literal: It both contains and nurtures the ten thousand natures, and yet, like straw dogs, is not benevolent.
translations.idiomatic: It contains and nurtures all natures, yet like straw dogs it is not benevolent.

sentences.zh: 隨因緣以授體，齊美惡而無分。

translations.literal: Following causes and conditions, it grants bodies, equalizing beautiful and ugly without distinction.
translations.idiomatic: Following conditions, it grants bodies, making no distinction between fair and foul.

sentences.zh: 生茲穢類，靡益於人。

translations.literal: It gives birth to this filthy kind, with no benefit to human beings.
translations.idiomatic: Thus this filthy kind is born, bringing no benefit to people.

sentences.zh: 名備羣品，聲損眾倫。

translations.literal: Its name is included among the many creatures, but its sound damages all relations.
translations.idiomatic: Its name is counted among living things, but its buzzing harms the order of all beings.

sentences.zh: 欹脛纖翼，紫首蒼身。

translations.literal: Crooked shins and slender wings, purple heads and blue bodies.
translations.idiomatic: Crooked legs, slender wings, purple heads, blue bodies.

sentences.zh: 飛不能迥，聲若遠聞。

translations.literal: It cannot fly far, but its sound seems heard from afar.
translations.idiomatic: It cannot fly far, yet its noise seems to carry into the distance.

sentences.zh: 點緇成素，變白為黑。

translations.literal: It dots black and makes white; it changes white into black.
translations.idiomatic: It spots black onto white and turns white into black.

sentences.zh: 寡愛蘭芳，偏貪穢食。

translations.literal: It has little love for orchid fragrance and is especially greedy for filthy food.
translations.idiomatic: It cares little for orchid fragrance and craves filthy food.

sentences.zh: 集桓公之屍，居平叔之側。

translations.literal: It gathered on Duke Huan's corpse and dwelt by Pingshu's side.
translations.idiomatic: It gathered on Duke Huan's corpse and lingered at Pingshu's side.

sentences.zh: 亂鷄鳴之響，毀皇宮之飾。

translations.literal: It disordered the sound of the cockcrow and ruined the ornaments of the imperial palace.
translations.idiomatic: It confused the sound of the cockcrow and defiled the ornaments of the imperial palace.

sentences.zh: 習習戶庭，營營榛棘。

translations.literal: Fluttering through doors and courtyards, buzzing among thorns and brambles.
translations.idiomatic: Fluttering through doors and courtyards, buzzing among thorns and brambles.

sentences.zh: 反覆往還，譬彼讒賊。

translations.literal: Back and forth it goes and returns, like those slanderous rebels.
translations.idiomatic: Back and forth it comes and goes, like slanderous traitors.

sentences.zh: 膚受既通，譖潤罔極。

translations.literal: Once skin-deep slander gets through, soaking accusations have no limit.
translations.idiomatic: Once slander penetrates the skin, its soaking accusations know no limit.

sentences.zh: 緝緝幡幡，交亂四國。

translations.literal: Whispering and fluttering, they cross and disorder the four states.
translations.idiomatic: Whispering and fluttering, they throw the four quarters into disorder.

sentences.zh: 於是妖姬進，邪士來，聖賢擁，忠孝摧。

translations.literal: Thereupon seductive women advance, wicked men come, sages and worthies are blocked, and the loyal and filial are crushed.
translations.idiomatic: Then seductive women advance, wicked men arrive, sages and worthies are blocked, and the loyal and filial are crushed.

sentences.zh: 周昌拘於牖里，天乙囚於夏臺。

translations.literal: Zhou Chang was confined at Youli, and Tianyi was imprisoned at Xiatai.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Chang was confined at Youli, and Tianyi imprisoned at Xiatai.

sentences.zh: 伯奇為之痛結，申生為之蒙災。

translations.literal: Boqi was knotted in pain by them, and Shensheng was covered with disaster by them.
translations.idiomatic: Boqi was bound in grief because of them, and Shensheng was overtaken by disaster because of them.

sentences.zh: 鴟鴞悲其室，採葛懼其懷。

translations.literal: The Owl grieved for its house, and Gathering Kudzu feared what was in the heart.
translations.idiomatic: The Owl lamented its ruined house, and Gathering Kudzu feared what lay in the heart.

sentences.zh: 小弁隕其涕，靈均表其哀。

translations.literal: Xiaobian shed its tears, and Lingjun displayed his sorrow.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaobian shed tears, and Lingjun made his sorrow known.

sentences.zh: 自古明哲猶如此，何況中庸與凡才。

translations.literal: From antiquity, the enlightened and wise were still like this; how much more the middling and ordinary talents?
translations.idiomatic: Even the enlightened and wise of antiquity suffered so; how much more men of middling or ordinary talent?

sentences.zh: 若夫天生地養，各有所親。

translations.literal: As for what Heaven gives birth to and Earth nourishes, each has what it is close to.
translations.idiomatic: As for the beings Heaven gives birth to and Earth nourishes, each has its proper affinities.

sentences.zh: 獸必依地，鳥亦憑雲。

translations.literal: Beasts must rely on the earth, and birds also depend on the clouds.
translations.idiomatic: Beasts rely on the earth, and birds depend on the clouds.

sentences.zh: 或來儀以呈祉，或自擾而見文。

translations.literal: Some come in ritual display to present blessings; some are tamed and show patterned beauty.
translations.idiomatic: Some come in stately display to present blessings; some are domesticated and display patterned beauty.

sentences.zh: 或負圖而歸德，或銜書以告真。

translations.literal: Some bear diagrams and return to virtue; some hold writings in their mouths and announce the true.
translations.idiomatic: Some bear diagrams and return to virtue; some carry writings in their mouths to reveal the true.

sentences.zh: 或夭胎而奉味，或殘軀以獻珍。

translations.literal: Some are cut short in the womb to offer flavor; some offer preciousness with damaged bodies.
translations.idiomatic: Some are taken before birth to provide flavor; some, with damaged bodies, offer delicacies.

sentences.zh: 或主皮而興禮，或牢豢以供神。

translations.literal: Some, as hides, promote ritual; some, as stall-fed animals, supply the spirits.
translations.idiomatic: Some, as hides, give rise to ritual; some, as sacrificial animals, serve the spirits.

sentences.zh: 雖死生之異質，俱有益於國人。

translations.literal: Although dead and living are different in substance, all are of benefit to the people of the state.
translations.idiomatic: Though they differ as living and dead, all benefit the people of the state.

sentences.zh: 非如蒼蠅之無用，唯構亂於蒸民。」

translations.literal: They are not like the bluebottle fly, which is useless and only constructs disorder among the multitudes."
translations.idiomatic: They are not like the bluebottle fly, useless and only sowing disorder among the people."

sentences.zh: 遂屬疾在家，杜絕慶弔。

translations.literal: He then became ill at home and cut off congratulations and condolences.
translations.idiomatic: He then fell ill at home and refused all visits of congratulation or condolence.

sentences.zh: 後除吏部尚書，兼右僕射。

translations.literal: Later he was appointed Minister of Personnel and concurrently Right Vice Director.
translations.idiomatic: Later he was appointed Minister of Personnel and concurrently Right Vice Director.

sentences.zh: 及上省，登階向榻，見榻甚故，問都令史徐仵起。

translations.literal: When he went up to the Department, climbed the steps toward the couch, and saw that the couch was very old, he asked the Chief Clerk Xu Wuqi about it.
translations.idiomatic: When he went up to the Department and approached the couch, he saw that it was very old and asked Chief Clerk Xu Wuqi about it.

sentences.zh: 仵起曰：「此榻曾經先王坐。」

translations.literal: Wuqi said, "This couch was once sat on by the former king."
translations.idiomatic: Wuqi said, "The former prince once sat on this couch."

sentences.zh: 順即哽塞，涕泗交流，久而不能言，遂令換之。

translations.literal: Shun immediately choked up, tears and mucus flowing together; for a long while he could not speak, and he then ordered it changed.
translations.idiomatic: Shun immediately choked up, tears streaming down; for a long while he could not speak, and then ordered the couch replaced.

sentences.zh: 時三公曹令史朱暉，素事錄尚書、高陽王雍，雍欲以為廷尉評，頻請託順，順不為用。

translations.literal: At the time Zhu Hui, a clerk in the Bureau of the Three Excellencies, had long served Yong, Recording Director of the Department and Prince of Gaoyang. Yong wished to make him an Evaluator in the Court of Justice and repeatedly asked and entrusted Shun, but Shun would not employ him.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Zhu Hui, a clerk in the Bureau of the Three Excellencies, had long served Yuan Yong, Prince of Gaoyang and Recording Director of the Department. Yong wanted to make him an Evaluator in the Court of Justice and repeatedly pressed Shun, but Shun refused to use him.

sentences.zh: 雍遂下命用之，順投之於地。

translations.literal: Yong then issued an order to use him, and Shun threw it on the ground.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Yong then issued an order appointing him, and Shun threw it on the ground.

sentences.zh: 雍聞之，大怒，昧爽坐都廳，召尚書及丞郎畢集，欲待順至，於眾挫之。

translations.literal: When Yong heard of this, he was furious. At dawn he sat in the metropolitan hall and summoned the Ministers, Aides, and Gentlemen to assemble completely, intending to wait for Shun to arrive and humiliate him before the crowd.
translations.idiomatic: When Yong heard, he was furious. At dawn he sat in the metropolitan hall and summoned all the Ministers, Aides, and Gentlemen, intending to humiliate Shun publicly when he arrived.

sentences.zh: 順日高方至，雍攘袂撫几而言曰：「身，天子之子，天子之弟，天子之叔，天子之相，四海之內，親尊莫二，元順何人，以身成命，投棄於地！」

translations.literal: Only when the sun was high did Shun arrive. Yong rolled up his sleeves, struck the armrest, and said, "I am son of the Son of Heaven, brother of the Son of Heaven, uncle of the Son of Heaven, and minister of the Son of Heaven. Within the four seas none is closer or more honored. What sort of man is Yuan Shun, to take an order completed by me and throw it away on the ground!"
translations.idiomatic: Shun arrived only when the sun was high. Yong rolled up his sleeves, struck the table, and said, "I am the Son of Heaven's son, brother, uncle, and chief minister. Within the four seas no one is closer or more honored. Who is Yuan Shun, to take my completed order and throw it on the ground!"

sentences.zh: 順鬚鬢俱張，仰面看屋，憤氣奔涌，長歔而不言。

translations.literal: Shun's beard and temples both bristled; he raised his face and looked at the roof, angry breath surging, and sighed long without speaking.
translations.idiomatic: Shun's beard and temples bristled. He looked up at the rafters, anger surging, and gave a long sigh without speaking.

sentences.zh: 久之，搖一白羽扇，徐而謂雍曰：「高祖遷宅中土，創定九流，官方清濁，軌儀萬古。

translations.literal: After a long while, he waved a white feather fan and slowly said to Yong, "Gaozu moved his residence to the central lands and first fixed the nine ranks; offices were divided into pure and impure, a model for ten thousand ages.
translations.idiomatic: After a long while, he waved a white feather fan and slowly said to Yong, "Gaozu moved the capital to the central lands and established the nine ranks; he distinguished pure and impure offices, setting a model for all ages.

sentences.zh: 而朱暉小子，身為省吏，何合為廷尉清官！

translations.literal: Yet Zhu Hui is a petty man, himself a department clerk. How is he fit for a pure office in the Court of Justice?
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Hui is a petty man, a mere Department clerk. How is he fit for a pure office in the Court of Justice?

sentences.zh: 殿下既先皇同氣，宜遵成旨，自有短垣而復踰之也。」

translations.literal: Since Your Highness is of the same breath as the former emperor, you should follow the completed decree. There is already a low wall, and yet you overstep it again."
translations.idiomatic: Your Highness shares the late emperor's blood and should follow the established decree. Even a low wall is still a boundary; why overstep it again?"

sentences.zh: 雍曰：「身為丞相、錄尚書，如何不得用一人為官？」

translations.literal: Yong said, "I am Chancellor and Recording Director of the Department of State Affairs; how can I not be allowed to use one man as an official?"
translations.idiomatic: Yong said, "I am Chancellor and Recording Director of the Department. How can I not appoint one man to office?"

sentences.zh: 順曰：「庖人雖不治庖，尸祝不得越樽俎而代之。

translations.literal: Shun said, "Though the cook does not manage the kitchen, the invocator may not step past the wine vessels and stands to replace him.
translations.idiomatic: Shun replied, "Even if the cook does not manage the kitchen, the invocator may not step beyond the vessels and stands to take his place.

sentences.zh: 未聞有別旨，令殿下參選事。」

translations.literal: I have not heard of a separate decree ordering Your Highness to take part in selection affairs."
translations.idiomatic: I have heard of no separate edict ordering Your Highness to take part in personnel selection."

sentences.zh: 順又厲聲曰：「殿下必如是，順當依事奏聞！」

translations.literal: Shun again said in a stern voice, "If Your Highness insists on being like this, I shall memorialize the matter according to the facts!"
translations.idiomatic: Shun then said sharply, "If Your Highness insists, I will memorialize the matter according to the facts!"

sentences.zh: 雍遂笑而言曰：「豈可以朱暉小人，便相忿恨。」

translations.literal: Yong then laughed and said, "How could we become angry with each other over a petty man like Zhu Hui?"
translations.idiomatic: Yong then laughed. "How could we become angry with one another over a petty man like Zhu Hui?"

sentences.zh: 遂起，呼順入室，與之極飲。

translations.literal: He then rose, called Shun into the inner room, and drank with him to the utmost.
translations.idiomatic: He rose, called Shun inside, and drank with him to the fullest.

sentences.zh: 順之亢毅不撓，皆此類也。

translations.literal: Shun's lofty firmness and refusal to bend were all of this kind.
translations.idiomatic: Shun's lofty firmness and refusal to bend were all of this sort.

sentences.zh: 後除征南將軍、右光祿大夫，轉兼左僕射。

translations.literal: Later he was appointed General Who Conquers the South and Right Guanglu Grandee, and was transferred to concurrently serve as Left Vice Director.
translations.idiomatic: Later he was appointed General Who Conquers the South and Right Guanglu Grandee, then transferred to concurrently serve as Left Vice Director.

sentences.zh: 爾朱榮之奉莊帝，召百官悉至河陰，素聞順數諫諍，惜其亮直，謂朱瑞曰：「可語元僕射，但在省，不須來。」

translations.literal: When Erzhu Rong received Emperor Zhuang, he summoned all the officials to Heyin. He had long heard that Shun had repeatedly remonstrated and argued, and he cherished his bright uprightness, so he said to Zhu Rui, "You may tell Vice Director Yuan only to remain in the Department; he need not come."
translations.idiomatic: When Erzhu Rong received Emperor Zhuang, he summoned all officials to Heyin. Having long heard that Shun often remonstrated and valuing his clear integrity, he told Zhu Rui, "Tell Vice Director Yuan to stay in the Department; he need not come."

sentences.zh: 順不達其旨，聞害衣冠，遂便出走，為陵戶鮮于康奴所害。

translations.literal: Shun did not understand his intent. Hearing that the officials were being harmed, he immediately fled and was killed by Xianyu Kangnu, a tomb household man.
translations.idiomatic: Shun did not understand the warning. Hearing that the officials were being slaughtered, he fled and was killed by Xianyu Kangnu, a tomb-household man.

sentences.zh: 家徒四壁，無物斂屍，止有書數千卷而已。

translations.literal: His house had only four bare walls, and there was nothing with which to enshroud the corpse; there were only several thousand scrolls of books.
translations.idiomatic: His house was bare, with nothing to shroud his body; it contained only several thousand scrolls of books.

sentences.zh: 門下通事令史王才達裂裳覆之。

translations.literal: Wang Caida, Clerk for Communications under the Gate, tore his garment to cover him.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Caida, Clerk for Communications under the Gate, tore his robe to cover the body.

sentences.zh: 莊帝還宮，遣黃門侍郎山偉巡喻京邑。

translations.literal: When Emperor Zhuang returned to the palace, he sent Yellow Gate Attendant Shan Wei to tour and reassure the capital.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Zhuang returned to the palace, he sent Yellow Gate Attendant Shan Wei to tour the capital and reassure it.

sentences.zh: 偉臨順喪，悲慟無已。

translations.literal: Wei came to Shun's funeral and grieved without cease.
translations.idiomatic: Shan Wei visited Shun's mourning place and wept without stopping.

sentences.zh: 既還，莊帝怪而問曰：「黃門何為聲散？」

translations.literal: After he returned, Emperor Zhuang was surprised and asked, "Why is the Yellow Gate's voice broken?"
translations.idiomatic: When he returned, Emperor Zhuang was surprised and asked, "Why is the Yellow Gate attendant's voice hoarse?"

sentences.zh: 偉以狀對。

translations.literal: Wei answered with the circumstances.
translations.idiomatic: Shan Wei told him what had happened.

sentences.zh: 莊帝敕侍中元祉曰：「宗室喪亡非一，不可周贍。

translations.literal: Emperor Zhuang ordered Palace Attendant Yuan Zhi, "There is more than one death in the imperial clan, and they cannot all be fully provided for.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Zhuang instructed Palace Attendant Yuan Zhi, "Many members of the imperial clan have died, and we cannot provide fully for all of them.

sentences.zh: 元僕射清苦之節，死乃益彰，特贈絹百匹，餘不得例。」

translations.literal: The austere integrity of Vice Director Yuan is only more manifest in death. Specially grant him one hundred bolts of silk; the rest may not follow this as precedent."
translations.idiomatic: Vice Director Yuan's austere integrity shines even more in death. Grant him one hundred bolts of silk as a special gift; let this not become precedent for the others."

sentences.zh: 贈驃騎大將軍、尚書令、司徒公、定州刺史，諡曰文烈。

translations.literal: He was posthumously granted Grand General of Agile Cavalry, Director of the Department of State Affairs, Minister over the Masses, and Inspector of Dingzhou, with the posthumous title Wenlie.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously granted Grand General of Agile Cavalry, Director of the Department of State Affairs, Minister over the Masses, and Inspector of Dingzhou, and was given the posthumous title Wenlie.

sentences.zh: 順撰帝錄二十卷，詩賦表頌數十篇，今多亡失。

translations.literal: Shun compiled Imperial Records in twenty fascicles, as well as several tens of poems, rhapsodies, memorials, and eulogies; most are now lost.
translations.idiomatic: Shun compiled Imperial Records in twenty fascicles and wrote several dozen poems, rhapsodies, memorials, and eulogies, most of which are now lost.

sentences.zh: 長子朗，時年十七。

translations.literal: His eldest son Lang was seventeen at the time.
translations.idiomatic: His eldest son Lang was seventeen at the time.

sentences.zh: 枕戈潛伏積年，乃手刃康奴，以首祭於順墓，然後詣闕請罪。

translations.literal: He slept on his spear and hid in secret for years, then personally killed Kangnu, sacrificed the head at Shun's tomb, and only afterward went to the palace gate to confess his crime.
translations.idiomatic: For years he slept on his spear and hid in secret. Then he killed Kangnu with his own hand, offered the head at Shun's tomb, and afterward went to the palace gate to confess.

sentences.zh: 朝廷嘉而不問。

translations.literal: The court praised him and did not prosecute.
translations.idiomatic: The court praised him and did not punish him.

sentences.zh: 朗涉歷書記，為司徒屬。

translations.literal: Lang had experience in documents and records and served as an attendant to the Minister over the Masses.
translations.idiomatic: Lang was experienced in documents and records and served as an attendant to the Minister over the Masses.

sentences.zh: 天平中，為奴所害。

translations.literal: In the Tianping era, he was killed by a slave.
translations.idiomatic: In the Tianping era, he was killed by a slave.

sentences.zh: 贈都督瀛冀二州諸軍事、□□將軍、尚書右僕射、冀州刺史。

translations.literal: He was posthumously granted Commander of all military affairs in Ying and Ji provinces, General with title missing, Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs, and Inspector of Jizhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously granted Commander of all military affairs in Ying and Ji provinces, an unspecified generalship, Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs, and Inspector of Jizhou.

sentences.zh: 順弟淑，淑弟悲，並早卒。

translations.literal: Shun's younger brother Shu and Shu's younger brother Bei both died young.
translations.idiomatic: Shun's younger brother Shu and Shu's younger brother Bei both died young.

sentences.zh: 悲弟紀，字子綱。

translations.literal: Bei's younger brother Ji was styled Zigang.
translations.idiomatic: Bei's younger brother Ji was styled Zigang.

sentences.zh: 永熙中，給事黃門侍郎。

translations.literal: In the Yongxi era, he was Attendant of the Yellow Gate.
translations.idiomatic: In the Yongxi era he served as Attendant of the Yellow Gate.

sentences.zh: 隨出帝，沒於關中。

translations.literal: He followed the Emperor Who Went Out and died in Guanzhong.
translations.idiomatic: He followed the Emperor Who Went Out and died in Guanzhong.

sentences.zh: 澄弟嵩，字道岳。

translations.literal: Cheng's younger brother Song was styled Daoyue.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng's younger brother Song was styled Daoyue.

sentences.zh: 高祖時，自中大夫遷員外常侍，轉步兵校尉。

translations.literal: In Gaozu's time, he was transferred from Palace Grandee to Regular Attendant Outside the Ranks, then transferred to Infantry Commandant.
translations.idiomatic: In Gaozu's time he moved from Palace Grandee to Regular Attendant Outside the Ranks, then became Infantry Commandant.

sentences.zh: 大司馬、安定王休薨，未及卒哭，嵩便遊田。

translations.literal: When Xiu, Grand Marshal and Prince of Anding, died, before the final wailing had been completed, Song immediately went hunting.
translations.idiomatic: When Xiu, Grand Marshal and Prince of Anding, died, Song went hunting before the mourning rites had even ended.

sentences.zh: 高祖聞而大怒，詔曰：「嵩不能克己復禮，企心典憲，大司馬薨殂甫爾，便以鷹鷂自娛。

translations.literal: When Gaozu heard of this, he was furious and issued an edict: "Song cannot overcome himself and return to ritual or set his mind on standards and laws. The Grand Marshal has only just died, and he immediately amuses himself with hawks and sparrowhawks.
translations.idiomatic: When Gaozu heard, he was furious and issued an edict: "Song cannot master himself and return to ritual or set his mind on law and precedent. The Grand Marshal has only just died, and already he amuses himself with hawks and falcons.

sentences.zh: 有如父之痛，無猶子之情，捐心棄禮，何其太速！

translations.literal: He has pain as though for a father, but lacks the feeling of a nephew; he casts aside feeling and abandons ritual. How far too quick this is!
translations.idiomatic: He should feel pain as for a father, yet he lacks even a nephew's feeling; he casts aside feeling and abandons ritual. How terribly hasty!

sentences.zh: 便可免官。」

translations.literal: He may be dismissed from office."
translations.idiomatic: He may be dismissed from office."

sentences.zh: 後從平沔北，累有戰功，除左中郎將，兼武衞將軍。

translations.literal: Later he followed in pacifying north of the Mian, repeatedly had battle merits, and was appointed Left Gentleman General of the Center, concurrently General of the Martial Guard.
translations.idiomatic: Later he took part in pacifying the north of the Mian, repeatedly earned battle merit, and was appointed Left Gentleman General of the Center, concurrently General of the Martial Guard.

sentences.zh: 高祖南伐，蕭寶卷將陳顯達率眾拒戰。

translations.literal: When Gaozu campaigned south, Xiao Baojuan's general Chen Xianda led troops to resist in battle.
translations.idiomatic: When Gaozu campaigned south, Xiao Baojuan's general Chen Xianda led troops to resist him.

sentences.zh: 嵩身備三仗，免冑直前，將士從之，顯達奔潰，斬獲萬計。

translations.literal: Song himself was equipped with three weapons, removed his helmet, and advanced straight ahead. The officers and soldiers followed him, Xianda fled in collapse, and beheadings and captures were counted by the ten thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Song armed himself with three weapons, removed his helmet, and advanced straight ahead. The officers and soldiers followed; Xianda's forces fled in collapse, and the dead and captured numbered in the tens of thousands.

sentences.zh: 嵩於爾日勇冠三軍。

translations.literal: On that day Song's courage topped the three armies.
translations.idiomatic: That day, Song's courage surpassed the whole army.

sentences.zh: 高祖大悅而言曰：「任城康王大有褔德，文武頓出其門。」

translations.literal: Gaozu was greatly pleased and said, "Prince Kang of Rencheng has great fortune and virtue; civil and martial talent have suddenly emerged from his gate."
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu was delighted. "Prince Kang of Rencheng had great fortune and virtue; civil and martial talent have both burst from his household."

sentences.zh: 以功賜爵高平縣侯，賚帛二千五百匹。

translations.literal: For his merit he was granted the title Marquis of Gaoping County and given two thousand five hundred bolts of silk.
translations.idiomatic: For his merit he was granted the title Marquis of Gaoping County and awarded twenty-five hundred bolts of silk.

sentences.zh: 初，高祖之發洛也，馮皇后以罪幽於宮內。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Gaozu departed Luoyang, Empress Feng had been confined inside the palace for an offense.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when Gaozu left Luoyang, Empress Feng had been confined inside the palace for an offense.

sentences.zh: 既平顯達，回次穀唐原，高祖疾甚，將賜后死，曰：「使人不易可得。」

translations.literal: After Xianda had been pacified, on the return they stopped at Gutangyuan. Gaozu was gravely ill and was about to grant the empress death, saying, "A suitable envoy is not easy to obtain."
translations.idiomatic: After Xianda was defeated, Gaozu stopped on the return at Gutangyuan. Gravely ill, he was about to order the empress to die and said, "A suitable envoy is not easy to find."

sentences.zh: 顧謂任城王澄曰：「任城必不負我，嵩亦當不負任城，可使嵩也。」

translations.literal: He looked back and said to Cheng, Prince of Rencheng, "Rencheng will surely not fail me, and Song will also not fail Rencheng. Song may be sent."
translations.idiomatic: He turned to Cheng, Prince of Rencheng: "Rencheng will not fail me, and Song will not fail Rencheng. Send Song."

sentences.zh: 於是引嵩入內，親詔遣之。

translations.literal: Thereupon Song was brought inside, and Gaozu personally issued an edict dispatching him.
translations.idiomatic: Song was then brought inside, and Gaozu personally ordered him dispatched.

sentences.zh: 世宗即位，以武衞將軍兼侍中，出為平南將軍、荊州刺史。

translations.literal: When Shizong took the throne, Song served as General of the Martial Guard concurrently Palace Attendant, and was sent out as General Who Pacifies the South and Inspector of Jingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When Shizong ascended the throne, Song served as General of the Martial Guard and concurrently Palace Attendant, then was sent out as General Who Pacifies the South and Inspector of Jingzhou.

sentences.zh: 嵩表曰：「蕭寶卷骨肉相殘，忠良先戮，臣下囂然，莫不離背，君臣攜貳，干戈日尋。

translations.literal: Song memorialized, "Xiao Baojuan's own flesh and blood harm one another, loyal and good men are first killed, his ministers are in uproar, and none fails to leave and turn away. Ruler and ministers are divided, and weapons are sought daily.
translations.idiomatic: Song memorialized, "Xiao Baojuan slaughters his own kin and kills loyal men first. His ministers are in uproar and all are turning from him. Ruler and ministers are divided, and war grows daily.

sentences.zh: 流聞寶卷雍州刺史蕭衍兄懿於建業阻兵，與寶卷相持，荊郢二州刺史並是寶卷之弟，必有圖衍之志。

translations.literal: I have heard it said that Xiao Yi, elder brother of Baojuan's Inspector of Yongzhou Xiao Yan, is holding troops at Jianye and opposing Baojuan, while the Inspectors of Jingzhou and Yingzhou are both Baojuan's younger brothers and surely intend to scheme against Yan.
translations.idiomatic: I have heard that Xiao Yi, elder brother of Xiao Yan, Baojuan's Inspector of Yongzhou, is holding troops at Jianye against Baojuan; the Inspectors of Jingzhou and Yingzhou are both Baojuan's younger brothers and surely plan to move against Yan.

sentences.zh: 臣若遣書相聞，迎其本謀，冀獲同心，并力除衍。

translations.literal: If I send letters to communicate with them and meet their original plan, I hope to obtain common purpose and combine strength to eliminate Yan.
translations.idiomatic: If I send letters and meet them in their own plans, we may act with one mind and combine forces to eliminate Yan.

sentences.zh: 平衍之後，彼必旋師赴救丹陽，當不能復經營疆陲，全固襄沔。

translations.literal: After Yan is pacified, they will surely turn their armies back to rescue Danyang, and then will no longer be able to manage the frontier and fully secure Xiang and Mian.
translations.idiomatic: Once Yan is pacified, they will have to turn back to rescue Danyang and will no longer be able to manage the frontier or secure Xiang and Mian.

sentences.zh: 臣之軍威已得臨據，則沔南之地可一舉而收。

translations.literal: If my army's power has already reached and occupied a commanding position, then the land south of the Mian can be taken in one move.
translations.idiomatic: If our army has already established a commanding position, the land south of the Mian can be taken in a single move.

sentences.zh: 緣漢曜兵，示以威德，思歸有道者則引而納之，受疑告危者則援而接之。

translations.literal: By displaying troops along the Han and showing them awe and virtue, those who think of returning to the Way can be drawn in and received, and those who are under suspicion and report danger can be aided and accepted.
translations.idiomatic: If we display troops along the Han and show both power and virtue, those who wish to return to the Way can be welcomed, and those in danger under suspicion can be rescued and received.

sentences.zh: 總兵竚銳，觀釁伺隙，若其零落之形已彰，怠懈之勢已著，便可順流摧鋒，長驅席卷。」

translations.literal: With the army gathered and its edge held ready, we can observe rifts and wait for openings. If their form of collapse is already clear and their slackened condition already manifest, then we can follow the current, crush their front, drive deep, and roll them up like a mat."
translations.idiomatic: With troops gathered and ready, we can watch for cracks and openings. Once their collapse is clear and their slackness plain, we can move with the current, break their front, drive deep, and sweep them up like a mat."

sentences.zh: 詔曰：「所陳嘉謀，深是良計。

translations.literal: The edict said, "The excellent plan you set forth is deeply a good strategy.
translations.idiomatic: The edict said, "The fine plan you present is truly sound strategy.

sentences.zh: 如當機形可進，任將軍裁之。」

translations.literal: If the opportunity and situation allow advance, it is entrusted to the General to decide."
translations.idiomatic: If the moment and situation permit an advance, the General may decide."

sentences.zh: 既而蕭衍尋克建業，乃止。

translations.literal: Soon afterward Xiao Yan captured Jianye, and so the matter stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward Xiao Yan captured Jianye, and the plan was dropped.

sentences.zh: 除平北將軍、恒州刺史。

translations.literal: He was appointed General Who Pacifies the North and Inspector of Hengzhou.
