translations.idiomatic: Song was appointed General Who Pacifies the North and Inspector of Hengzhou.

sentences.zh: 轉平東將軍、徐州刺史。

translations.literal: He was transferred to General Who Pacifies the East and Inspector of Xuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to General Who Pacifies the East and Inspector of Xuzhou.

sentences.zh: 又轉安南將軍、揚州刺史。

translations.literal: He was again transferred to General Who Pacifies the South and Inspector of Yangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was later transferred again as General Who Pacifies the South and Inspector of Yangzhou.

sentences.zh: 蕭衍湘州刺史楊公則率眾二萬，屯軍洛口，姜慶真領卒五千，據於首陂，又遣其左軍將軍騫小眼，軍主何天祚、張俊興等率眾七千，攻圍陸城，嵩乃遣統軍封邁、王會等步騎八千討之。

translations.literal: Xiao Yan's Inspector of Xiangzhou Yang Gongze led twenty thousand men and stationed his army at Luokou; Jiang Qingzhen led five thousand soldiers and occupied Shoubei; and Yan also sent his Left Army General Qian Xiaoyan, army commanders He Tianzuo, Zhang Junxing, and others with seven thousand men to attack and surround Lucheng. Song then sent Commanders Feng Mai, Wang Hui, and others with eight thousand infantry and cavalry to attack them.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Gongze, Xiao Yan's Inspector of Xiangzhou, led twenty thousand men to Luokou; Jiang Qingzhen led five thousand to Shoubei; and Yan sent Left Army General Qian Xiaoyan, with army commanders He Tianzuo, Zhang Junxing, and others, leading seven thousand men to besiege Lucheng. Song sent Feng Mai, Wang Hui, and other commanders with eight thousand infantry and cavalry against them.

sentences.zh: 邁達陸城，賊皆夜遁，追擊破之，斬獲數千，公則、慶真退還馬頭。

translations.literal: When Mai reached Lucheng, the rebels all fled by night; he pursued and defeated them, beheading and capturing several thousand, and Gongze and Qingzhen retreated back to Matou.
translations.idiomatic: When Feng Mai reached Lucheng, the rebels fled by night. He pursued and defeated them, killing or capturing several thousand, while Gongze and Qingzhen retreated to Matou.

sentences.zh: 衍徐州刺史昌義之屯據高皇，遣三軍潛寇陰陵，以淮水淺竭，不通船艦，屯於馬頭。

translations.literal: Yan's Inspector of Xuzhou Chang Yizhi garrisoned and occupied Gaohuang, and sent three armies secretly to raid Yinling. Because the Huai water was shallow and exhausted and boats could not pass, he stationed at Matou.
translations.idiomatic: Chang Yizhi, Yan's Inspector of Xuzhou, held Gaohuang and sent three armies in a secret raid on Yinling. Since the Huai was too shallow for boats to pass, he stationed at Matou.

sentences.zh: 衍將田道龍、何景先等領卒三千已至衡山，規寇陸城。

translations.literal: Yan's generals Tian Daolong, He Jingxian, and others led three thousand soldiers and had already reached Hengshan, planning to raid Lucheng.
translations.idiomatic: Yan's generals Tian Daolong, He Jingxian, and others led three thousand soldiers to Hengshan, planning to raid Lucheng.

sentences.zh: 寇並充逼。

translations.literal: The raiders were all pressing in densely.
translations.idiomatic: The raiders pressed in from all sides.

sentences.zh: 嵩遣兼統軍李叔仁等援合肥、小峴、楊石，頻戰破之。

translations.literal: Song sent acting Commander Li Shuren and others to reinforce Hefei, Xiaoxian, and Yangshi, and in repeated battles they defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: Song sent acting Commander Li Shuren and others to reinforce Hefei, Xiaoxian, and Yangshi, repeatedly defeating the enemy in battle.

sentences.zh: 衍征虜將軍趙草屯於黃口，嵩遣軍司趙熾等往討之，先遣統軍安伯醜潛師夜渡，伏兵下蔡。

translations.literal: Yan's General Who Conquers Caitiffs Zhao Cao was stationed at Huangkou. Song sent Army Marshal Zhao Chi and others to attack him, first sending Commander An Bochou to lead a hidden force across by night and place ambush troops at Xiacai.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Cao, Yan's General Who Conquers Caitiffs, was stationed at Huangkou. Song sent Army Marshal Zhao Chi and others to attack, first dispatching Commander An Bochou to cross secretly by night and set an ambush at Xiacai.

sentences.zh: 草率卒四千，逆來拒戰，伯醜與下蔡戍主王虎等前後夾擊，大敗之，俘斬溺死四千餘人。

translations.literal: Cao led four thousand soldiers to come against them and resist in battle; Bochou and Wang Hu, commander of the Xiacai Garrison, attacked from front and rear and greatly defeated him, capturing, beheading, and drowning more than four thousand men.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Cao led four thousand men to meet them. An Bochou and Wang Hu, commander of Xiacai Garrison, struck from front and rear, badly defeated him, and captured, killed, or drowned more than four thousand men.

sentences.zh: 統軍李叔仁等夜襲硤石之賊，又破之。

translations.literal: Commander Li Shuren and others made a night attack on the rebels at Xiashi and again defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: Commander Li Shuren and others made a night attack on the rebels at Xiashi and defeated them as well.

sentences.zh: 衍將姜慶真專據肥汭，冠軍將軍曹天寶屯於鷄口，軍主尹明世屯東硤石。

translations.literal: Yan's general Jiang Qingzhen alone occupied Feirui, Champion General Cao Tianbao was stationed at Jikou, and army commander Yin Mingshi was stationed at Eastern Xiashi.
translations.idiomatic: Yan's general Jiang Qingzhen held Feirui, Champion General Cao Tianbao was stationed at Jikou, and army commander Yin Mingshi at Eastern Xiashi.

sentences.zh: 嵩遣別將羊引次于淮西，去賊營十里，司馬趙熾率兵一萬為表裏聲勢。

translations.literal: Song sent separate general Yang Yin to halt at Huaixi, ten li from the rebel camp, while Marshal Zhao Chi led ten thousand soldiers to form an inner and outer show of force.
translations.idiomatic: Song sent the separate general Yang Yin to camp at Huaixi, ten li from the rebel camp, while Marshal Zhao Chi led ten thousand troops to create pressure from inside and outside.

sentences.zh: 眾軍既會，分擊賊之四壘。

translations.literal: Once the various armies had assembled, they divided and attacked the rebels' four fortifications.
translations.idiomatic: When the armies had assembled, they split up and attacked the rebels' four forts.

sentences.zh: 四壘之賊，戰敗奔走，斬獲數千，溺死萬數。

translations.literal: The rebels in the four fortifications were defeated in battle and fled; several thousand were beheaded or captured, and those who drowned were counted by the ten thousand.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels in the four forts were defeated and fled; several thousand were killed or captured, and tens of thousands drowned.

sentences.zh: 統軍牛敬賓攻硤石，明世宵遁。

translations.literal: Commander Niu Jingbin attacked Xiashi, and Mingshi fled by night.
translations.idiomatic: Commander Niu Jingbin attacked Xiashi, and Yin Mingshi fled by night.

sentences.zh: 慶真合餘燼浮淮下，下蔡戍主王略截流擊之，俘斬太半。

translations.literal: Qingzhen gathered the remaining embers and floated down the Huai; Wang Lue, commander of the Xiacai Garrison, cut off the current and attacked him, capturing and beheading more than half.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang Qingzhen gathered the remnants and moved down the Huai; Wang Lue, commander of Xiacai Garrison, intercepted him on the river and captured or killed more than half.

sentences.zh: 於是威名大振。

translations.literal: Thereupon Song's awe-inspiring reputation greatly flourished.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter Song's reputation for military power greatly flourished.

sentences.zh: 後為蒼頭李太伯等同謀害嵩，并妻穆氏及子世賢。

translations.literal: Later the cangtou Li Taibo and others conspired together and murdered Song, along with his wife Lady Mu and his son Shixian.
translations.idiomatic: Later Li Taibo and other cangtou retainers conspired to murder Song, together with his wife Lady Mu and his son Shixian.

sentences.zh: 世宗為嵩舉哀於東堂，賻絹一千匹，贈車騎將軍、領軍，諡曰剛侯。

translations.literal: Shizong raised mourning for Song in the Eastern Hall, gave one thousand bolts of silk for funeral expenses, posthumously granted him General of Chariots and Cavalry and Commander of the Guards, and gave him the posthumous title Marquis Gang.
translations.idiomatic: Shizong held mourning for Song in the Eastern Hall, granted one thousand bolts of silk for the funeral, posthumously awarded him General of Chariots and Cavalry and Commander of the Guards, and gave him the posthumous title Marquis Gang.

sentences.zh: 第二子世儁，頗有幹用，而無行業。

translations.literal: His second son Shijun had considerable practical ability, but no moral conduct.
translations.idiomatic: His second son Shijun had some practical ability but no moral conduct.

sentences.zh: 襲爵，除給事中、東宮舍人。

translations.literal: He inherited the title and was appointed Supervising Attendant and Household Gentleman of the Eastern Palace.
translations.idiomatic: He inherited the title and was appointed Supervising Attendant and Household Gentleman of the Eastern Palace.

sentences.zh: 伯父澄表求轉階授之，於是除員外散騎常侍。

translations.literal: His uncle Cheng memorialized requesting that his rank be transferred and awarded to him, and thereupon he was appointed Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary Outside the Ranks.
translations.idiomatic: His uncle Cheng memorialized asking that a rank be transferred to him, and Shijun was appointed Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary Outside the Ranks.

sentences.zh: 肅宗時，追論嵩勳，封世儁衞縣開國男，食邑二百戶。

translations.literal: In Suzong's time, Song's merit was retrospectively discussed, and Shijun was enfeoffed as Founding Baron of Wei County, with a fief of two hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: In Suzong's reign, Song's merits were reviewed, and Shijun was enfeoffed as Founding Baron of Wei County with two hundred households.

sentences.zh: 遷冠軍將軍、宗正少卿，又為散騎常侍、安南將軍、武衞將軍、河南尹。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Champion General and Junior Chamberlain for the Imperial Clan, and later became Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary, General Who Pacifies the South, General of the Martial Guard, and Governor of Henan.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to Champion General and Junior Chamberlain for the Imperial Clan, then served as Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary, General Who Pacifies the South, General of the Martial Guard, and Governor of Henan.

sentences.zh: 尋除鎮東將軍、青州刺史，轉征東將軍，加散騎常侍。

translations.literal: Soon he was appointed General Who Guards the East and Inspector of Qingzhou, transferred to General Who Conquers the East, and additionally made Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was appointed General Who Guards the East and Inspector of Qingzhou, then transferred to General Who Conquers the East with the added title Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary.

sentences.zh: 邢杲之亂，圍逼州城，世儁憑城拒守，遂得保全。

translations.literal: During Xing Gao's rebellion, Gao surrounded and pressed the provincial city, and Shijun relied on the walls to resist and defend, so that it was preserved intact.
translations.idiomatic: During Xing Gao's rebellion, the provincial city was surrounded and pressed hard. Shijun held the walls and defended it, preserving the city intact.

sentences.zh: 孝莊時，除衞將軍、吏部尚書。

translations.literal: In Emperor Xiaozhuang's time, he was appointed General of the Guard and Minister of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: In Emperor Xiaozhuang's reign, he was appointed General of the Guard and Minister of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 爾朱兆寇京師，詔世儁以本官為都督，防守河橋。

translations.literal: When Erzhu Zhao raided the capital, an edict appointed Shijun, in his original office, as Commander-in-Chief to defend Heqiao.
translations.idiomatic: When Erzhu Zhao raided the capital, an edict kept Shijun in his current office and made him Commander-in-Chief for the defense of Heqiao.

sentences.zh: 及兆至河，世儁初無拒守意，便隔岸遙拜，時論疾之。

translations.literal: When Zhao reached the river, Shijun from the start had no intention of resisting and defending, and at once bowed from across the bank; opinion at the time detested him.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhao reached the river, Shijun had no intention of resisting. He immediately bowed from across the bank, and public opinion despised him.

sentences.zh: 前廢帝世，為驃騎將軍，仍加尚書，尤為爾朱世隆所昵。

translations.literal: In the reign of the Former Deposed Emperor, he was General of Agile Cavalry and was additionally made Minister of State Affairs; he was especially intimate with Erzhu Shilong.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Former Deposed Emperor, he was General of Agile Cavalry with the added title Minister of State Affairs, and he was especially close to Erzhu Shilong.

sentences.zh: 出帝初，加儀同三司，改封武陽縣開國子，食邑五百戶。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the reign of the Emperor Who Went Out, he was given Equal in Honor to the Three Excellencies, his enfeoffment was changed to Founding Viscount of Wuyang County, with a fief of five hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of the Emperor Who Went Out's reign, he was given Equal in Honor to the Three Excellencies and re-enfeoffed as Founding Viscount of Wuyang County with five hundred households.

sentences.zh: 世儁居選曹，不能厲心，多所受納，為中尉彈糾，坐免官。

translations.literal: When Shijun occupied the selections bureau, he could not discipline his mind and accepted many gifts; he was impeached by the Censor-in-Chief and dismissed from office for the offense.
translations.idiomatic: While Shijun served in the selections bureau, he failed to discipline himself and accepted many gifts. The Censor-in-Chief impeached him, and he was dismissed.

sentences.zh: 尋復本職。

translations.literal: Soon he was restored to his original office.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was restored to his former office.

sentences.zh: 孝靜初，加侍中、尚書右僕射，遷尚書令。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Emperor Xiaojing's reign, he was given the added title Palace Attendant and Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs, and was promoted to Director of the Department of State Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of Emperor Xiaojing's reign, he was made Palace Attendant and Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs, then promoted to Director of the Department.

sentences.zh: 世儁輕薄，好去就，詔送晉陽。

translations.literal: Shijun was frivolous and liked to shift his allegiances, so an edict sent him to Jinyang.
translations.idiomatic: Shijun was frivolous and fond of shifting allegiance, so an edict sent him to Jinyang.

sentences.zh: 興和中，薨。

translations.literal: In the Xinghe era, he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the Xinghe era.

sentences.zh: 贈侍中、都督冀定瀛殷四州諸軍事、驃騎大將軍、太傅、定州刺史，尚書令、開國公如故，諡曰躁戾。

translations.literal: He was posthumously granted Palace Attendant, Commander of all military affairs in Ji, Ding, Ying, and Yin provinces, Grand General of Agile Cavalry, Grand Tutor, and Inspector of Dingzhou; Director of the Department of State Affairs and Founding Duke remained as before; his posthumous title was Zaoli.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously granted Palace Attendant, Commander of all military affairs in Ji, Ding, Ying, and Yin provinces, Grand General of Agile Cavalry, Grand Tutor, and Inspector of Dingzhou, while retaining Director of the Department of State Affairs and Founding Duke as before. His posthumous title was Zaoli.

sentences.zh: 子景遠襲，散騎侍郎。

translations.literal: His son Jingyuan succeeded; he was Cavalier Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: His son Jingyuan succeeded and served as Cavalier Attendant.

sentences.zh: 世賢弟世哲，武定中，吏部郎。

translations.literal: Shixian's younger brother Shizhe, in the Wuding era, was Gentleman of the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: Shixian's younger brother Shizhe served in the Wuding era as Gentleman of the Ministry of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 嵩弟贍，字道周。

translations.literal: Song's younger brother Zhan was styled Daozhou.
translations.idiomatic: Song's younger brother Zhan was styled Daozhou.

sentences.zh: 高祖時，自□大夫稍遷宗正少卿、龍驤將軍、光州刺史、散騎常侍、左將軍，遷平東將軍、兗州刺史。

translations.literal: In Gaozu's time, from a Grandee title with one character missing he gradually rose to Junior Chamberlain for the Imperial Clan, Longxiang General, Inspector of Guangzhou, Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary, and General of the Left, and was promoted to General Who Pacifies the East and Inspector of Yanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In Gaozu's time, from a Grandee title with one missing character, he gradually rose to Junior Chamberlain for the Imperial Clan, Longxiang General, Inspector of Guangzhou, Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary, and General of the Left, then was promoted to General Who Pacifies the East and Inspector of Yanzhou.

sentences.zh: 頗愛書史，而貪暴好殺。

translations.literal: He rather loved books and histories, but was greedy, violent, and fond of killing.
translations.idiomatic: He had some love for books and histories, but was greedy, violent, and fond of killing.

sentences.zh: 澄深恥忿之，絕其往來。

translations.literal: Cheng was deeply ashamed and angered by him and cut off dealings with him.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng was deeply ashamed and angered by him and broke off all contact.

sentences.zh: 有四子。

translations.literal: He had four sons.
translations.idiomatic: He had four sons.

sentences.zh: 長子遠，尚書郎。

translations.literal: The eldest son, Yuan, was a Gentleman of the Department of State Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: The eldest son, Yuan, was a Gentleman of the Department of State Affairs.

sentences.zh: 史臣曰：顯祖之將禪讓，可謂國之大節。

translations.literal: The historian says: When Xianzu was about to abdicate, it may be called a great joint of the state.
translations.idiomatic: The historian says: When Xianzu was about to abdicate, it was a great test of the state.

sentences.zh: 康王毅然庭諍，德音孔昭，一言興邦，其斯之謂歟？

translations.literal: Prince Kang firmly remonstrated in court, and his virtuous words were very bright; one word raised the state. Is this not what is meant?
translations.idiomatic: Prince Kang remonstrated firmly in court, his virtuous words shining clearly; one word raised the state. Is this not the phrase made real?

sentences.zh: 文宣貞固俊遠，鬱為宗傑，身因累朝，寧濟夷險，既社稷是任，其梁棟之望也。

translations.literal: Wenxuan was upright, firm, outstanding, and far-reaching, richly becoming a hero of the imperial clan; in person he followed successive reigns, calmly crossing ease and danger, and since the altars of state were entrusted to him, he was the hope of beams and pillars.
translations.idiomatic: Wenxuan was upright, firm, outstanding, and far-seeing, a flourishing hero of the imperial clan. Serving through successive reigns, calm in ease and danger, he bore responsibility for the state and was the hope of its beams and pillars.

sentences.zh: 順謇諤俶儻，有汲黯之風，不用於時，橫招非命，惜矣。

translations.literal: Shun was blunt in remonstrance and free in spirit, with the manner of Ji An. Not used by his age, he unjustly met untimely death. A pity!
translations.idiomatic: Shun was blunt and free-spirited, with the air of Ji An. Unused by his time, he wrongly met an untimely death. A pity!

sentences.zh: 嵩有行陳之氣，儁則裂冠之徒歟？

translations.literal: Song had the spirit of the battle line, while Jun was the sort of man who tears the cap, was he not?
translations.idiomatic: Song had the spirit of the battle line; Jun was surely a cap-tearing sort of man, was he not?
